definition_zh: 寿命；使用寿命；存在期限；有效年限
definition_en: the length of time that a living thing, an object or a system lasts or is expected to last
core_image: 一支被刻上刻度的旧温度计，两端各有一道标记，中间拉出一条时间轴
scene: 博物馆的展柜里放着一支旧温度计，旁边的标签写着它从出厂到报废之间的年份跨度。 A simple label recorded the lifespan of the instrument from the day it was made to the day it failed.
sceneCN: 这里指器物从出厂到失效的使用寿命（第 4 个义项：产品与设备的使用期限）；句意为标签记下了这支仪器从制成到损坏的寿命。图中可辨识物件：展柜、旧温度计、刻度、纸质标签。

pos.zh: 名词：可数，指寿命或使用期限；常带表示所属的介词短语

derivatives.zh: 分写形式，与本词同义，多见于较早的文本
本词复数，指多个物种或多种产品的寿命
由 life 与 time 构成的近义复合词，义为「一生；终身」
由 life 与 long 构成，义为「终身的」
同一构词方式下的复合词，义为「翼展」
同一构词方式下的复合词，义为「时间跨度」

senses.title: Maximum lifespan of a species
senses.definition: the longest time that an individual of a species has been known to live under ideal conditions
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种的个体在理想条件下已知能存活的最长时间
senses.example: The maximum lifespan of the bristlecone pine is measured in thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 刺果松的寿命上限以千年计。
senses.why: Biologists separate the ceiling from the average because the oldest known individual marks the genetic limit of a species.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家把上限与平均值分开，因为已知最老的个体标记着该物种的遗传极限。

senses.title: Average or expected lifespan
senses.definition: the typical number of years members of a group actually live, usually given as a mean
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体成员实际存活的典型年数，通常以平均值表示
senses.example: Average lifespan in the region rose by nearly a decade after clean water arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁水源到位后，该地区的平均寿命提高了近十年。
senses.why: Public health needs a single summary number, and the mean of many lives provides it.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生需要一个概括性的数字，众多个体寿命的平均值正好提供它。

senses.title: An individual's lifetime
senses.definition: the whole period during which one person or animal is alive
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一只动物活着的整个时期
senses.example: Her lifespan covered two wars and the first moon landing.
senses.exampleCN: 她的一生横跨两次战争与首次登月。
senses.why: The compound can also be read one life at a time, as a span with a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词也可以一次只指一条生命，看作有起点与终点的一段时间。

senses.title: Product or device lifespan
senses.titleCN: 产品与设备的使用寿命
senses.definition: the period for which a manufactured object remains usable before failure or replacement
senses.definitionCN: 制成品在失效或更换之前保持可用的时期
senses.example: The pump has a lifespan of about eight years under normal load.
senses.exampleCN: 这台泵在正常负荷下的使用寿命约为八年。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the biological word because machines also wear out along a predictable curve.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用了生物学的词，因为机器也沿着可预测的曲线磨损。

senses.title: Battery and component lifespan
senses.definition: the number of charge cycles or operating hours a component delivers before its capacity falls below a threshold
senses.definitionCN: 部件在容量降到阈值之前所能提供的充电循环次数或工作小时数
senses.example: Cycle testing is used to estimate the lifespan of the new cells.
senses.exampleCN: 循环测试被用来估算新电芯的寿命。
senses.why: A component's life is counted in cycles rather than years, so the word gains a technical unit.
senses.whyCN: 部件的寿命以循环而非年计数，这个词因此获得了技术性的计量单位。

senses.title: Lifespan of a star
senses.definition: the time a star spends fusing hydrogen and then heavier elements before it ends as a remnant
senses.definitionCN: 恒星从开始聚变氢到最终成为残骸所经历的时间
senses.example: A massive star has a much shorter lifespan than a small one.
senses.exampleCN: 大质量恒星的寿命远短于小质量恒星。
senses.why: Astronomy applies the same span to objects that were never alive, because their evolution has a clear start and finish.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把同一跨度用到了从未有生命的天体上，因为它们的演化有明确的开始与结束。

senses.title: Lifespan of an institution or custom
senses.definition: the period during which an organisation, language or practice continues to exist
senses.definitionCN: 组织、语言或习俗持续存在的时期
senses.example: The guild had a lifespan of three centuries before it dissolved.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行会存在了三个世纪才解散。
senses.why: Social scientists extend the word to anything that is founded, maintained and finally ended.
senses.whyCN: 社会科学家把这个词扩展到任何被创立、维持并最终结束的事物。

senses.title: Lifespan of stored data
senses.titleCN: 数据与载体的保存寿命
senses.definition: the time for which a storage medium keeps its contents readable without error
senses.definitionCN: 存储介质在不出现错误的情况下保持内容可读的时间
senses.example: Archivists test the lifespan of optical discs before committing to them.
senses.exampleCN: 档案人员在使用光盘之前会测试其保存寿命。
senses.why: Digital preservation turned the word into a specification: how long before the bits decay.
senses.whyCN: 数字保存把这个词变成了一项指标：比特在多长时间后开始劣化。

senses.title: Working lifespan
senses.titleCN: 职业寿命与有效工作年限
senses.definition: the number of years a person can remain in a demanding job or profession
senses.definitionCN: 一个人能留在高强度岗位或专业领域工作的年数
senses.example: Better recovery routines have extended the working lifespan of many athletes.
senses.exampleCN: 更好的恢复安排延长了许多运动员的职业寿命。
senses.why: Careers also begin, peak and end, so the biological span is applied to employment.
senses.whyCN: 职业生涯同样有开始、顶峰与结束，于是生物学的跨度被用到就业上。

intro.en: The word is a plain English compound of life and span, whose second element first meant the distance from thumb to little finger. The source is clear; the date of the compound's first recorded use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是 life 与 span 组成的普通英语复合词，其中 span 最初指拇指到小指之间的一拃长度。来源清楚，复合词的确切首见年代为约数。

items.en: Spann named a unit of length, the stretch between an outstretched thumb and the little finger.
items.cn: 这个词原是一个长度单位，指张开拇指与小指之间的一拃。

items.en: From a hand's width the sense widened to any stretch or extent, and then to a stretch of time.
items.cn: 从一只手的宽度，词义扩展到任何伸展或范围，再扩展到一段时间。

items.en: Life has meant a living being's existence since the oldest English records.
items.cn: 自最早的英语文献起，这个词就指活物的存在。

items.en: Life and span joined to name the length of one life, first recorded in American usage in the mid-nineteenth century.
items.cn: 两者结合，用来指一条生命的长度，最早见于十九世纪中期的美国用法。

items.en: The compound then spread from creatures to machines, batteries, stars and institutions.
items.cn: 此后这个复合词从生物扩展到机器、电池、恒星与机构。

items.en: Reference works differ by decades on the earliest citation, so the first date is best given as approximate.
items.cn: 各类辞书对最早引例的年份相差数十年，因此首见年代只能给约数。

note.en: The first group shares the second element or the same compound pattern; the second group names other measures of duration.
note.cn: 第一组共享第二个构词成分或相同的复合方式；第二组表示其他「时长」概念。

entries.definitionCN: 从一侧翼尖到另一侧翼尖的距离。

entries.definitionCN: 两个时点之间的一段时间。

entries.definition: The whole period during which someone is alive.

entries.definition: The number of years a person is statistically expected to live.
entries.definitionCN: 按统计预期一个人能活的年数。

entries.definition: Long duration of life, especially an unusually long one.
entries.definitionCN: 长寿，尤指异常长的寿命。

entries.definition: The length of time during which something continues.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物持续的时长。

entries.definition: The period an object remains usable in service.

entries.definition: The time food or a product stays good before spoiling.

normalIntro.en: Normal associations run from the hand-span measure to a life, then to machines and stars; abstract ones treat the word as a bounded interval.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想从「一拃」的量度走到一条生命，再到机器与恒星；抽象联想把这个词看作一段有界的区间。

normal.en: Span first meant a hand's width, thumb to little finger.
normal.cn: 表示跨度的那个成分最初指一只手的宽度，从拇指到小指。

normal.en: Stretch the hand into a timeline and you get a life span.
normal.cn: 把手张开拉成一条时间轴，就得到了生命周期。

normal.en: A pump outlives its warranty but still has a lifespan.
normal.cn: 泵的保修期早过了，但它仍有使用寿命。

normal.en: A battery counts its life in cycles, not birthdays.
normal.cn: 电池的寿命以循环计，而不是以生日计。

normal.en: Stars are not alive, yet they too have a lifespan.
normal.cn: 恒星没有生命，却同样有寿命。

abstract.en: A lifespan is not a number but an interval with two edges.
abstract.cn: 寿命不是一个数字，而是一段有两条边的区间。

abstract.en: Anything founded can also be spent, which is why institutions borrow the word.
abstract.cn: 凡被创立者皆可耗尽，机构因此也借用这个词。

abstract.en: Knowing the span changes how you plan the middle of it.
abstract.cn: 知道跨度有多长，会改变你对中间那段日子的安排。

examples.en: The average lifespan of the species is about twelve years.
examples.cn: 该物种的平均寿命约为十二年。

examples.en: Regular maintenance can double the lifespan of the machine.
examples.cn: 定期维护能让这台机器的寿命翻倍。

examples.en: Researchers compared the lifespan of wild and captive animals.
examples.cn: 研究人员比较了野生与圈养动物的寿命。

dict_mnemonic.text: life（生命）+ span（跨度）——生命的跨度就是寿命

root: 由英语 life「生命」与 span「跨度」复合而成。span 源自古英语 spann，本指拇指到小指张开的一拃长度，后引申为任何延伸范围与时间跨度。复合词最早见于十九世纪中期的美国用法，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses extend one measure of duration from a species to a single life, then to pumps, batteries, stars, guilds and archives.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项把同一个「时长」量度从物种延伸到单个生命，再到泵、电池、恒星、行会与档案。

core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子贴着一条生命摆放，两端各有一道刻痕。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGICAL RANGE: the ceiling a species can reach and the average its members actually reach.
branches.cn: 生物学区间：物种能达到的上限与成员实际达到的平均值。

branches.en: THE SINGLE SPAN: one person's whole stretch of being alive.
branches.cn: 单条跨度：一个人活着的整段时光。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERED SPAN: a product's usable years and a component's counted cycles.
branches.cn: 工程跨度：产品的可用年数与部件的循环计数。

branches.en: THE NON-LIVING SPAN: a star's fusion years and a disc's readable years.
branches.cn: 非生命跨度：恒星的聚变年数与光盘的可读年数。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL SPAN: how long an institution lasts and how long a career lasts.
branches.cn: 社会跨度：机构能存续多久，职业能维持多久。

definition_zh: adj. 可疑的；靠不住的；半信半疑的；犹豫的
definition_en: probably not honest, safe or reliable; feeling doubt about something; of questionable value or quality
core_image: 一份合同里几处条款被荧光笔涂黄，签字的手停在半空；一个人歪着头看对方，一条眉毛挑起而嘴不动；货架上一罐标签褪色的果酱，盖子微微鼓起
scene: 合同里几处条款被荧光笔涂黄，签字的手停在半空，笔尖离纸面只差一厘米。 He was dubious about the clauses marked in yellow.
sceneCN: 这里 dubious 指「心存疑虑、不愿轻易接受」（第 2 个义项：半信半疑的）；句意是他对那些涂黄的条款半信半疑。图中可辨识物件：荧光笔涂黄的条款、停在半空的手、笔尖与纸面的一厘米间隙。

pos.zh: 可疑的；靠不住的；半信半疑的；犹豫的

senses.title: Not to be trusted
senses.definition: probably not honest, safe or reliable
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）很可能不诚实、不安全或不可靠的
senses.example: The firm made a dubious claim about its returns.
senses.exampleCN: 那家公司对收益提出了可疑的说法。
senses.why: A contract with clauses marked in yellow while the signing hand stops in mid air.
senses.whyCN: 一份合同里几处条款被涂黄，签字的手停在半空。

senses.title: Feeling doubt
senses.definition: feeling doubt about something and not ready to accept it
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）对某事心存疑虑、不愿轻易接受的
senses.example: He was dubious about the clauses marked in yellow.

senses.why: A head tilted to one side with one eyebrow raised and the mouth kept still.
senses.whyCN: 头歪向一侧，一条眉毛挑起，嘴却不动。

senses.title: Of doubtful quality
senses.definition: of questionable value, quality or usefulness

senses.example: The shop sold sweets of dubious freshness.
senses.exampleCN: 那家店卖的糖果新鲜度成问题。
senses.why: A jar on a shelf with a faded label and a lid that bulges a little.
senses.whyCN: 货架上一罐标签褪色的果酱，盖子微微鼓起。

intro.en: Dubious comes from Latin dubius, moving in two directions: a mind that can go either way has not settled, so the word first described the thing that causes doubt and later the person who feels it.
intro.cn: dubious 来自拉丁语 dubius「朝两个方向移动」：一颗能往两边走的心还没有定下来，所以这个词先指引起怀疑的事物，后来也指心存疑虑的人。

items.en: Latin duo means two.
items.cn: 拉丁语 duo 意为二。

items.en: Latin dubius means moving in two directions, hence uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dubius 意为朝两个方向移动，因而指不确定。

items.en: Latin dubitare means to doubt or to hesitate.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dubitare 意为怀疑或犹豫。

items.en: English dubious is borrowed for something that causes doubt.
items.cn: 英语 dubious 被借入，指引起怀疑的事物。

items.en: The word is also used of a person who feels doubt.
items.cn: 这个词也用于指心存疑虑的人。

items.en: Dubious now covers unsafe claims, hesitant people and goods of doubtful quality.
items.cn: dubious 如今涵盖不可靠的说法、犹豫的人与质量成问题的货物。

note.en: Dubious shares its ending with obvious and previous, while its neighbours name other shades of not being sure.
note.cn: dubious 与 obvious、previous 共用词尾，而它的近义词则指「拿不准」的其他层次。

dict_mnemonic.text: dubious ＝ 拉丁语 dubius（朝两个方向移动）＋ -ous（形容词后缀）。心往两边走，就是「拿不定」：说事物是「可疑的」（a dubious claim），说人是「半信半疑的」（be dubious about），说质量是「靠不住的」（of dubious value）。同源的 doubt、dubitable 都带着这个「二」；反义词 obvious 是「摆在眼前、无需怀疑」。

root: 拉丁语 duo（二）→ dubius（朝两个方向、不确定）→ dubitare（怀疑）→ 英语 dubious（可疑的；半信半疑的）

intro.en: Dubious is Latin dubi- plus -ous; -ly and -ness build dubiously and dubiousness, while duo- keeps the two and cert- names the settled opposite.
intro.cn: dubious 由拉丁语 dubi- 加 -ous 组成；-ly 与 -ness 造出 dubiously 与 dubiousness，而 duo- 保留那个「二」，cert- 指称确定下来的反面。

latinIntro.en: Latin dubius means uncertain, dubitare to doubt, duo two and certus settled or sure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dubius 意为不确定，dubitare 意为怀疑，duo 意为二，certus 意为确定的。

definition_zh: 隐私；不受他人打扰的状态，以及对个人信息的控制权
definition_en: the state of being free from public attention or disturbance, and the control a person has over personal information
core_image: 一间只亮着一盏灯的屋子，窗帘拉严，门外的人只能看见布上的影子，却进不来
scene: 深夜的屋子里只亮着一盏台灯，窗帘拉得很严，门外的人只能看见布上的影子。 She drew the curtain because privacy mattered more to her than the view.
sceneCN: 这里 privacy 指不受他人注视与打扰的状态（第 1 个义项：独处不受扰）；句意：她拉上窗帘，因为对她来说，不被打扰比窗外的景色更重要。

pos.zh: 隐私；私生活；独处不受扰；信息控制权

senses.title: Freedom from being disturbed
senses.definition: the condition of being alone and free from other people's interruption
senses.definitionCN: 独处且不被他人打断的状态
senses.example: He reads in the garden for an hour of privacy each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上在花园里读一小时书，享受不被打扰的时光。
senses.why: the Latin adjective described something withdrawn from public life, and withdrawal begins as simple freedom from company.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词指从公共生活中退开，而退开最初就是免于他人陪伴。

senses.title: Freedom from public attention
senses.definition: the state of not being watched, reported on or discussed by the public
senses.definitionCN: 不被公众注视、报道或议论的状态
senses.example: The family moved inland to raise the children in privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人搬到内陆，想在不受注视的环境里抚养孩子。
senses.why: publicity is the opposite pole, and the word names the absence of it rather than the presence of walls.
senses.whyCN: 「公开」是对立的一端，这个词指公开的缺席，而不是墙的存在。

senses.title: Control over one's own information
senses.definition: a person's power to decide who learns what about them
senses.definitionCN: 个人决定谁能知道自己哪些情况的权力
senses.example: Privacy means the choice to tell, not the duty to hide.
senses.exampleCN: 隐私意味着「可以选择说」，而不是「必须藏」。
senses.why: once information could be copied and shared at scale, withdrawal became a matter of control rather than of distance.
senses.whyCN: 当信息能被大规模复制与共享，退开就从「隔开距离」变成了「掌握控制权」。

senses.title: Data privacy as a field of practice
senses.titleCN: 数据隐私这一实务领域
senses.definition: the handling of personal data by organisations under rules of collection, use and deletion
senses.definitionCN: 机构按收集、使用与删除规则处理个人数据
senses.example: The company hired a lawyer to lead its data privacy work.
senses.exampleCN: 公司聘请了一位律师主管数据隐私工作。
senses.why: a social value is turned into a managed operation, and its name follows the operation.
senses.whyCN: 一项社会价值被转化为可管理的业务，其名称便随业务走。

senses.title: The legal right to seclusion
senses.definition: the recognised claim that others may not intrude into one's personal sphere
senses.definitionCN: 被承认的、他人不得侵入个人领域的主张
senses.example: The court treated privacy as a limit on how evidence may be gathered.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把隐私视为取证方式的一条界限。
senses.why: a value argued in courts becomes a right, and the abstract noun carries that legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上被论证的价值会变成一项权利，这个抽象名词便承担了法律分量。

senses.title: Settings that limit visibility
senses.definition: the options in an app or account that decide who can see what
senses.definitionCN: 应用或账号中决定谁能看到什么的选择项
senses.example: She changed her privacy so that only friends could see the album.
senses.exampleCN: 她改动了隐私设置，只有好友能看到那本相册。
senses.why: when exposure is governed by menus, the value word is used for the switches themselves.
senses.whyCN: 当曝光由菜单控制时，这个价值名词就被用来指那些开关。

senses.title: Confidentiality of a matter
senses.definition: the quality of a discussion or document that stays within a trusted circle
senses.definitionCN: 谈话或文件只留在可信圈子内的性质
senses.example: They asked for privacy during the settlement talks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们要求和解谈判过程保持保密。
senses.why: a thing kept from outsiders is private in the old sense, and the abstract noun covers that condition.
senses.whyCN: 不让外人知道的事在旧义上就是「私下的」，抽象名词涵盖这种状态。

senses.title: Physical seclusion of a place
senses.definition: the shielding of a room or home from view, sound or entry
senses.definitionCN: 房间或住宅在视线、声音与进入上受到的遮蔽
senses.example: The hedge gives the terrace a little privacy from the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那道树篱让露台与马路之间有了一点遮蔽。
senses.why: walls, hedges and curtains are the oldest tools of withdrawal, so the word attaches to physical shelter.
senses.whyCN: 墙、树篱与窗帘是「退开」最古老的工具，因此这个词也依附于实体的遮蔽。

senses.title: Protection against surveillance
senses.definition: the expectation that states and companies will not track a person without cause
senses.definitionCN: 国家对个人的追踪需有正当理由这一期待
senses.example: Cameras on every corner turned privacy into a public argument.
senses.exampleCN: 街角的摄像头把隐私变成了公共议题。
senses.why: the word sharpens when watching becomes cheap, because the old freedom now needs defending.
senses.whyCN: 当「观看」变得廉价，这个词就变得尖锐，因为旧的自由如今需要辩护。

senses.title: Personal space in shared settings
senses.titleCN: 共享场所中的个人空间
senses.definition: the informal room a person keeps around themselves among others
senses.definitionCN: 在他人之间为自己留出的非正式余地
senses.example: Open desks leave almost no privacy for a phone call.
senses.exampleCN: 开放式工位几乎不给人打电话的私人余地。
senses.why: the word stretches from legal seclusion to the small distance people maintain in a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律的清静延伸到人群中人们维持的那点距离。

intro.en: Privacy comes from Latin privatus, withdrawn from public office and belonging to oneself. The abstract ending -acy names a state, so the word names a condition rather than a thing.
intro.cn: privacy 来自拉丁语 privatus，指「退出公职、属于个人」。抽象词尾 -acy 表示状态，因此这个词指一种处境，而不是一件东西。

items.en: Latin privus meant single, each for itself, and the derived verb privare meant to set apart or deprive.
items.cn: 拉丁语 privus 意为「单个的、各自的」，派生动词 privare 意为「分开、剥夺」。

items.en: Privatus described a person withdrawn from public office, a private citizen as opposed to a magistrate.
items.cn: privatus 描述退出公职的人，即与官员相对的普通公民。

items.en: French privé carried the sense of personal or secluded, and English borrowed the adjective as private.
items.cn: 法语 privé 带有「个人的、僻静的」之意，英语借入形容词 private。

items.en: The ending -acy, from Latin -acia, turns an adjective into the name of a state, so privacy is the state of being private.
items.cn: 词尾 -acy 来自拉丁 -acia，把形容词变成状态之名，因此 privacy 就是「处于私人状态」。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word moved from seclusion to information, as records became easy to copy and share.
items.cn: 二十世纪，随着记录变得易于复制与共享，这个词从「清静」转向「信息」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the link between privus and the wider family of Latin separating words is debated, and the deeper forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：privus 与拉丁语中其他表示「分开」的词是否同源仍有争论，更古的形式属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is built on the same private root; the second group is the neighbouring ideas of secrecy, solitude and protection.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「私人」词根上；第二组是保密、独处与保护这些相邻概念。

entries.definition: Belonging to a person rather than the public; a private room is the place where privacy is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 属于个人而非公众；private 的房间就是能有 privacy 的地方。

entries.definition: In a way that avoids public view; it describes how something is done, not the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以避开公众视线的方式；它描述做事方式，而不是状态本身。

entries.definition: To take something away from someone; it comes from the same Latin verb of setting apart but means loss, not seclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从某人处拿走；出自同一个表示「分开」的拉丁动词，但指失去，不是清静。

entries.definition: A special right granted to a person or group; the root idea of a private law applied to one party survives here.
entries.definitionCN: 授予个人或群体的特殊权利；这里保留的是「针对一方的私人法规」这一词根含义。

entries.definition: The keeping of information from others; privacy protects a person's sphere, secrecy hides a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息瞒住；privacy 保护个人领域，secrecy 隐藏某个事实。

entries.definition: The state of being alone, often chosen for calm; privacy can be enjoyed in company by being left undisturbed.
entries.definitionCN: 独处的状态，常为求安宁而选择；privacy 也可以在人群中通过不被打扰而获得。

entries.definition: The obligation not to pass on information given in trust; it is a duty, while privacy is a condition or right.
entries.definitionCN: 不转述受托信息的义务；它是义务，而 privacy 是状态或权利。

entries.definition: The state of not being identified; privacy may keep a known person unobserved, anonymity removes the name itself.
entries.definitionCN: 不被识别的状态；privacy 可让已知的人不被注视，anonymity 则连名字都去掉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Latin root and the real legal and technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实拉丁词根与真实的法律、技术搭配。

normal.en: The adjective is private and the state is privacy: the ending -acy names a condition.
normal.cn: 形容词是 private，状态名词是 privacy：词尾 -acy 表示状态。

normal.en: The old sense is a private citizen withdrawn from office, not a secret kept from a friend.
normal.cn: 旧义是退出公职的普通公民，而不是对朋友隐瞒的秘密。

normal.en: Fixed phrases run from law to software: right to privacy, privacy policy, privacy settings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配从法律延伸到软件：隐私权、隐私政策、隐私设置。

normal.en: The verb is invade or protect: privacy is something done to, not something done.
normal.cn: 动词是 invade 或 protect：privacy 是被对待的对象，而不是动作。

normal.en: Data privacy is the modern centre of gravity of the word.
normal.cn: 数据隐私是这个词现代的重心所在。

abstract.en: Picture a lit room whose curtain lets light out but keeps eyes out.
abstract.cn: 想象一间亮灯的屋子，窗帘把光放出去，却把目光挡在外面。

abstract.en: Picture a door with no handle on the outside and no lock on the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，外面没有把手，里面没有锁。

abstract.en: Picture a name written in water and read only by the person who wrote it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写在水上的名字，只有写下它的人读得到。

examples.en: Privacy is not secrecy; it is the power to decide what is shared.
examples.cn: 隐私不是保密，而是决定分享什么的权力。

examples.en: The new rules give patients more privacy over their records.
examples.cn: 新规让患者对自己的病历拥有更多隐私掌控。

examples.en: A thin wall gave the neighbours almost no privacy.
examples.cn: 一堵薄墙几乎没给邻居留下任何私人空间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来（pri）为谁（vacy）」——扑过来想知道「为谁」，正是要守住隐私

root: 拉丁 privus「单个的、各自的」→ privare「分开、剥夺」→ privatus「退出公职的私人」→ 法语 privé → 英语 private；加 -acy（拉丁 -acia）表状态构成 privacy。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses start from being left alone, pass through public attention, information control, professional handling, legal right, app settings, confidentiality and physical shelter, and end at surveillance and shared space.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从「不被打扰」出发，经过公众注视、信息控制、行业实务、法律权利、应用设置、保密与实体遮蔽，最后落在监控与共享空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room sealed by a curtain, visible as a glow from outside but not open to eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮灯的屋子被窗帘封住，外面只看见光，却看不进去。

branches.en: QUIET AND SHELTER: being undisturbed, and the walls or hedges that make it possible.
branches.cn: 清静与遮蔽：不被打扰，以及使之成为可能的墙与树篱。

branches.en: PUBLICITY AND WATCHING: the absence of public notice, and the defence of that absence against surveillance.
branches.cn: 公开与注视：不受公众关注，以及针对监控为这种缺席辩护。

branches.en: INFORMATION CONTROL: deciding who may know what about oneself.
branches.cn: 信息控制：决定谁能知道自己哪些情况。

branches.en: ROUTINE AND SETTINGS: organisational data handling, and the switches that govern visibility.
branches.cn: 实务与设置：机构的数据处理，以及控制可见性的开关。

branches.en: RIGHT, CONFIDENCE, SPACE: a legal claim, a confidential circle, and the small room kept in a crowd.
branches.cn: 权利、信任与空间：法律主张、可信圈子，以及在人群中留出的余地。

intro.en: Privacy is a Latin adjective turned into a state noun by the ending -acy; English later built private and privately from the same base.
intro.cn: privacy 是拉丁形容词加 -acy 构成的状态名词；英语后来又从同一词基造出 private 与 privately。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is privus, single or separate, with privatus as its adjective of withdrawal; -acia supplied the abstract ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 privus「单个的、分开的」，其形容词 privatus 表示退出；抽象词尾来自 -acia。

items.example: The adjective begins the idea of what belongs to one person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词开启了「属于一个人」的观念。

items.example: The verb supplies both the sense of separation and of loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时提供「分开」与「失去」两层含义。

items.example: The adjective describes a private citizen rather than a magistrate.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述普通公民而非官员。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective into the name of a condition.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成状态之名。

items.example: Private is the adjective behind the state noun.
items.exampleCN: private 是状态名词背后的形容词。

items.example: The adverb describes the manner of doing something.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词描述做某事的方式。

items.example: The prefixed verb names loss rather than seclusion.
items.exampleCN: 带前缀的动词指失去，而不是清静。

items.example: The same base appears in a word for a special right.
items.exampleCN: 同一词基也出现在表示特殊权利的词中。

items.example: The second element ties the word to a private law.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件把这个词与「私人法规」联系起来。

definition_en: an animal that eats both plant and animal food, or a person with broadly varied tastes and interests

senses.title: Eating both plants and animals
senses.titleCN: 杂食动物：植物与动物通吃
senses.definition: an animal whose diet includes substantial amounts of both plant and animal material
senses.definitionCN: 指食物中植物与动物材料都占相当比重的动物
senses.example: The raccoon is an omnivore that takes fruit, insects and carrion.
senses.exampleCN: 浣熊是杂食动物，吃果实、昆虫与腐肉。
senses.why: The word fills the plus-plus dietary cell, defined by neither plant nor flesh alone but by both.
senses.whyCN: 这个词填补食性表格中「两者都吃」的格子，既不只靠植物也不只靠肉，而是两者兼有。

senses.title: The human omnivore
senses.titleCN: 人类杂食者：生理上适应混合饮食
senses.definition: a human considered as a species adapted to a mixed diet of plants and animal products
senses.definitionCN: 指从物种层面被看作适应植物与动物性混合饮食的人类
senses.example: As an omnivore, the human gut can use both grains and meat.
senses.exampleCN: 作为杂食者，人的肠道既能利用谷物也能利用肉类。
senses.why: The label is used in nutrition and anthropology to describe a species-level capacity, not an individual choice.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签在营养学与人类学中描述物种层面的能力，而非个人选择。

senses.title: Opportunistic omnivore
senses.titleCN: 机会主义杂食者：随资源变化切换
senses.definition: an omnivore whose diet shifts with whatever is available, rather than following a fixed preference
senses.definitionCN: 指食性随可得资源变化、而非遵循固定偏好的杂食动物
senses.example: The fox is an opportunistic omnivore that follows the fruit season.
senses.exampleCN: 狐狸是机会主义杂食者，跟着果实季节改变食物。
senses.why: Flexibility is the point: the same animal can live through seasons when one food source fails.
senses.whyCN: 灵活性是关键：当一种食物来源失败时，同一种动物仍能熬过季节。

senses.title: Member of a feeding guild
senses.titleCN: 取食集团成员：生态学分类单位
senses.definition: in community ecology, an omnivore as a member of a guild that feeds at several trophic levels
senses.definitionCN: 群落生态学中指作为在多个营养级取食的集团成员的杂食动物
senses.example: Omnivores link the plant and animal channels of the food web.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食动物连接食物网中的植物通道与动物通道。
senses.why: Omnivores complicate the tidy trophic pyramid, because one species occupies several levels at once.
senses.whyCN: 杂食动物让整齐的营养金字塔变复杂，因为一个物种同时占据多个层级。

senses.title: Gut generalist
senses.titleCN: 消化道泛化：酶与菌群兼顾两类食物
senses.definition: an omnivore defined by a digestive system able to handle both plant fibre and animal protein
senses.definitionCN: 指消化道能够同时处理植物纤维与动物蛋白的杂食动物
senses.example: The omnivore's midgut carries enzymes for starch as well as for protein.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食者的中肠既带淀粉酶也带蛋白酶。
senses.why: The class is physiological as well as behavioural: the gut must be a compromise between two diets.
senses.whyCN: 这一类既是行为类别也是生理类别：消化道必须是两种食性的折中。

senses.title: Cultural omnivore
senses.titleCN: 文化杂食者：品味跨越雅俗
senses.definition: in sociology, a person who consumes both highbrow and popular culture rather than sticking to one tier
senses.definitionCN: 社会学中指既消费高雅文化也消费通俗文化、不固守单一层级的人
senses.example: The survey found that cultural omnivores attended both opera and football.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现文化杂食者既看歌剧也看足球。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the dietary word because taste is treated as a menu with many courses.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用饮食词汇，因为品味被当作有许多菜目的菜单。

senses.title: Digital omnivore
senses.titleCN: 数字杂食者：跨设备跨平台使用内容
senses.definition: in media research, a user who consumes content across several devices and platforms rather than one channel
senses.definitionCN: 媒介研究中指跨多种设备与平台、而非只用单一渠道消费内容的用户
senses.example: Digital omnivores move between phone, laptop and television in one evening.
senses.exampleCN: 数字杂食者一个晚上就在手机、笔记本与电视之间切换。
senses.why: Media studies extends the diet metaphor to attention, where the menu is platforms rather than plants and meat.
senses.whyCN: 媒介研究把饮食比喻扩展到注意力，菜单从植物与肉变成平台。

senses.title: A broadly curious person
senses.titleCN: 兴趣广泛者：什么都想读一点
senses.definition: an informal use for a person who reads, studies or tries many unrelated things
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，指阅读、研究或尝试许多不相关事物的人
senses.example: He is an omnivore of ideas, equally at home in physics and poetry.
senses.exampleCN: 他是观念上的杂食者，在物理与诗歌中都自在。
senses.why: The dietary metaphor softens specialisation into appetite, which is why it is used approvingly.
senses.whyCN: 饮食比喻把专业化软化为胃口，因此这个说法常带赞许。

intro.en: Omnivore combines Latin omnis 'all' with vorare 'to devour'. The adjective omnivorous is older; the noun is generally treated as a later back-formation.
intro.cn: omnivore 由拉丁语 omnis「全部」与 vorare「吞食」构成。形容词 omnivorous 出现更早，名词一般认为是由它逆构而来。

items.en: Omnis meant all or every, and it also gives omnibus, omnipotent and omniscient.
items.cn: omnis 意为全部、每个，也是 omnibus、omnipotent、omniscient 的来源。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour, the same verb that closes herbivore and carnivore.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食，与 herbivore、carnivore 结尾的动词相同。

items.en: Omnivorus was formed in scientific Latin as the adjective for a mixed diet. Its exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: omnivorus 在科学拉丁语中构成，作为混合食性的形容词；确切首用存疑。

items.en: English omnivorous is recorded in the seventeenth century. The exact first citation is uncertain, and the early uses may have been figurative.
items.cn: 英语 omnivorous 见于 17 世纪；确切首见书证存疑，早期用法可能已是比喻。

items.en: Omnivore as a noun is generally dated to the nineteenth century and treated as a back-formation from omnivorous, though the dating is not fixed.
items.cn: 名词 omnivore 一般认为出现在 19 世纪，被视为由 omnivorous 逆构而来，但年代并不确定。

items.en: Twentieth-century sociology and media studies formed cultural omnivore and digital omnivore, extending 'all' to tastes and platforms.
items.cn: 20 世纪的社会学与媒介研究造出文化杂食者与数字杂食者，把「全部」扩展到品味与平台。

note.en: The look-alike group is the three diet classes; the near-meaning group separates the broad eater from the flexible strategist.
note.cn: 形近组是三个食性类别；近义组区分广泛取食者与灵活策略者。

entries.definition: An animal that eats plants. It is the plant-only class, and the first element herba- marks the difference.
entries.definitionCN: 指以植物为食的动物。它是纯植食类别，前半 herba- 标出差别。

entries.definition: An animal that eats flesh. It is the flesh-only class, and omni- 'all' is what separates it from omnivore.
entries.definitionCN: 指以肉为食的动物。它是纯肉食类别，正是 omni-「全部」把它与杂食动物区分开。

entries.definition: The adjective form meaning mixed-diet. Omnivore is the noun, so a bear is an omnivore and has an omnivorous diet.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，意为混合食性的。omnivore 是名词，因此熊是 omnivore，饮食是 omnivorous。

entries.definition: A species that uses many resources. It overlaps with omnivore but is broader, since a generalist may use many habitats without eating both plants and meat.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用多种资源的物种。它与杂食动物重叠但更宽，因为广适种可能利用多种生境却不吃植物与肉。

entries.definition: One that takes whatever chance offers. It describes behaviour, while omnivore describes diet.
entries.definitionCN: 指抓住任何机会者。它描述行为，而 omnivore 描述食性。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for feeding on many kinds of food, common in entomology. It is close to omnivorous but usually applied to invertebrates.
entries.definitionCN: 技术形容词，指取食多种食物，常见于昆虫学。它接近 omnivorous，但多用于无脊椎动物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: omni 'all' + vore 'eater': the eater of everything.
normal.cn: omni「全部」+ vore「吃……者」：什么都吃者。

normal.en: The family runs omnivorous, omnivory, omnibus, omnipotent and omniscient.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 omnivorous、omnivory、omnibus、omnipotent、omniscient。

normal.en: Typical phrases: opportunistic omnivore, omnivore diet, cultural omnivore, digital omnivore.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：机会主义杂食者、杂食食谱、文化杂食者、数字杂食者。

normal.en: The three classes share -vore; only the first element changes: herbi-, carni-, omni-.
normal.cn: 三个类别共享 -vore，只有前半变化：herbi-、carni-、omni-。

normal.en: The noun is generally a back-formation from the older adjective omnivorous.
normal.cn: 名词一般被视为由更早的形容词 omnivorous 逆构而来。

abstract.en: Picture a bear pulling berries with one paw and breaking into an anthill with the other.
abstract.cn: 想象熊一只爪摘浆果，另一只爪扒开蚁巢。

abstract.en: Picture a reader with opera tickets and a football scarf in the same bag.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者的包里同时装着歌剧票与球迷围巾。

abstract.en: Picture one person switching between phone, laptop and television before dinner ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在晚饭结束前就在手机、笔记本与电视之间切换。

examples.en: The raccoon is an omnivore that thrives beside human settlements.
examples.cn: 浣熊是杂食动物，在人类聚居地旁也能繁盛。

examples.en: As omnivores, humans can digest both starch and meat.
examples.cn: 作为杂食者，人类既能消化淀粉也能消化肉类。

examples.en: The survey described her as a cultural omnivore with wide tastes.
examples.cn: 调查把她描述为品味广泛的文化杂食者。

dict_mnemonic.text: omni（全部）+ vore（吃……者）→ 什么都吃 → omnivore 杂食动物

root: 拉丁 omnis「全部」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 omnivorus；名词 omnivore 一般认为由形容词 omnivorous 逆构而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with the mixed diet and extend 'all' to human physiology, opportunity, trophic levels, taste and platforms.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从混合食性出发，把「全部」扩展到人类生理、机会、营养级、品味与平台。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bear taking berries and ants with different paws.
core.cn: 核心意象：熊用两只不同的爪子取浆果与蚂蚁。

branches.en: DIET: the base sense is both plant and animal food.
branches.cn: 食性：基本义是植物与动物性食物兼有。

branches.en: PHYSIOLOGY: the human species and its gut are described as mixed-diet generalists.
branches.cn: 生理：人类物种及其肠道被描述为混合食性的泛化者。

branches.en: ECOLOGY: flexibility lets the animal follow seasons and link trophic levels.
branches.cn: 生态：灵活性让动物随季节变化，并连接不同营养级。

branches.en: MEDIA AND CURIOSITY: platforms and reading habits become menus with many courses.
branches.cn: 媒介与好奇心：平台使用与阅读习惯也成了多道菜的菜单。

branches.en: CULTURAL WIDENING: 'all' extends from food to a taste that crosses every level.
branches.cn: 文化扩展：「全部」从食物延伸到跨越各层级的口味。

intro.en: Omnivore is the 'all' branch of the -vore family, and the prefix omni- is productive far beyond diet.
intro.cn: omnivore 是 -vore 词族中的「全部」支，前缀 omni- 的能产性远超饮食领域。

latinIntro.en: Omnis is a Latin adjective meaning all; vorare is the eating verb; the noun ending was added in scientific Latin and later in English.
latinIntro.cn: omnis 是意为「全部」的拉丁形容词，vorare 是吃的动词，名词词尾先在科学拉丁语、后在英语中加上。

items.meaning: an animal eating both plants and flesh
items.meaningCN: 既吃植物也吃肉的动物
items.example: Every omnivore has a favourite food.
items.exampleCN: 每种杂食动物都有偏爱的食物。

items.example: The omnivorous reader takes any genre.
items.exampleCN: 这位杂食读者任何体裁都读。

items.meaning: the practice of eating both diets
items.example: Omnivory blurs the trophic pyramid.
items.exampleCN: 杂食性模糊了营养金字塔。

items.example: Omni- appears in omnibus and omnipotent.
items.exampleCN: omni- 出现在 omnibus 与 omnipotent 中。

items.meaning: for all; a collected volume; a bus
items.meaningCN: 为所有人的；汇编本；公共汽车
items.example: The publisher issued an omnibus of the trilogy.
items.exampleCN: 出版社推出了三部曲的合集。

items.example: Herbivores and omnivores share the meadow.
items.exampleCN: 植食动物与杂食动物共用这片草甸。

items.example: The carnivore takes only meat.
items.exampleCN: 这只食肉动物只吃肉。

items.meaning: a species or person using many resources
items.meaningCN: 利用多种资源的物种或人
items.example: The omnivore is a dietary generalist.
items.exampleCN: 杂食动物是食性上的泛化者。

items.example: Polyphagous insects damage many crops.
items.exampleCN: 多食性昆虫危害多种作物。

latinEntries.structure: vorare, voro, voravi, voratum (v., first conjugation)

definition_zh: 比较分析；对比研究；跨案例的比较方法；（法律、政策、文学等领域的）比较分析
definition_en: a method of study that sets two or more cases side by side and explains their similarities and differences
core_image: 两张摊开的表格并排放在桌上，同一栏的数据被红笔一对一对连起来
scene: 研究团队把六个城市的垃圾分类政策列成同一张表，逐项对照回收率与罚款额度。 Their comparative analysis of six cities showed that deposit schemes worked better than fines.
sceneCN: 这里指把多个案例并置、逐项对照的研究方法（第 1 个义项：跨案例的比较分析）；句意为他们对六座城市的比较分析显示押金制比罚款更有效。场景图取象：两张表格并排，同一栏的数据被红线两两相连。

pos.zh: 比较分析；对比研究（方法）
（法律）比较法上的分析
（政策、文学、历史等领域的）跨案例比较分析

derivatives.zh: 比较（由「一起」＋「使齐备」的拉丁构件合成，指把两物摆到一处量）
比较；对照（比较动词的名词形式，指动作或结论）
比较的；比较研究的（加表示「倾向于、用于」的形容词后缀）
分析（由希腊语「向上、彻底」的前缀加「松开」的动词构成，字面即把整体拆开看）
分析；解析（上述动词的名词形式，指拆解后看清结构）
分析者；分析师（加表示「人」的名词后缀）

senses.title: A cross-case method
senses.definition: a research method that examines several cases together in order to explain why they differ
senses.definitionCN: 把若干案例放在一起考察、以解释其差异的研究方法
senses.example: A comparative analysis of six cities showed that deposit schemes worked better than fines.
senses.exampleCN: 对六座城市的比较分析显示押金制比罚款更有效。
senses.why: One case can only describe; a second case gives the first something to be measured against.
senses.whyCN: 单一案例只能描述，第二个案例才给第一个提供可比的参照。

senses.title: Policy comparison
senses.definition: the systematic contrast of policies or institutions across jurisdictions
senses.definitionCN: 跨辖区对政策或制度所作的系统对照
senses.example: Their comparative analysis of welfare systems covered nine countries.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对福利制度的比较分析覆盖九个国家。
senses.why: Governments borrow from each other, and a structured comparison is how they decide what can travel.
senses.whyCN: 政府彼此借鉴，而结构化的比较正是判断哪些做法可以移植的办法。

senses.title: Comparative legal analysis
senses.definition: the study of how different legal systems treat the same question
senses.definitionCN: 研究不同法律体系如何处理同一问题的学问
senses.example: The article offers a comparative analysis of liability rules in three codes.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章对三部法典中的责任规则作了比较分析。
senses.why: Lawyers compare codes to see whether a rule is universal or merely local.
senses.whyCN: 法律人比较法典，是要看一条规则是普遍的，还是只是本地的。

senses.title: Comparative literature
senses.definition: the study of works from different languages or traditions in relation to each other
senses.definitionCN: 把不同语言或传统的作品放在一起考察的研究
senses.example: Her comparative analysis of two epics changed the reading of both.
senses.exampleCN: 她对两部史诗的比较分析改变了对两者的解读。
senses.why: A work seen beside a foreign cousin reveals conventions that a single tradition hides.
senses.whyCN: 作品旁边站着一个异国亲戚，才会露出单一传统所遮蔽的成规。

senses.title: Statistical group comparison
senses.definition: the formal contrast of two or more groups or conditions using quantitative data
senses.definitionCN: 用定量数据对两个或多个组别或条件所作的正式对照
senses.example: A comparative analysis of the two cohorts found no difference in survival.
senses.exampleCN: 对两个队列的比较分析未发现存活率差异。
senses.why: Numbers make comparison precise, and precision is what turns an impression into a finding.
senses.whyCN: 数字让比较变得精确，而精确正是把印象变成发现的关口。

senses.title: Comparative historical analysis
senses.definition: the comparison of historical cases or periods to identify causes and patterns
senses.definitionCN: 比较历史案例或时期，以找出原因与模式
senses.example: Comparative historical analysis explained why two revolutions ended so differently.
senses.exampleCN: 比较历史分析解释了两场革命为何结局迥异。
senses.why: History never repeats a case exactly, so the method compares near-cases to isolate what mattered.
senses.whyCN: 历史不会原样重演，方法便比较相近的案例，以分离出真正起作用的因素。

senses.title: A business cost comparison
senses.definition: a structured comparison of costs, benefits or options before a decision
senses.definitionCN: 决策前对成本、收益或备选方案所作的结构化比较
senses.example: The board asked for a comparative analysis of building versus leasing.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会要求对自建与租赁作一份比较分析。
senses.why: Firms compare options on one sheet so that a choice can be defended later.
senses.whyCN: 企业把备选方案放在一张表上比较，好让日后的选择有据可依。

senses.title: A research design
senses.definition: a formal design in which case selection and comparison are planned in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先规划好案例选择与对照方式的一种正式研究设计
senses.example: The course teaches comparative analysis as a design, not just a technique.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课把比较分析当作一种研究设计来教，而不只是一种技巧。
senses.why: Choosing which cases to compare decides the answer before the data arrive, so it belongs to design.
senses.whyCN: 选哪些案例来比，在数据到手前就决定了答案，所以它属于设计。

intro.en: Comparative analysis joins a Latin pair of words meaning 'to pair together' and a Greek one meaning 'to loosen up'. Both halves are well documented; the compound itself is a modern research label.
intro.cn: comparative analysis 把一个意为「配成对」的拉丁词与一个意为「拆开松开」的希腊词合在一起。两半的来源都有充分记录，这个复合词本身则是现代研究标签。

items.en: Latin comparare meant to bring two things level and measure one against the other, from com- 'together' and parare 'to make ready'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 comparare 意为把两物摆平、互相比量，由 com-「一起」与 parare「使齐备」构成。

items.en: The Latin adjective comparativus marked whatever serves for comparison, and English took it as comparative.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词 comparativus 标出用于比较之物，英语取为 comparative。

items.en: Greek analyein meant to loosen or break up a whole into its parts, from ana- 'up, throughout' and lyein 'to loosen'.
items.cn: 希腊语 analyein 意为把整体松开、拆成部分，由 ana-「向上、彻底」与 lyein「松开」构成。

items.en: The two words were joined in nineteenth-century research writing, when comparison became an organised method.
items.cn: 这两个词在十九世纪的研究写作中结合，当时比较已成为有组织的方法。

items.en: Anatomy, law and religion all developed a comparative method, and each needed a name for its core operation.
items.cn: 解剖学、法学与宗教学都发展出比较方法，各自都需要一个名称来指其核心操作。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase settled as a term for cross-case research in social science and policy.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这一短语定型为社会科学与政策研究中跨案例研究的术语。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two roots or looks close; the second group holds methods that are often put beside comparative analysis.
note.cn: 第一组或共享两个词根之一，或字形相近；第二组是常与比较分析并列的其他方法。

entries.definition: The adjective alone, naming work based on comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 单用的形容词，指以比较为基础的工作。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or the contrast, without the method's formality.
entries.definitionCN: 指比较动作或对照的名词，不含方法上的正式性。

entries.definition: The breaking up of a whole into parts, the second half of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 把整体拆成部分，是这个词组的后一半。

entries.definition: The adjective from analysis, describing a method that separates parts.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 analysis 的形容词，描述拆解部分的方法。

entries.definition: A deep study of one case, which comparative analysis deliberately contrasts with others.
entries.definitionCN: 对单一案例的深入研究所，比较分析有意拿它与别的案例对照。

entries.definition: A study of many cases at one moment, usually statistical rather than historical.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一时点考察许多案例，通常偏统计而非历史。

entries.definition: Comparing one's own performance with an external standard, common in management.
entries.definitionCN: 把自身表现与外部标准相比，常见于管理领域。

entries.definition: Combining the results of many studies into one statistical summary.
entries.definitionCN: 把许多研究的结果合成一个统计汇总。

entries.definition: Systematically coding texts, which may then be compared across sources.
entries.definitionCN: 对文本系统编码，随后可跨来源比较。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real two roots, the real fixed phrases and the real research family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的两个词根、真实固定说法与真实研究词族。

normal.en: The first half says pair together, the second half says break apart, so the phrase means pair cases and take them apart.
normal.cn: 前一半说配成对，后一半说拆开来，整个词组就是先把案例配对再拆开看。

normal.en: The family runs compare, comparison, comparative, analyse and analysis.
normal.cn: 同族词有 compare、comparison、comparative、analyse 与 analysis。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: conduct a comparative analysis, cross-national comparative analysis, comparative legal analysis.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：进行比较分析、跨国比较分析、比较法律分析。

normal.en: The plural is comparative analyses, because the head noun is analysis.
normal.cn: 复数形式是 comparative analyses，因为中心词是 analysis。

normal.en: A comparative analysis always names its cases, since the second case is half the method.
normal.cn: 比较分析总要说明拿哪些案例来比，因为第二个案例就是方法的一半。

abstract.en: Comparison without analysis lists differences; analysis without comparison explains only one world.
abstract.cn: 只比较不分析，只是列出差别；只分析不比较，只解释一个世界。

abstract.en: The method's honesty lies in saying which cases were left out.
abstract.cn: 这一方法的诚实，在于说出哪些案例被漏掉了。

abstract.en: Analysis without a second case is a portrait; comparison without analysis is a list.
abstract.cn: 没有第二个案例的分析只是一幅肖像；没有分析比较只是一张清单。

examples.en: Their comparative analysis of the two health systems took four years.
examples.cn: 他们对两套医疗体系的比较分析花了四年。

examples.en: A comparative analysis of rainfall records explained the crop failure.
examples.cn: 对降雨记录的比较分析解释了这次歉收。

examples.en: The paper's comparative analysis is careful about what the cases share.
examples.cn: 这篇论文的比较分析对案例之间的共同点很谨慎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「先配对、再拆开」——把几个案例并排摆好，逐项对看：比较分析

root: comparative（拉丁语 comparativus ← comparare「配成对」← com-「一起」＋ parare「使齐备」）＋ analysis（希腊语 analyein「松开、拆解」← ana-「彻底」＋ lyein「松开」）。复合术语于十九世纪研究写作中成形，二十世纪定型为跨案例研究之名。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one method: a cross-case design, policy comparison, legal comparison, literary comparison, statistical groups, historical cases, business options, and the design itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种方法展开：跨案例设计、政策比较、法律比较、文学比较、统计分组、历史案例、商业备选方案，以及研究设计本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two open tables side by side, with entries in the same column joined by red lines.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张摊开的表格并排，同一栏的条目被红线两两连起。

branches.en: THE METHOD AND THE DESIGN: cases chosen and compared on purpose, not merely noticed.
branches.cn: 方法与设计：案例是被有意挑选、有意对照的，不只是顺手看见。

branches.en: THE PRACTICAL CHOICE: policies and business options weighed on one sheet before a decision.
branches.cn: 实务上的取舍：政策与商业备选方案在决策前放到一张表上称量。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION AND THE PERIOD: legal codes compared, and historical cases set beside each other.
branches.cn: 制度与时期：法典被对照，历史案例被并置。

branches.en: THE LITERARY COMPARISON: two traditions read against each other so that conventions show.
branches.cn: 文学比较：两个传统互相映照，使成规显形。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: groups and cohorts compared with data rather than with impression.
branches.cn: 数字：用数据而非印象比较组别与队列。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin comparative adjective and a Greek noun of breaking up, both still productive in English.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁的比较形容词与希腊的拆解名词合在一起，两者在英语中仍有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Comparare supplies the first half; analyein supplies the second, through Latin and French forms.
latinIntro.cn: 前半出自 comparare，后半出自 analyein，经由拉丁与法语形态进入英语。

items.meaning: a study by comparison of cases
items.meaningCN: 通过比较案例所作的研究
items.example: The phrase is a fixed research term.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语是固定的研究术语。

items.example: It gives the first half its pairing sense.
items.exampleCN: 它给前半部分配对之意。

items.example: It also builds prepare and repair.
items.exampleCN: 它还构成 prepare 与 repair。

items.example: It turns comparare into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把 comparare 变成形容词。

items.example: It gives analysis the sense of taking apart thoroughly.
items.exampleCN: 它给 analysis 彻底拆解之意。

items.example: The root supplies the image of loosening a knot.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供解开绳结的意象。

items.example: It builds analysis, synthesis and diagnosis.
items.exampleCN: 它构成分析、综合与诊断等词。

items.example: It builds analytical from analysis.
items.exampleCN: 它从 analysis 造出 analytical。

items.example: It builds analyst, the person who does the work.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 analyst，指做这项工作的人。

latinEntries.example: The verb supplies the comparing half of the term.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词提供该术语中「比较」那一半。

latinEntries.meaning: a loosening; a resolving into parts
latinEntries.example: Greek analysis means a loosening up, a resolving into parts.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 analysis 意为松开，即拆解为部分。

latinEntries.example: Greek lyein means to loosen, and gives -lysis in English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 希腊语 lyein 意为松开，并给出英语的 -lysis。

definition_zh: 温度波动；温度在某段时间内围绕基准值上下起伏的现象
definition_en: the rise and fall of temperature around a baseline over a period of time
core_image: 恒温箱的记录纸上，一条锯齿线始终围着平直的基准线上下抖动
scene: 实验室的恒温箱前，技术员盯着记录纸上的锯齿线，那条线始终围着一条平直的基准线上下抖动。 The chart showed a small temperature fluctuation around the set point.
sceneCN: 这里指受控设备中围绕设定值的温度波动（第 5 个义项：恒温系统内的温度起伏）；句意为记录图显示设定点附近有小幅温度波动。图中可辨识物件：恒温箱、记录纸、锯齿曲线、基准线。

pos.zh: 名词短语：可数，指一次或一段温度起伏；常带表示幅度的介词短语

collocations.phrase: a temperature fluctuation of two degrees

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语表示「调和、适度」的动词派生，义为「温度」
由拉丁语表示「波动」的动词构成，义为「起伏；波动」
由动词加表示「作用、过程」的词尾构成，义为「波动」
由动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「起伏不定的」
与本短语第一成分同源，义为「温和的；温带的」

senses.title: Rise and fall around a baseline
senses.definition: the general movement of temperature up and down rather than in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 温度上下往复而非单向变化的总体运动
senses.example: A temperature fluctuation of two degrees was enough to change the reaction rate.
senses.exampleCN: 两度的温度波动就足以改变反应速率。
senses.why: Change can be directional or oscillating, and this phrase names the oscillating kind.
senses.whyCN: 变化可以是单向的，也可以是往复的，这个短语命名的是往复的那一类。

senses.title: Short-term wobble versus trend
senses.definition: a brief departure from the average that carries little information about the long run
senses.definitionCN: 对平均值的短暂偏离，对长期走势几乎不提供信息
senses.example: A single temperature fluctuation says little about a long-term trend.
senses.exampleCN: 单次温度波动对长期趋势说明不了什么。
senses.why: Mixing up a wiggle with a slope is one of the commonest mistakes in reading data.
senses.whyCN: 把一次抖动当成一段斜坡，是读数据时最常见的错误之一。

senses.title: Diurnal fluctuation
senses.definition: the daily cycle of warming by day and cooling by night
senses.definitionCN: 白天升温、夜间降温的每日循环
senses.example: Diurnal temperature fluctuation is largest under clear skies and dry air.
senses.exampleCN: 晴朗干燥的空气下，昼夜温度波动最大。
senses.why: Sunlight arrives and leaves on a schedule, so the temperature follows a daily rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 阳光按时间表到来与离开，温度便随之有每日的节律。

senses.title: Seasonal fluctuation
senses.definition: the yearly swing between warm and cold seasons
senses.definitionCN: 一年之中暖季与冷季之间的摆动
senses.example: Seasonal temperature fluctuation drives the timing of migration.
senses.exampleCN: 季节温度波动决定迁徙的时间。
senses.why: The planet's tilt imposes a yearly wave, and living things read that wave as a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 行星的倾斜造成一年的波，生物把这列波读成日历。

senses.title: Fluctuation in a controlled system
senses.titleCN: 受控系统中的温度波动
senses.definition: the small deviation from a set point inside an oven, incubator or reactor
senses.definitionCN: 烤箱、培养箱或反应器内偏离设定值的小幅偏差
senses.example: The incubator keeps temperature fluctuation below a tenth of a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这台培养箱把温度波动控制在十分之一度以内。
senses.why: Control engineering cares about the size of the wiggle, not the average alone.
senses.whyCN: 控制工程关心抖动的幅度，而不只是平均值。

senses.title: Fluctuation in climate records
senses.titleCN: 气候记录中的温度波动
senses.definition: a multi-year or multi-century rise and fall recovered from proxies and instruments
senses.definitionCN: 从代用资料与仪器中复原的多年或数百年尺度的升降
senses.example: Proxy records reveal a temperature fluctuation that lasted several centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 代用资料揭示了一次持续数百年的温度波动。
senses.why: Past climates are read as waves, so the phrase describes the shape rather than a single value.
senses.whyCN: 过去的气候被读成波，因此这个短语描述的是形状而非单个数值。

senses.title: Statistical fluctuation
senses.definition: variation that comes from random sampling rather than from a real physical change
senses.definitionCN: 源于随机抽样而非真实物理变化的变化
senses.example: Some of the variation is just statistical temperature fluctuation, not a real signal.
senses.exampleCN: 其中一部分变化只是统计上的温度涨落，并非真实信号。
senses.why: Randomness alone can produce wiggles, so a signal has to rise above the noise.
senses.whyCN: 随机性本身就能制造抖动，因此信号必须高出噪声。

senses.title: Body temperature fluctuation
senses.definition: the normal or abnormal daily variation in the temperature of a living body
senses.definitionCN: 活体温度的正常或异常日常变化
senses.example: A temperature fluctuation of half a degree can signal an infection.
senses.exampleCN: 半度的体温波动就可能提示感染。
senses.why: Physiology uses a narrow band, so even a small wiggle becomes clinically meaningful.
senses.whyCN: 生理学的带宽很窄，因此即使很小的抖动也具有临床意义。

senses.title: Ocean temperature fluctuation
senses.definition: the rise and fall of sea surface temperature that buoys and satellites track
senses.definitionCN: 浮标与卫星所追踪的海表温度升降
senses.example: Ocean temperature fluctuation on the equator is what the buoys are built to track.
senses.exampleCN: 赤道上的海温波动正是这些浮标被造出来追踪的对象。
senses.why: The ocean stores and releases heat slowly, so its wiggles run on longer periods than air.
senses.whyCN: 海洋缓慢地储存与释放热量，因此它的波动周期比空气更长。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun for a moderate mixture with a Latin noun for wave motion. Both roots are well documented; the phrase itself was assembled in scientific writing, so its first appearance is dated only approximately.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示「适度调和」的拉丁名词，与一个表示波浪运动的拉丁名词组合起来。两个词根来源有据；短语本身是在科学写作中组合而成的，首次出现只有约数。

items.en: Temperare meant to mix in due proportion or to moderate.
items.cn: 这个动词表示按适当比例混合或使之适度。

items.en: The noun named a balanced mixture and later the moderate state of the air.
items.cn: 这个名词指调和的比例，后指空气的适中状态。

items.en: English shifted the noun from balance to the degree of heat measured by a scale.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词从「平衡」转到用刻度测量的热度。

items.en: Fluctus meant a wave on water, from the verb for flowing.
items.cn: 这个词表示水面上的波浪，来自表示「流动」的动词。

items.en: The verb meant to move like a wave, to rise and fall, to waver.
items.cn: 这个动词表示像波浪一样运动、上下起伏、摇摆。

items.en: Scientific writing joined the two nouns to name heat that will not hold still.
items.cn: 科学写作把两个名词连在一起，命名不肯静止的热度。

note.en: The first group shares the word temperature but names different features of it; the second group names other kinds of up-and-down movement.
note.cn: 第一组共享「温度」一词但指它的不同特征；第二组指其他上下起伏的运动。

entries.definition: The rate at which temperature changes with distance.
entries.definitionCN: 温度随距离变化的速率。

entries.definition: A layer where temperature rises with height instead of falling.
entries.definitionCN: 温度随高度上升而非下降的一层大气。

entries.definition: The departure of temperature from a long-term average.
entries.definitionCN: 温度对长期平均值的偏离。

entries.definition: The span between the highest and lowest values.
entries.definitionCN: 最高值与最低值之间的跨度。

entries.definition: A device that converts heat into a reading.
entries.definitionCN: 把热量转换为读数的装置。

entries.definition: A change in amount or level.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或水平的变化。

entries.definition: A regular back-and-forth movement.
entries.definitionCN: 有规律的往复运动。

entries.definition: A large movement from one extreme to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个极端到另一端的大幅移动。

entries.definition: A departure from a standard or expected value.
entries.definitionCN: 对标准或预期值的偏离。

entries.definition: Random variation that obscures a signal.
entries.definitionCN: 掩盖信号的随机变化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow one line on a chart as it wiggle around a straight reference; abstract ones treat fluctuation as information that must be separated from trend and noise.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想跟随图上一条围着直线抖动的曲线；抽象联想把波动看作必须与趋势、噪声分开的信息。

normal.en: A recorder draws a sawtooth around a straight set line.
normal.cn: 记录仪在平直的设定线周围画出锯齿。

normal.en: At dawn the line climbs, at night it falls, and that is the daily wiggle.
normal.cn: 黎明曲线上升，夜里下降，那就是每日的抖动。

normal.en: A summer and winter swing is just the same wiggle at a slower tempo.
normal.cn: 夏冬之间的摆动只是同一抖动放慢了节奏。

normal.en: A good oven keeps its wiggle smaller than a tenth of a degree.
normal.cn: 好的烤箱把抖动控制在十分之一度以内。

normal.en: Buoys watch the same wiggle on the surface of the ocean.
normal.cn: 浮标在海洋表面观察同一种抖动。

abstract.en: Fluctuation is a wave in a number, not necessarily a wave in the world.
abstract.cn: 波动是数字里的波，未必是世界里的波。

abstract.en: Before calling a wiggle a trend, ask how long the record is.
abstract.cn: 把抖动称为趋势之前，先问记录有多长。

abstract.en: Every measurement carries a small tremble that belongs to the instrument, not the object.
abstract.cn: 每个测量都带着一点颤抖，那属于仪器而不属于对象。

examples.en: The reactor is designed to tolerate a small temperature fluctuation.
examples.cn: 该反应堆被设计成能承受小幅温度波动。

examples.en: Scientists separated the long-term trend from yearly temperature fluctuation.
examples.cn: 科学家把长期趋势与逐年温度波动分开。

examples.en: A sudden temperature fluctuation cracked the glass.
examples.cn: 一次突然的温度波动使玻璃裂了。

dict_mnemonic.text: temperature（温度）+ fluctuation（波动）——温度的上下起伏，即温度波动

root: 由 temperature 与 fluctuation 组合。前者源自拉丁语 temperatura「调和的比例」，出自 temperare「调和、使适度」；后者源自拉丁语 fluctus「波浪」及其动词 fluctuare「起伏摇摆」，与表示「流动」的词根相关。短语在科学写作中组合而成，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses take one wiggle and read it at different scales: around a baseline, against a trend, across a day, a season, a machine, a century, a sample, a body and an ocean.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项拿同一次抖动在不同尺度上解读：围绕基准、对照趋势、跨一天、跨一季、在一台设备里、跨一个世纪、在一个样本里、在一具身体里与在一片海洋上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sawtooth line hugging a straight reference line on recorder paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录纸上贴着直线基准的锯齿曲线。

branches.en: THE CORE: up-and-down motion, and the warning not to mistake it for a slope.
branches.cn: 核心：上下往复的运动，以及不要把它误认成斜坡的提醒。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR SCALES: one turn of the earth and one turn of the year.
branches.cn: 日历尺度：地球自转一圈与一年一圈。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: a set point and the small deviation allowed around it.
branches.cn: 机器：一个设定点，以及允许其周围的小偏差。

branches.en: THE LONG RECORD AND THE SAMPLE: centuries recovered from proxies, and randomness inside a measurement.
branches.cn: 长记录与样本：从代用资料复原的数百年，以及测量内部的随机性。

branches.en: THE TWO BODIES: a narrow physiological band and the slow heat of the sea.
branches.cn: 两个躯体：狭窄的生理带宽与海洋缓慢的热量。

intro.en: Two Latin roots, one of moderation and one of waves, supply both halves of the phrase.
intro.cn: 两个拉丁词根，一个表示「调和」，一个表示「波浪」，提供了短语的两半。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies temperare and its noun for balanced heat, then fluctus and its verb for wave motion; English adds the noun endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示调和及其名词，以及表示波浪的名词与动词；英语加上名词词尾。

items.example: The idea of balance is older than the idea of heat.
items.exampleCN: 「平衡」的观念比「热度」的观念更古老。

items.example: The noun moved from mixture to the state of the air.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从「混合比例」转到空气的状态。

items.example: It forms the English noun for the measured state.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示被测状态的英语名词。

items.example: It is the root of all the wave words in the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是短语中所有「波」类词的根。

items.example: The verb describes motion that will not settle.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描述不肯安定下来的运动。

items.example: It turns the verb into the name of the movement.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成该运动的名称。

items.example: The first half of the phrase names what is moving.
items.exampleCN: 短语的前半命名了在动的东西。

items.example: The second half names how it moves.
items.exampleCN: 短语的后半命名了它如何动。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语表示「调和、适度」的动词派生，义为「温度」
由拉丁语表示「波动」的动词构成，义为「起伏；波动」
由动词加表示「作用、过程」的词尾构成，义为「波动」
由动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「起伏不定的」
与本短语第一成分同源，义为「温和的；温带的」

definition_zh: n. 复制；重复；副本；（生物）重复段
definition_en: the act of making an exact copy, a needless repeat of work, or a thing produced as a second copy
core_image: 复印机连续吐出同一页纸，纸盘里叠成一模一样的一摞；同一间办公室两面墙上贴着同一张进度表，各由一个队伍更新；档案柜里正本与副本并放，副本角上盖着「复制」章
scene: 复印机连续吐出同一页纸，纸盘里叠成一模一样的一摞，连页边的订书钉孔都对齐。 The duplication of the file took only a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 duplication 指「制作与某物完全一样的副本这一行为」（第 1 个义项：复制）；句意是复制这份文件只花了一分钟。图中可辨识物件：复印机、一模一样的一摞纸、对齐的订书钉孔。

pos.zh: 复制；重复；副本；（生物）重复段

forms.label: 复数（多份副本／多次重复）

senses.title: Making a copy
senses.definition: the act of making an exact copy of something
senses.definitionCN: （名词）制作与某物完全一样的副本这一行为
senses.example: The duplication of the file took only a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 复制这份文件只花了一分钟。
senses.why: A copier keeps handing out the same page until the tray holds one identical stack.
senses.whyCN: 复印机不停吐出同一页，直到纸盘里叠成一模一样的一摞。

senses.title: A needless repeat
senses.definition: the act of doing something again so that effort or material is wasted
senses.definitionCN: （名词）把某事再做一遍，致使人手或材料白费
senses.example: Two departments ran the same survey, a duplication of effort nobody had planned.
senses.exampleCN: 两个部门做了同一项调查，这是谁也没安排过的重复劳动。
senses.why: Two walls in one office carry the same progress chart, each updated by a different team.
senses.whyCN: 同一间办公室的两面墙上贴着同一张进度表，各由一个队伍更新。

senses.title: A second copy
senses.definition: a thing produced as an exact copy of another
senses.definitionCN: （名词）作为另一物的完全复制品而产生的东西
senses.example: The archive keeps a duplication of every signed contract in a separate room.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆在另一个房间保存着每份已签合同的副本。
senses.why: A cabinet holds the original and its copy, the copy stamped in one corner.
senses.whyCN: 档案柜里放着正本与副本，副本角上盖着一个章。

intro.en: Duplication is the noun of duplicare, to fold twice: the ending -ation turns the folding into an act, so duplication is either the making of a second copy or the copy that results.
intro.cn: duplication 是 duplicare「折两次」的名词：-ation 把折叠变成一个行为，所以 duplication 既指做出第二份的动作，也指由此产生的那一份。

items.en: Latin duo means two.
items.cn: 拉丁语 duo 意为二。

items.en: Latin plicare means to fold.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠。

items.en: Latin duplicare means to double or to fold twice.
items.cn: 拉丁语 duplicare 意为加倍或折两次。

items.en: Latin duplicatio names the act of doubling.
items.cn: 拉丁语 duplicatio 指加倍这一行为。

items.en: English duplication is borrowed for the making of a second copy.
items.cn: 英语 duplication 被借入，指做出第二份。

items.en: The word covers copying, wasted repetition and repeated segments in genes or data.

dict_mnemonic.text: duplication ＝ duplicate（复制）＋ -ation（行为名词后缀）＝「折成两份这件事」。拉丁语 duo（二）＋ plicare（折叠）→ duplicare「折两次」。三个用法要分清：duplication of the file 是「复制文件」（有用），duplication of effort 是「重复劳动」（白费），gene duplication 是「基因重复」（演化的原料）。avoid duplication 是公文里最常见的「避免重复」。别和 duplicity（两面派）混。

definition_zh: 股票市场；股票交易所；股市行情
definition_en: the market in which shares of companies are bought and sold
core_image: 一座喧闹的拍卖大厅，无数公司股份在报价声中易手
scene: 午后的交易大厅里，大屏幕上的指数快速下滑，经纪人纷纷抛售手中股份。 The stock market fell sharply after the central bank raised interest rates.
sceneCN: 这里指「股票市场整体」，对应第 1 个义项：买卖公司股份的市场；句意为央行加息后股市大幅下跌。画面要点：交易大厅、行情大屏、下单电话。

pos.zh: 股票市场；股市（可指交易场所、交易体系或整体行情）

senses.title: The market where shares are traded
senses.definition: the system or place in which shares of public companies are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 公开买卖公司股份的体系或场所
senses.example: Pension funds are major players in the stock market.
senses.exampleCN: 养老基金是股票市场的重要参与者。
senses.why: Stock supplies the object and market supplies the meeting place for exchange, so the compound names the arena where shares change hands.
senses.whyCN: stock 提供交易对象，market 提供交换的场所，复合词因此指股份易手的场域。

senses.title: The secondary market for listed shares
senses.titleCN: 已上市股份的二级交易市场
senses.definition: the market in which existing shares are traded after the company has listed them
senses.definitionCN: 公司上市之后，已有股份在投资者之间转手的市场
senses.example: Most trading on the stock market happens between investors, not with the company.
senses.exampleCN: 股票市场上的交易大多发生在投资者之间，而不是与公司本身进行。
senses.why: Once shares exist, the market lets owners exchange them without the company issuing anything new, so the arena becomes a second-hand market for claims.
senses.whyCN: 股份一旦存在，市场就让持有者在彼此之间交换，公司不再发行新东西，于是这个场域成了权利主张的二手市场。

senses.title: The level of prices at a time
senses.definition: the general level or direction of share prices at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻股份价格的总体水平或走向
senses.example: The stock market was up three percent by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到中午时股市上涨了三个百分点。
senses.why: Because the arena is visible mainly through its prices, the name shifts from the place to the number that the place produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个场域主要通过价格显现，于是名称从场所转到场所产生的数字上。

senses.title: The physical exchange building
senses.definition: the building or floor where dealers meet to trade shares
senses.definitionCN: 交易员聚集买卖股份的建筑或交易大厅
senses.example: Tourists photographed the old stock market on Wall Street.
senses.exampleCN: 游客在华尔街拍摄那座古老的证券交易所。
senses.why: Before screens, the market was a room full of shouted orders, so the compound keeps a literal architectural sense.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕时代之前，市场就是一间充满喊价的屋子，因此这个复合词仍保留字面的建筑义。

senses.title: A barometer of the economy
senses.titleCN: 作为经济晴雨表的股市
senses.definition: the stock market understood as an indicator of economic confidence
senses.definitionCN: 被当作经济信心指标的股票市场
senses.example: Policymakers watch the stock market for signs of panic.
senses.exampleCN: 政策制定者观察股市以寻找恐慌迹象。
senses.why: Prices aggregate many people's expectations, so the arena is read as a signal about the wider economy rather than only about companies.
senses.whyCN: 价格汇总了许多人的预期，于是这个场域被读成关于更广经济的信号，而不只是关于公司。

senses.title: The global network of exchanges
senses.titleCN: 全球各交易所组成的网络
senses.definition: the worldwide system of linked exchanges trading shares around the clock
senses.definitionCN: 全球各地交易所在不同时区连成的股份交易体系
senses.example: A shock in one stock market spreads to others within hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个股市的震荡会在数小时内传到其他股市。
senses.why: When many local arenas are connected by information and capital flows, the singular name stands for the whole network.
senses.whyCN: 当许多地方场域被信息与资本流动连在一起，单数的名称就代表整个网络。

senses.title: A speculative arena
senses.definition: the stock market seen as a place of speculation, euphoria and sudden loss
senses.definitionCN: 被视为投机、狂热与骤然亏损之所的股市
senses.example: He lost his savings in the stock market.
senses.exampleCN: 他在股市里赔掉了积蓄。
senses.why: The arena language invites a figurative reading in which traders are players and prices are bets, so the word can name a gamble.
senses.whyCN: 「场域」的说法引出比喻读法：交易者是玩家，价格是赌注，于是这个词也能指一场赌博。

senses.title: Public judgement of company value
senses.titleCN: 对公司价值的公开评判
senses.definition: the daily public assessment of what companies are worth
senses.definitionCN: 每天由市场给出的公司价值评估
senses.example: The stock market valued the startup at twice its sales.
senses.exampleCN: 股市给这家初创公司的估值达到其销售额的两倍。
senses.why: Each trade is a small verdict on value, so the arena becomes a continuous public judgement rather than a mere meeting place.
senses.whyCN: 每一笔交易都是对价值的一次小裁决，于是这个场域成了持续的公开评判，而不只是会面之处。

intro.en: Stock market joins two words of different origins: a Germanic stock for the shares and a Latin market for the place of trade. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stock market 把两个来源不同的词拼在一起：表示股份的日耳曼语 stock，与表示交易场所的拉丁语 market。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stock first meant a post or trunk and later a stored fund; in finance it came to mean the capital of a company divided into shares.
items.cn: stock 最初指木桩或树干，后来指储存的资金；在金融中转而指被分成股份的公司资本。

items.en: Mercatus meant trade or a marketplace, from mercari 'to trade' and merx 'merchandise', the source of merchant and mercantile.
items.cn: mercatus 意为交易或集市，出自 mercari「做买卖」与 merx「商品」，也是 merchant 与 mercantile 的来源。

items.en: Market entered English through Old North French and settled as the ordinary word for a place where buyers and sellers meet.
items.cn: market 经古北法语进入英语，逐渐固定为买卖双方会面之处的常用词。

items.en: The compound stock market is generally dated to the early nineteenth century, when organized exchanges and daily share lists became common.
items.cn: 复合词 stock market 一般定在十九世纪早期，当时有组织的交易所与每日股价表开始普及。

items.en: Electronic trading detached the market from any single floor and made the singular name stand for a worldwide network.
items.cn: 电子交易把市场与任何单一交易大厅分开，使单数名称代表一个全球网络。

note.en: The first group contains phrases that look nearly identical but point to the exchange or the place rather than the market as a whole; the second group names the same arena from other vocabularies.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来几乎相同、却指交易所或场所而非整体市场的说法；第二组用别的词汇指同一场域。

entries.definition: The organized institution that runs trading in shares; it is the venue and operator, while the stock market is the wider activity and price level.
entries.definitionCN: 组织股份交易的有形机构；它指场所与运营者，而股票市场指更广的交易活动与价格水平。

entries.definition: Any place, physical or digital, where buyers and sellers meet; it lacks the specific link to company shares.
entries.definitionCN: 任何实体或数字的买卖双方会面之处；不含与公司股份的具体联系。

entries.definition: The shares themselves; the market is the arena, while stock is what is traded inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 股份本身；market 是场域，stock 是场域中被交易的东西。

entries.definition: A general system of exchange; alone it can mean any trade in goods, services or labour.
entries.definitionCN: 一般的交换体系；单独使用时可以指任何商品、服务或劳动力的交易。

entries.definition: The market for equity, meaning shares; it is the formal finance term for the same arena.
entries.definitionCN: 权益即股份的市场；这是同一场域的正式金融说法。

entries.definition: A common synonym in Australian and New Zealand usage, built on share instead of stock.
entries.definitionCN: 澳大利亚与新西兰常用的同义说法，用 share 而不是 stock 构成。

entries.definition: A continental European stock exchange, especially in French-speaking countries; it names an institution rather than the abstract market.
entries.definitionCN: 欧洲大陆的证券交易所，尤指法语地区；它指机构而非抽象市场。

entries.definition: The market for long-term funds, including both shares and bonds; the stock market is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 长期资金市场，包括股票与债券；股票市场只是其中一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves of the compound, real synonyms and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：复合词两个真实的组成部分、真实同义词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Stock is what is traded; market is where it is traded, so the phrase is transparent.
normal.cn: stock 是被交易的东西，market 是交易发生的地方，所以这个短语一目了然。

normal.en: Stock itself began as a post or trunk and later became stored capital, which is why shares are called stock.
normal.cn: stock 本指木桩或树干，后来变成储存的资本，股份因此被称为 stock。

normal.en: Market comes from a Latin word for trade, the same source as merchant and mercantile.
normal.cn: market 出自拉丁语表示交易词，与 merchant、mercantile 同源。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show its force: crash, rally, index, bubble.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它的力度：崩盘、反弹、指数、泡沫。

normal.en: Stock exchange is the institution; stock market is the activity and the price level.
normal.cn: 证券交易所是机构，股票市场是活动与价格水平。

abstract.en: Picture a vast room where every shout is a tiny verdict on what a company is worth.
abstract.cn: 想象一间巨大的厅堂，每一声喊价都是对公司价值的一次微小裁决。

abstract.en: Picture prices as weather over that room, rising and falling while the floor stays fixed.
abstract.cn: 把价格想成那间厅堂上空的天气，起伏变化而地面不动。

abstract.en: Picture the room dissolving into screens, so the place becomes a network without walls.
abstract.cn: 想象厅堂化入屏幕，场所于是变成没有围墙的网络。

examples.en: The stock market reacted calmly to the election result.
examples.cn: 股市对选举结果反应平静。

examples.en: Small investors can now enter the stock market through apps.
examples.cn: 小投资者现在可以通过应用程序进入股市。

examples.en: A falling stock market often precedes a slowdown in hiring.
examples.cn: 股市下跌往往先于招聘放缓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「stock（股份）+ market（市场）」——买卖股份的市场 → 股票市场

root: stock 出自古英语 stocc「木桩、树干」，后来指储存的资本与股份；market 出自拉丁语 mercatus「交易、集市」，经古北法语进入英语。两者在十九世纪初合成 stock market。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the arena itself to its prices, its buildings, its economic signal, its global network and finally to its speculative and judgemental force.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从场域本身出发，依次转到价格、建筑、经济信号、全球网络，最后落到投机与评判的力量上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowded trading floor where every shouted order is a small verdict on value.
core.cn: 核心意象：拥挤的交易大厅，每一次喊单都是对价值的一次小裁决。

branches.en: THE ARENA: the market is first the meeting place where listed shares change hands.
branches.cn: 场域：市场首先是已上市股份易手的会面之处。

branches.en: PRICE LEVEL: the place is then read through the number it produces each day.
branches.cn: 价格水平：场所再通过它每天产生的数字被读取。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: before screens, the arena was a literal room with a floor and a crowd.
branches.cn: 建筑：屏幕时代之前，场域就是一间有地面、有人群的真实屋子。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND NETWORK: many local arenas linked together become a barometer and a worldwide system.
branches.cn: 信号与网络：许多地方场域连在一起，成了晴雨表与全球体系。

branches.en: GAMBLE AND VERDICT: the same arena can be a place of speculation or a continuous public judgement of worth.
branches.cn: 博弈与裁决：同一场域既可以是投机之地，也可以是对价值的持续公开评判。

intro.en: Stock market combines a Germanic noun and a Latin-derived noun, and each half brings its own small family of compounds.
intro.cn: stock market 由一个日耳曼语名词与一个拉丁来源名词合成，两半各自带来一小族复合词。

latinIntro.en: Market descends from Latin mercatus, which also gives merchant, mercantile and commerce.
latinIntro.cn: market 源自拉丁语 mercatus，merchant、mercantile 与 commerce 也出自这一支。
