definition_zh: 肖像画艺术；肖像画（总称）；人像摄影
definition_en: the art or practice of making portraits, or portraits considered as a group
core_image: 许多张脸在同一面墙上排开，构成一种看人的传统
scene: 美术馆把四个世纪的肖像排成一条线索，从木板画一直排到照片。 The exhibition traces four centuries of portraiture, from panel painting to photography.
sceneCN: 这里 portraiture 指「肖像创作这门艺术及其历史实践」（第 1 个义项：制作肖像的艺术）；句意为展览梳理四个世纪的肖像艺术，从木板画直到摄影。

pos.zh: 肖像画艺术；肖像画总称（通常不可数）

forms.label: 可数用法（少见，指多种实践）

derivatives.zh: portraiture 逆构 → 单幅肖像；从「整体实践」转到「一件作品」
portrait + -ist（人）→ 肖像作者；从「实践」转到「从业者」
self- + portraiture → 自我肖像实践；从「他人」转到「自我」

senses.title: The art of making portraits
senses.definition: the art, skill or practice of making portraits
senses.definitionCN: 制作肖像的艺术、技巧或实践
senses.example: The exhibition traces four centuries of portraiture.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览梳理四个世纪的肖像艺术。
senses.why: The suffix -ure, from Latin -ura, names an activity and its result; added to portrait, it turns one work into the practice that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ure 来自拉丁 -ura，命名活动及其结果；加在 portrait 上，就把单件作品变成生产它的实践。

senses.title: Portraits considered as a group
senses.definition: portraits collectively, especially in a collection or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 肖像作品的集合，尤指一个收藏或传统中的总体
senses.example: The castle's portraiture fills three galleries.
senses.exampleCN: 城堡的肖像藏品装满三个展厅。
senses.why: An uncountable mass noun treats many works as one body, the way furniture gathers many objects.
senses.whyCN: 不可数集合名词把许多作品当作一个整体，正如 furniture 收拢许多物件。

senses.title: A single portrait, in older use
senses.definition: one portrait, a countable use now largely replaced by portrait
senses.definitionCN: 一幅肖像；这一可数用法现在大多被 portrait 取代
senses.example: The inventory lists a portraiture of the duke.
senses.exampleCN: 清单上列有一幅公爵肖像。
senses.why: Before the back-formed portrait spread, portraiture could still mean one picture; the newer word took over the count.
senses.whyCN: 在逆构的 portrait 普及之前，portraiture 仍可指一幅画；较新的词接管了计数功能。

senses.title: A literary portrayal
senses.definition: a description or portrayal of a person in writing
senses.definitionCN: 文字中对一个人的描写或刻画
senses.example: The chapter is a portraiture of the family in one long evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章以漫长的一夜刻画了这个家庭。
senses.why: The metaphor of painting extends to writing: a text can be called a portraiture when it builds a person detail by detail.
senses.whyCN: 绘画的隐喻扩展到写作：当文本逐笔构建一个人物时，就可以被称为一幅 portraiture。

senses.title: The genre in art history
senses.definition: portrait-making as a recognised genre of art
senses.definitionCN: 作为受认可艺术门类的肖像制作
senses.example: Portraiture was ranked below history painting.
senses.exampleCN: 肖像画在等级上低于历史画。
senses.why: Once a practice is classified, its name becomes a genre label in academies and museums.
senses.whyCN: 一旦实践被分类，其名称就成为学院与博物馆中的门类标签。

senses.title: A style or approach within the genre
senses.titleCN: 肖像门类中的风格或路径
senses.definition: a distinctive manner or approach to making portraits
senses.definitionCN: 制作肖像的独特方式或路径
senses.example: Her portraiture avoids the frontal stare.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肖像手法回避正面直视。
senses.why: A practice can be done in different ways, so the mass noun also names a manner, not only the category.
senses.whyCN: 同一实践可以有不同做法，因此这个集合名词也命名一种手法，而不只是类别。

senses.title: The commissioning business
senses.definition: the social and commercial system of commissioning portraits
senses.definitionCN: 委托制作肖像的社会与商业体系
senses.example: Eighteenth-century portraiture depended on aristocratic commissions.
senses.exampleCN: 18 世纪的肖像业依赖贵族委托。
senses.why: Portraits cost money and mark status, so the practice also names the economy of patrons and sitters.
senses.whyCN: 肖像耗资且标示身份，因此这门实践也命名赞助人与被画者构成的经济。

senses.title: Photographic portrait practice
senses.definition: the practice of making portraits with a camera
senses.definitionCN: 用相机制作肖像的实践
senses.example: Studio portraiture moved from painted backdrops to paper rolls.
senses.exampleCN: 影室人像从手绘背景转到纸卷背景。
senses.why: When the camera took over the likeness, the old practice word went with it and named a new medium's version.
senses.whyCN: 当相机接管肖像制作，旧的实践名词也随之而去，命名新媒介中的版本。

intro.en: Portraiture came into English from Old French in the late fourteenth century, from the same verb that gives portray and portrait. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: portraiture 于 14 世纪后期从古法语进入英语，与 portray、portrait 同出一个动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Protrahere 'to draw forth' joined pro- 'forth' and trahere 'to draw'; medieval Latin used it for painting as well as revealing.
items.cn: protrahere「拉出、描绘」由 pro-「向前」与 trahere「拉」组合；中世纪拉丁也用它指绘画，而不只是显露。

items.en: Old French portraire meant 'to draw, paint, portray'; its noun forms supplied both portrait and portraiture.
items.cn: 古法语 portraire 意为「画、描绘」；其名词形式同时提供 portrait 与 portraiture。

items.en: Old French portraiture (twelfth century) meant 'portrait, image, portrayal, resemblance'.
items.cn: 古法语 portraiture（12 世纪）意为「肖像、形象、描绘、相似」。

items.en: English portraiture is recorded in the late fourteenth century for 'the art of making portraits; a painting or drawing'.
items.cn: 英语 portraiture 于 14 世纪后期有记录，指「制作肖像的艺术；一幅绘画或素描」。

items.en: The countable sense 'a portrait' passed to the back-formed portrait in the sixteenth century, leaving portraiture for the art and the collective.
items.cn: 可数义「一幅肖像」在 16 世纪转给逆构的 portrait，portraiture 则保留给艺术与总称。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century photography extended the practice word to camera portraits without changing its core meaning.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪的摄影把这一实践名词扩展到相机肖像，核心意义未变。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words that differ in count or word class; group two holds labels for the practice seen from other trades.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、但计数或词类不同的词；第二组是从其他行当看待这门实践的标签。

entries.definition: A single likeness; portraiture is the practice or the whole body.
entries.definitionCN: 单件形象；portraiture 是实践或整体。

entries.definition: A maker of portraits; the ending -ist names the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 肖像制作者；词尾 -ist 命名从业者。

entries.definition: To depict a person or scene; portraiture is the resulting practice noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描绘人物或场景；portraiture 是相应的实践名词。

entries.definition: The practice of making portraits of oneself; the compound adds self to the practice word.
entries.definitionCN: 制作自我肖像的实践；复合词在实践名词前加了 self。

entries.definition: Portrait-making in paint specifically; portraiture also covers photography, sculpture and drawing.
entries.definitionCN: 特指用颜料制作肖像；portraiture 还涵盖摄影、雕塑与素描。

entries.definition: The act of representing anything in image or words; portraiture is limited to persons and their likeness.
entries.definitionCN: 以图像或文字再现任何事物的行为；portraiture 限于人物及其形象。

entries.definition: The quality of resembling someone, or an image that does so; portraiture is the organised practice of producing such images.
entries.definitionCN: 相似的性质，或相似的形象；portraiture 是生产此类图像的成体系实践。

entries.definition: Image-making with light; photographic portraiture is one branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用光成像；人像摄影是其中的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: portrait + -ure: the activity and its accumulated result.
normal.cn: portrait + -ure：活动及其累积结果。

normal.en: The word came through Old French portraiture from portraire, 'to draw forth'.
normal.cn: 这个词经古法语 portraiture 来自 portraire「向前描出」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the practice: the art of portraiture, British portraiture, commissioned portraiture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出实践：肖像艺术、英国肖像画、委托肖像创作。

normal.en: The family runs portrait, portraits, portraitist, portray and self-portraiture.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 portrait、portraits、portraitist、portray 与 self-portraiture。

normal.en: The -ure ending also appears in literature and furniture, both mass-like nouns of activity or result.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ure 也出现在 literature 与 furniture 中，都是偏集合的活动或结果名词。

abstract.en: Picture many faces lined up until they become one tradition.
abstract.cn: 想象许多张脸排成一行，直到变成一种传统。

abstract.en: Picture a practice that outlives every sitter it depicts.
abstract.cn: 想象一门比它所描绘的每位被画者都活得久的实践。

abstract.en: Picture a verb, a single work and a whole wall sharing one root.
abstract.cn: 想象一个动词、一件作品与一整面墙共享同一个词根。

examples.en: Portraiture was the academy's steadiest source of income.
examples.cn: 肖像画是学院最稳定的收入来源。

examples.en: The book surveys portraiture from panel to screen.
examples.cn: 这本书梳理从木板到屏幕的肖像实践。

examples.en: Her portraiture gives equal weight to hands and faces.
examples.cn: 她的肖像手法给手与脸同等的分量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「portrait（肖像）+ -ure（行为/结果）」——画肖像这件事 → 肖像画艺术

root: 拉丁 protrahere「拉出、描绘」经古法语 portraire 与名词 portraiture（12 世纪），14 世纪后期进入英语，指制作肖像的艺术；16 世纪单数义转给 portrait。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the art itself to the collective body, the older single picture, the literary portrayal, the genre, a style, the commissioning economy and photographic practice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从艺术本身转到作品总称、较早的单幅用法、文学刻画、门类、风格、委托经济与摄影实践。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many faces are lined up on one wall until they form a way of looking at people.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多张脸在同一面墙上排开，直到构成一种看人的方式。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE AND ITS PURSE: making portraits, and the commissions that pay for them.
branches.cn: 实践及其钱袋：制作肖像，以及为此付费的委托。

branches.en: MANY AND ONE: the collective body, then the older countable single picture.
branches.cn: 多与一：作品总称，然后是较早的可数单幅用法。

branches.en: IN WORDS: the practice borrowed for literary character-building.
branches.cn: 文字之中：这门实践被借去构建文学人物。

branches.en: GENRE AND MANNER: the category, then a distinctive way of working inside it.
branches.cn: 门类与手法：先是类别，再是类别内独特的工作方式。

branches.en: THE CAMERA: the same practice in a new medium.
branches.cn: 相机：同一实践在新媒介中的形态。

intro.en: Portraiture is a French noun of action and result; its ending is no longer productive in English, but the root family still is.
intro.cn: portraiture 是法语的动作与结果名词；其词尾在英语中已不再能产，但词根词族仍能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin protrahere and trahere are the deep sources; French supplied the -ure noun shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 protrahere 与 trahere 是深层来源；法语提供 -ure 的名词形态。

items.example: The prefix adds the sense of drawing out.
items.exampleCN: 前缀加上「拉出」之义。

items.example: The root also gives trace and tractor.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 trace 与 tractor。

items.example: The verb became English portray.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词成为英语 portray。

items.example: Literature and furniture use the same ending.
items.exampleCN: literature 与 furniture 用同一个词尾。

items.example: Portraiture filled the long gallery.
items.exampleCN: 肖像画挂满了长厅。

items.structure: French past participle used as noun
items.example: The portrait is signed on the back.
items.exampleCN: 这幅肖像在背面签名。

items.example: The portraitist preferred chalk.
items.exampleCN: 这位肖像画家偏爱粉笔。

items.example: The mural portrays the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 壁画描绘收获。

items.example: Self-portraiture runs through his late work.
items.exampleCN: 自我肖像贯穿他晚期的作品。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun suffix of action or result

definition_zh: 旷工；缺勤；长期缺席的现象
definition_en: the habit or pattern of frequently being absent from work, school, or another duty
core_image: 一排工位上总有几个空位，天天如此
scene: 工厂主管翻看月度记录，发现请病假的人越来越多。 High absenteeism was slowing production at the plant.
sceneCN: 这里 absenteeism 是「旷工、缺勤现象」（第 1 个义项：员工经常不到岗的整体模式）；句意为高缺勤率正在拖慢工厂生产。

pos.zh: 旷工；缺勤（现象）
长期缺席；不到场

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉表示现象的后缀构成，义为「缺席者；旷工者」
由本词去掉后缀构成，义为「缺席的；不在的」
由本词去掉后缀构成，义为「缺席；缺乏」

senses.title: Habitual absence from work
senses.definition: the pattern of workers regularly failing to come to work
senses.definitionCN: 员工经常不到岗的整体模式
senses.example: High absenteeism was slowing production.
senses.exampleCN: 高缺勤率正在拖慢生产。
senses.why: Absenteeism adds -ism to absentee, turning a person who is away into a collective social pattern.
senses.whyCN: absenteeism 在 absentee 后加 -ism，把「不在的人」变成一种集体的社会现象。

senses.title: Pupil absenteeism
senses.definition: the rate at which students miss school
senses.definitionCN: 学生缺课的比例或模式
senses.example: The school reported rising absenteeism in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 学校报告冬季缺课现象上升。
senses.why: The same pattern word applies to schools, where missing class is measured as a rate.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「模式」的词适用于学校，缺课在那里被当作比率衡量。

senses.title: Unexcused absence
senses.definition: absence without a valid reason, considered as a problem
senses.definitionCN: 没有正当理由的缺席，被视为问题
senses.example: The policy targets unexcused absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策针对无正当理由的缺勤。
senses.why: The -ism suffix turns repeated unexcused absence into a recognized category for managers.
senses.whyCN: -ism 后缀把反复的无故缺席变成管理者认可的一类问题。

senses.title: Long-term absence
senses.definition: absence that continues over an extended period
senses.definitionCN: 持续较长时间的缺席
senses.example: Long-term absenteeism often follows a serious illness.
senses.exampleCN: 长期缺勤常常出现在重病之后。
senses.why: When absence lasts long enough to become a state rather than an event, the abstract noun fits.
senses.whyCN: 当缺席长到成为状态而非事件时，这个抽象名词就适用了。

senses.title: Sickness absence
senses.definition: absence attributed to illness, tracked by employers
senses.definitionCN: 归因于疾病的缺勤，由雇主统计
senses.example: Sickness absenteeism rose during the flu season.
senses.exampleCN: 流感季期间因病缺勤上升。
senses.why: Health reasons are the most common source of the pattern, so the word often appears with sickness.
senses.whyCN: 健康原因是最常见的模式来源，因此这个词常与 sickness 连用。

senses.title: An organisational problem
senses.definition: the overall level of absence treated as a management issue
senses.definitionCN: 被当作管理问题处理的整体缺席水平
senses.example: The report links absenteeism to low morale.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把缺勤与士气低落联系起来。
senses.why: Once absence is measured across a workforce, it becomes an indicator of how an organisation is doing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦在整个劳动力范围内衡量缺席，它就成为组织运行状况的指标。

senses.title: Landlord absenteeism
senses.definition: the historical pattern of owners living away from their estates
senses.definitionCN: 历史上地主不住在自己的地产上、长期不在地的现象
senses.example: The old estate suffered from landlord absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧庄园深受不在地主现象之苦。
senses.why: The word once described owners who were absent from their land, an older sense now overshadowed by workplace use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾描述不在自己土地上的所有者，这个较早义如今被职场用法盖过。

senses.title: Absence from meetings
senses.definition: the pattern of members regularly missing meetings
senses.definitionCN: 成员经常不参加会议的模式
senses.example: Committee absenteeism delayed every vote.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会成员的缺席让每次表决都推迟。
senses.why: Any group that expects attendance can turn repeated absence into the same -ism pattern.
senses.whyCN: 任何期待出席的群体，都能把反复缺席变成同样的 -ism 现象。

intro.en: Absenteeism is a modern formation: the person noun absentee plus the suffix -ism for a practice or pattern.
intro.cn: absenteeism 是现代构词：人物名词 absentee 加表示做法或模式的后缀 -ism。

items.en: abesse meant 'to be away', from ab- 'away' and esse 'to be'.
items.cn: abesse 意为「不在、离开」，由 ab-（离开）与 esse（存在）构成。

items.en: The participle absens, 'being away', produced English absent.
items.cn: 分词 absens 意为「不在的」，构成英语 absent。

items.en: English absentee, formed with the person suffix -ee, named someone who lives away from their property or duty.
items.cn: 英语 absentee 由人物后缀 -ee 构成，指不住在自己的产业或岗位所在地的人。

items.en: The suffix -ism turns a person or practice into a named system or pattern.
items.cn: 后缀 -ism 把人物或做法变成被命名的制度或模式。

items.en: Absenteeism appeared in the nineteenth century, first often in reports about landlords who lived away from their estates.
items.cn: absenteeism 出现在十九世纪，最初常见于关于不在地主的报告。

items.en: Modern usage shifted the centre of gravity to workplaces and schools, where absenteeism is measured as a rate.
items.cn: 现代用法把重心转到职场与学校，缺勤在那里被当作比率衡量。

note.en: The first group gathers the person, adjective, and noun from which the word is built; the second gathers words for absence and skipping.
note.cn: 第一组收构成本词的人物、形容词与名词；第二组收表示缺席与逃避的词。

entries.definition: A person who is regularly away from work or property.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席者、旷工者」，指经常不在工作或产业所在地的人。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning not present.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺席的、不在的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席、不在」，指离开的状态。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in a distracted manner'.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「心不在焉地」。

entries.definition: A single period of being away, rather than a repeated pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席」，指一次离开的时段，而非反复的模式。

entries.definition: The practice of staying away from school without permission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「逃学」，指未经允许不去上学的做法。

entries.definition: The fact of not being present at an event or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「未出席、未到场」。

entries.definition: The informal British word for avoiding work or duty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式非正式用语，义为「偷懒、逃避工作」。

entries.definition: A person who fails to appear when expected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爽约者、未到场者」，指应出现却没出现的人。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks build the word from absentee plus -ism and connect it to workplace metrics; the abstract hooks picture the row of empty desks.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点把词拆成 absentee 加 -ism，并联系职场指标；抽象记忆点想象一排空工位。

normal.en: Absentee plus -ism: the person who is away becomes the pattern of being away.
normal.cn: absentee 加 -ism：不在的人变成了「不在」的整体模式。

normal.en: Reduce absenteeism and absenteeism rates are standard management phrases.
normal.cn: reduce absenteeism 与 absenteeism rates 是标准管理短语。

normal.en: Sickness absenteeism separates health-related absence from other kinds.
normal.cn: sickness absenteeism 把与健康相关的缺勤与其他缺勤区分开。

normal.en: Chronic absenteeism describes a long-running pattern rather than one missed day.
normal.cn: chronic absenteeism 描述长期模式，而不是某一天没来。

normal.en: The word began with landlords who lived away from their estates.
normal.cn: 这个词最初指不住在自己庄园的地主。

abstract.en: Picture a row of desks with three chairs empty every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一排工位，每天早上都有三把椅子空着。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with the same dates crossed out month after month.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上同样的日期被一月月地划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a manager's chart with a line that refuses to fall.
abstract.cn: 想象主管的图表上有一条怎么也不下降的线。

examples.en: The company introduced new rules to reduce absenteeism.
examples.cn: 公司出台新规以减少旷工。

examples.en: Absenteeism among night-shift staff remains high.
examples.cn: 夜班员工的缺勤率仍然很高。

examples.en: Chronic absenteeism affects a child's learning.
examples.cn: 长期缺课会影响孩子的学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布森提森」——座位上的名字还在，人却一天天不来，空位成了常态。

root: 英语 absentee（缺席者，源自拉丁语 absens）+ -ism（表示做法或现象的后缀）；核心义是「反复不在场形成的常态」

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from habitual workplace absence to schools, unexcused and long-term patterns, sickness, organisational measures, historical landlords, and meetings.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从职场习惯性缺勤，走到学校、无故与长期模式、病假、组织指标、历史上的地主，以及会议缺席。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of empty desks that stays half empty
core.cn: 核心意象：一排总是空着一半的工位

branches.en: Repeated absence at work becomes a recognized pattern or problem.
branches.cn: 工作中的反复缺席成为被认可的模式或问题。

branches.en: Schools and committees measure absence as a rate.
branches.cn: 学校与委员会把缺席当作比率衡量。

branches.en: Illness is the most common labelled cause of the pattern.
branches.cn: 疾病是这种模式最常见的标注原因。

branches.en: Across a workforce, absence becomes an organisational indicator.
branches.cn: 在整个劳动力范围内，缺席成为组织指标。

definition_en: the act of taking someone away by force or deception, or the movement of a limb away from the body
core_image: 一只手把人和物从原来的位置带走
scene: 监控里，一名男子抱起街边的孩子就上了车。 Police launched an investigation into the abduction of a young boy.
sceneCN: 这里 abduction 是「诱拐、绑架」（第 1 个义项：非法带走他人）；句意为警方对一名男孩被诱拐展开调查。

由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「诱拐者；绑架者；外展肌」
由动词加表示被动者的后缀构成，义为「被绑架者；被诱拐者」

senses.title: Taking a child away
senses.definition: the illegal taking away of a child, often by deception or force
senses.definitionCN: 以欺骗或暴力非法带走儿童
senses.example: The abduction of the child was caught on camera.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子被诱拐的过程被摄像头拍了下来。
senses.why: Latin abducere meant 'to lead away'; the noun abductio named the act of carrying someone off, and the criminal sense grew from that plain image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abducere 意为「带走」；名词 abductio 指把人带离的行为，犯罪义项正是从这个朴素意象发展出来的。

senses.title: Kidnapping an adult
senses.definition: the act of seizing and carrying off an adult against their will
senses.definitionCN: 违背成人意愿将其抓住并带走
senses.example: The gang was convicted of the abduction of a businessman.
senses.exampleCN: 该团伙因绑架一名商人而被定罪。
senses.why: The same leading-away action applies to adults; the word stresses the carrying off rather than the ransom.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「带离」动作也适用于成人；这个词强调的是带走本身，而非赎金。

senses.title: Anatomical abduction
senses.definition: the movement of a limb or body part away from the midline of the body
senses.definitionCN: 肢体或身体部位离开身体中线的动作
senses.example: The therapist tested shoulder abduction through its full range.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师完整测试了肩关节外展的活动范围。
senses.why: Anatomists reused the Latin verb for leading away: the limb is led away from the body's centre line.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家沿用了这个表示「带走」的拉丁动词：肢体被带离身体中线。

senses.title: Abductive reasoning
senses.definition: a form of reasoning that infers the most likely explanation for an observation
senses.definitionCN: 为某个观察推断最可能解释的推理形式
senses.example: Detectives rely on abduction when they form a hypothesis from clues.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探根据线索提出假设时，依靠的正是溯因推理。
senses.why: Logic borrowed the term for 'leading away' because the mind is led away from the observed fact to a possible cause behind it.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借用了「带走」这个词，因为思维被从观察到的事实带向其背后可能的原因。

senses.title: Unlawful taking in law
senses.definition: the legal charge for taking a person away unlawfully, especially a minor
senses.definitionCN: 法律上非法带走他人、尤指未成年人的罪名
senses.example: The court treated the case as abduction rather than a custody dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把此案按诱拐处理，而非监护权纠纷。
senses.why: The law adopts the plain 'leading away' image and fixes it to a charge, so the act itself names the offence.
senses.whyCN: 法律采用「带走」这个朴素意象并把它固定为一项罪名，于是行为本身就成了罪名的名称。

senses.title: Carrying off young animals
senses.definition: the taking away of young animals from their group or parent
senses.definitionCN: 把幼崽从其群体或亲代身边带走
senses.example: Researchers recorded the abduction of a cub by a rival male.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员记录了一头幼崽被敌对雄性带走的情况。
senses.why: Field biology applies the human term to animals when one animal carries off another's young.
senses.whyCN: 野外生物学把人的术语用于动物，指一只动物带走另一只的幼崽。

senses.title: Muscle action of abducting
senses.definition: the action of a muscle that pulls a limb away from the midline
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉把肢体拉离中线的动作
senses.example: The abductor muscle performs abduction of the little finger.
senses.exampleCN: 外展肌完成小指的外展动作。
senses.why: The movement sense is narrowed to the muscle that produces it, so the noun can name the action of a specific muscle.
senses.whyCN: 动作义被收窄到产生它的肌肉上，因此这个名词也能指某块肌肉的具体动作。

senses.title: Alien abduction
senses.definition: a claimed case in which aliens take a person away, usually temporarily
senses.definitionCN: 声称外星人把人带走、通常短暂带离的说法
senses.example: The witness described an alleged alien abduction.
senses.exampleCN: 证人描述了一次据称的外星人绑架。
senses.why: Popular culture stretches the criminal image into science fiction, where the kidnappers come from the sky.
senses.whyCN: 流行文化把犯罪意象延伸到科幻领域，绑架者来自天上。

intro.en: Abduction goes back to a Latin verb meaning 'to lead away', built from a prefix of separation and the verb for leading.
intro.cn: abduction 可追溯到意为「带走」的拉丁语动词，由表示分离的前缀与表示「引导」的动词构成。

items.en: The root *deuk- is reconstructed with the sense 'to lead'; it also lies behind duke and duct.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *deuk- 被重构为「引导」之义；duke 与 duct 也源自它。

items.en: ducere meant 'to lead, draw'; it produced a large family including ductus and dux.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」，衍生出 ductus、dux 等一大批词。

items.en: ab- 'away' plus ducere formed abducere, 'to lead away, carry off'.
items.cn: ab-（离开）与 ducere 构成 abducere，意为「带走、领走」。

items.en: The noun abductio named the act of leading away, including in anatomical writing.
items.cn: 名词 abductio 指带走的行为，解剖学文献中也有此用法。

items.en: English adopted abduction for the criminal sense and for the anatomical movement.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收该词，用于犯罪义项与解剖学动作。

items.en: Logic added the sense of inference to the best explanation, and popular culture added alien abduction.
items.cn: 逻辑学补充了「最佳解释推断」之义，流行文化又补充了「外星人绑架」之义。

note.en: The first group gathers the verb, the person who acts, the person acted upon, and the adjective; the second gathers words for taking a person away.
note.cn: 第一组收动词、施动者、被施动者与形容词；第二组收表示把人带走的词。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Latin pieces, the anatomical pairing, and the criminal collocations; the abstract hooks picture the carrying away.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用拉丁构件、解剖学配对与犯罪搭配；抽象记忆点想象「带走」的动作。

normal.en: ab- means away and ducere means to lead, so abduction is literally a leading away.
normal.cn: ab- 表示离开，ducere 表示引导，因此 abduction 字面就是「带走」。

normal.en: Abduction and adduction are a pair: away from the midline and toward it.
normal.cn: abduction 与 adduction 是一对：一个离开中线，一个靠向中线。

normal.en: Child abduction and attempted abduction are common news collocations.
normal.cn: child abduction 与 attempted abduction 是常见新闻搭配。

normal.en: The abductor takes the abductee; the two endings keep the roles apart.
normal.cn: abductor 带走 abductee；两个后缀把施动者与受动者区分开。

normal.en: Abductive reasoning is the logic sense, inferring the best explanation.
normal.cn: abductive reasoning 是逻辑义，指推断最佳解释。

branches.cn: 解剖学的带离：肢体或肌肉离开中线。

definition_zh: 加强；加剧；强化；增强
definition_en: to make something stronger, sharper or more concentrated, or to become so
core_image: 炉门被拉开，风箱越推越快，火苗从橙红窜成刺眼的白
scene: 谈判没有进展，双方反而把条件提得更高，气氛越来越紧。 Both sides intensify pressure as the talks stall.
sceneCN: 这里指把压力加得更强（第 2 个义项：加剧冲突或压力）；句意为谈判停滞后双方都在加大压力。图中可辨识物件：被拉开的炉门、加速的风箱、窜高的火焰。

pos.zh: 加强；加剧；强化

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「加强；加剧」
由该动词加表示施动者或工具的名词尾构成，义为「加强成分；增强剂」
由同一拉丁词干加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「强度」
由同一拉丁词干构成的形容词，义为「强烈的；紧张的」
由同一词干加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「密集的；加强的」

senses.title: To increase strength
senses.definition: to raise the strength, force or level of an action or quality
senses.definitionCN: 提高某一行动或性质的强度、力度或水平
senses.example: The crew intensified the light before the final inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后检查前，班组把照明加强了。
senses.why: The root means stretched tight, and intensifying is pulling that tension higher.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「拉紧」，加强就是把那股张力再拉高。

senses.title: To sharpen a conflict
senses.definition: to make a dispute, pressure or hostility more acute
senses.definitionCN: 使争端、压力或敌意更尖锐
senses.example: Sanctions intensified the dispute over the border.
senses.exampleCN: 制裁加剧了边境争端。
senses.why: Conflict is tension between two sides, and the verb raises the tension.
senses.whyCN: 冲突是两方之间的张力，这个动词把张力调高。

senses.title: To heighten a feeling
senses.definition: to make an emotion or sensation more vivid or harder to ignore
senses.definitionCN: 使情绪或感觉更鲜明、更难忽视
senses.example: The silence intensified the fear in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默让屋里的恐惧更强烈。
senses.why: Feelings are measured by how tightly they hold attention, so more tension means more feeling.
senses.whyCN: 情绪以攥住注意力的松紧来衡量，张力越大，感受越强。

senses.title: To step up an effort
senses.definition: to make work or a campaign more concentrated and frequent
senses.definitionCN: 使工作或运动更集中、更频繁
senses.example: Volunteers intensified the search after nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 入夜后，志愿者加紧搜寻。
senses.why: Effort has a dial, and the verb turns it up rather than changing its direction.
senses.whyCN: 努力有一个旋钮，这个动词把它拧大，而不是换方向。

senses.title: To raise scrutiny or attention
senses.definition: to make examination, attention or criticism closer and more constant
senses.definitionCN: 使审视、关注或批评更贴近、更持续
senses.example: Regulators intensified checks on the export route.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构加强了对出口路线的检查。
senses.why: Scrutiny is pressure applied to a process, and the verb says the pressure rose.
senses.whyCN: 审视是对流程施加的压力，这个动词说压力升高了。

senses.title: To strengthen an effect
senses.definition: to make the visible or audible effect of something more pronounced
senses.definitionCN: 使某物的视觉或听觉效果更明显
senses.example: The new coating intensified the contrast of the print.
senses.exampleCN: 新涂层增强了印刷的对比度。
senses.why: Effects are read by the senses, and intensifying pushes the reading further from neutral.
senses.whyCN: 效果由感官读取，加强就是把读数推得离中性更远。

senses.title: To concentrate a signal or colour
senses.definition: to increase the concentration of light, sound or colour in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 提高某一区域内光、声或颜色的浓度
senses.example: The filter intensified the red without changing the shape.
senses.exampleCN: 滤镜让红色更浓，却没有改变形状。
senses.why: Technical optics use the verb for concentration, the same tightening applied to a beam.
senses.whyCN: 技术光学用这个动词表示「集中」，即把同一股收紧作用用到光束上。

senses.title: To focus attention sharply
senses.definition: to make focus or concentration narrower and more forceful
senses.definitionCN: 使专注或集中更窄、更有力
senses.example: A deadline intensified her focus on the last chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 截止日期让她把注意力更集中在最后一章。
senses.why: A narrower beam is a stronger beam, which is why focus and intensity share a vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 光束越窄越强，所以「聚焦」与「强度」共用一套词。

intro.en: Intensify is formed in English from intense and the suffix -ify. Intense goes back to Latin intensus, stretched, the participle of intendere, to stretch toward.
intro.cn: 这个词在英语里由 intense 加后缀 -ify 构成；intense 可追溯到拉丁语 intensus「拉紧」，即 intendere「朝……伸展」的分词。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch, and it supplies intend, tend, tension and intense alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为「伸展」，供应了 intend、tend、tension 与 intense。

items.en: Intendere meant to stretch toward or direct attention to, with the prefix marking direction.
items.cn: 这个词意为朝某处伸展或把注意力指向某处，前缀标出方向。

items.en: The participle meant stretched tight, and that physical tightness became the English sense of strong.
items.cn: 这个分词意为「拉得很紧」，而这种物理紧绷变成英语的「强烈」。

items.en: English adopted intense through French, using it for heat, colour, feeling and attention.
items.cn: 英语经法语引入 intense，用于热度、颜色、情绪与注意力。

items.en: The suffix comes from Latin facere, to make, so intensify literally means to make intense.
items.cn: 后缀出自拉丁语 facere「做」，所以这个词字面就是「使强烈」。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the eighteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain in the sources.
items.cn: 这个动词自十八世纪有记录，确切首见年代在各家资料中不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the tense stem or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of increase.
note.cn: 第一组与「intensify」共享「拉紧」词干或只是形近；第二组是与「增强」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the strength or force of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物强度或力度的名词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of making something stronger.
entries.definitionCN: 指加强这一行为的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning very strong or very serious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指非常强烈或非常严肃的。

entries.definition: Purpose or determination, from the same stretching verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指意图或决心，同出「伸展」动词。

entries.definition: To plan or mean to do, literally to stretch toward.
entries.definitionCN: 指打算，字面是「朝……伸展」。

entries.definition: The state of being stretched, the physical source of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 指被拉紧的状态，是这一族词的物理源头。

entries.definition: To make stronger, the broad neutral verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指使更强，是宽泛中性的说法。

entries.definition: To raise the level of a feeling or effect.
entries.definitionCN: 指提高情绪或效果的强度。

entries.definition: To make larger or louder, especially a signal.
entries.definitionCN: 指放大或增强，尤指信号。

entries.definition: To become or make more intense, often of conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 指升级、加剧，多用于冲突。

entries.definition: To make a feeling or problem more profound.
entries.definitionCN: 指使情绪或问题更深。

entries.definition: To add to something, often making it worse.
entries.definitionCN: 指叠加，常使情况更糟。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the stretched-tight participle, the -ify suffix and the fixed objects that pair with the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「拉紧」的分词、-ify 后缀，以及与这个动词固定的宾语。

normal.en: The participle meant stretched tight, so intensify is to tighten the string further.
normal.cn: 分词意为「拉紧」，所以这个词就是把弦再绞紧一点。

normal.en: Intense, intensity, tension and intend all come from the same stretching verb.
normal.cn: intense、intensity、tension、intend 都出自同一个「伸展」动词。

normal.en: The -ify suffix means to make, so the verb means to make intense.
normal.cn: -ify 后缀意为「使」，所以动词就是「使强烈」。

normal.en: Pressure, efforts, competition and scrutiny are its most common objects.
normal.cn: 压力、努力、竞争、审视是它最常见的宾语。

normal.en: It takes -ies, -ied and -ying, and the y never doubles.
normal.cn: 第三人称、过去式、现在分词依次换词尾，词干的字母不双写。

abstract.en: Intensity is not more of the same thing; it is the same thing held tighter.
abstract.cn: 强度不是更多同样的东西，而是同样的东西被攥得更紧。

abstract.en: A beam made narrower is a beam made stronger, and that is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 光束变窄就是变强，这就是这个词的全部。

abstract.en: Pressure intensified is not pressure doubled; it is pressure that no longer leaves room to breathe.
abstract.cn: 压力加大不是压力翻倍，而是不再留出喘息的余地。

examples.en: The company intensified training after the second accident.
examples.cn: 第二次事故之后，公司加强了培训。

examples.en: Wind intensified through the afternoon and closed the ferry route.
examples.cn: 午后风力加大，渡轮航线因此关闭。

examples.en: The debate intensified as new evidence appeared.
examples.cn: 随着新证据出现，争论更加激烈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因坦西法伊」——风箱越推越快，火苗窜成白色：加强、加剧

root: 拉丁语 tendere「伸展」→ intendere「朝……伸展」→ intensus「拉紧的」→ 法语 intense；英语十八世纪以 intense + -ify 构成动词，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all tighten one tension: strength, conflict, feeling, effort, scrutiny, effect, signal and focus.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在收紧同一股张力：力度、冲突、感受、努力、审视、效果、信号与专注。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bellows speed up and the flame turns from orange to a blinding white.
core.cn: 核心意象：风箱越推越快，火苗从橙红变成刺眼的白。

branches.en: THE FORCE RISES: an action or quality is turned up on its own dial.
branches.cn: 力量上升：某项行动或性质在自己的旋钮上被拧大。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE TIGHTENS: a dispute or a system of checks is pressed harder.
branches.cn: 压力收紧：争端或审查体系被压得更紧。

branches.en: THE FEELING SHARPENS: emotion becomes too vivid to ignore.
branches.cn: 感受变锐：情绪鲜明到无法忽视。

branches.en: THE EFFORT THICKENS: work is made more frequent and more concentrated.
branches.cn: 努力变密：工作变得更频繁、更集中。

branches.en: THE EFFECT CONCENTRATES: contrast, colour or focus is brought to a narrower, stronger beam.
branches.cn: 效果集中：对比、色彩或专注被收成一束更窄更强的光。

intro.en: Intensify joins a Latin participle to an English suffix, so its affixes are the pieces of that joining.
intro.cn: 这个词把一个拉丁分词接在一个英语后缀上，其词缀就是这次接合的两端。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies tendere, intendere and intensus; facere supplies the suffix, and every piece is well recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 tendere、intendere、intensus；facere 提供后缀，每个部件都有清楚记录。

items.example: The verb is the physical source of tension.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是「张力」的物理源头。

items.example: It marks direction in intendere.
items.exampleCN: 它在 intendere 中标出方向。

items.example: The participle became the English adjective intense.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成英语形容词 intense。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a verb of increase.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表示增强的动词。

items.example: It appears in words such as intensify and amplify.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 intensify、amplify 这类词里。

items.example: It forms intensification.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intensification。

items.meaning: the one or the thing that acts
items.example: It forms intensifier.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intensifier。

items.example: It forms intensity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intensity。

items.example: It forms intensive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intensive。

items.example: It appears in tension, the oldest family member.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 tension 这个最老的家族成员里。

由该动词加表示施动者或工具的名词尾构成，义为「加强成分」

由同一词干加表示倾向的形容词尾构成，义为「密集的」

definition_zh: 观察；观测；观察结果；评论；（对规则的）遵守
definition_en: the act of watching something carefully, a recorded result of such watching, or a remark based on it
core_image: 一个人站在窗前，手里拿着本子，把鸟落下的时间一秒一秒写下来。
scene: 医生让病人先留院一晚，第二天早上再看检查数据。 The patient stayed in the hospital for a night of observation.
sceneCN: 这里 observation 是“医学上的观察期、留观”（第 4 个义项）；句意：病人留院接受一晚的观察；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观察；观测；观察结果；评论；遵守

senses.title: Watching with attention
senses.definition: the act of watching someone or something closely and with attention
senses.definitionCN: 密切而专注地注视某人或某事的行为
senses.example: Careful observation showed that the birds returned at the same hour each day.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细观察显示，这些鸟每天在同一时刻返回。
senses.why: Observation is not passive seeing: the watcher has chosen an object and a purpose, so attention is the defining element.
senses.whyCN: 观察不是被动地看见：观察者已经选定了对象与目的，因此“专注”才是定义性的要素。

senses.title: A recorded result
senses.titleCN: 观察结果：本子上那行字
senses.definition: a piece of information obtained by watching and often written down for later use
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察获得、常被记录下来备用的信息
senses.example: The notebook contained observations from six mornings at the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 笔记本里记着六个早晨在湖边的观察结果。
senses.why: Once written, the act becomes a fact others can read; the word then names the record rather than the watching.
senses.whyCN: 一旦写下来，行为就变成别人可读的事实；此时这个词命名的是记录，而不是“看”本身。

senses.title: A remark drawn from noticing
senses.definition: a spoken or written remark based on something noticed
senses.definitionCN: 基于所注意到的事情而作出的口头或书面评论
senses.example: His observation that the room felt colder was correct.
senses.exampleCN: 他说房间变冷了，这个观察是对的。
senses.why: The sense shifts from the eye to the mouth: a remark is called an observation when it reports a noticed fact rather than an opinion.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从眼睛移到嘴：当一句话报告的是被注意到的事实而非意见时，它就被称作 observation。

senses.title: A medical watch
senses.titleCN: 留观：先看着，等数据说话
senses.definition: a period during which a patient is watched in hospital before a decision is made
senses.definitionCN: 病人留院接受看护、等待作出决定的一段时间
senses.example: She was kept in observation overnight after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔倒后她被留院观察了一夜。
senses.why: Medicine uses observation as a treatment stage: when the diagnosis is still open, watching is safer than acting.
senses.whyCN: 医学把观察当作一个治疗阶段：诊断尚未确定时，看着比动手更安全。

senses.title: Keeping a rule
senses.titleCN: 遵守：把规定看在眼里并照做
senses.definition: the keeping or honouring of a law, custom, or religious practice
senses.definitionCN: 遵守或尊重法律、习俗或宗教实践
senses.example: Observation of the Sabbath was strict in that community.
senses.exampleCN: 那个社群对安息日的遵守很严格。
senses.why: The older sense of observare is to heed or keep; the same verb that means watch over also means keep faith with a rule.
senses.whyCN: observare 更早的含义是“留意、守护”；同一个既表示“看护”又表示“守信于规则”的动词。

senses.title: A post for watching
senses.titleCN: 观察位：专门用来盯的地方
senses.definition: a place, especially a military one, set up for watching an area
senses.definitionCN: 为监视某一区域而设置的场所，尤指军事用途
senses.example: The soldiers held the observation post on the ridge through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们整夜守住山脊上的观察哨。
senses.why: The act needs a place; when watching is continuous, the place itself takes the name and becomes part of the operation.
senses.whyCN: 观察需要地点；当观察持续进行时，地点本身也取了这个名字，成为行动的一部分。

senses.title: Studying from inside a group
senses.titleCN: 参与式观察：进去，同时记下来
senses.definition: a research method in which the researcher joins a group and records its life while taking part in it
senses.definitionCN: 研究者加入某群体、在参与其生活的同时作记录的研究方法
senses.example: Her participant observation of the night market lasted a full year.
senses.exampleCN: 她对夜市的参与式观察持续了整整一年。
senses.why: The method accepts a tension: to see ordinary life closely one must enter it, yet entering changes what is being observed.
senses.whyCN: 这种方法接受一种张力：要贴近看日常生活就必须进去，可一旦进去，被观察的对象也变了。

senses.title: Measuring the sky
senses.titleCN: 天文观测：把望远镜对准天上
senses.definition: the systematic recording of celestial objects and events with instruments
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器对天体与天象作系统记录
senses.example: The observation of the eclipse required clear skies and an exact location.
senses.exampleCN: 观测这次日食需要晴朗天空和精确地点。
senses.why: Astronomy turns observation into data: the eye is replaced by a detector, and the record must state time, place, and instrument.
senses.whyCN: 天文学把观察变成数据：眼睛被探测器取代，记录必须写明时间、地点与仪器。

intro.en: Observation comes from Latin observatio, a watching or a heed, from observare: ob- 'over, before' plus servare 'to keep, watch over'. Servare also gives preserve, reserve, and conserve.
intro.cn: observation 来自拉丁语 observatio“看护、留意”，出自 observare：ob-“在上、在前”加 servare“守护、留意”。servare 还给出 preserve、reserve、conserve。

items.en: Servare meant to keep, guard, or preserve. The idea of keeping is older than the idea of looking.
items.cn: servare 意为保持、守护、保存。“守”的观念比“看”的观念更早。

items.en: Ob- added the sense of direction or attention: to watch over, to heed, to keep a rule, and to observe signs.
items.cn: ob- 增加了方向与注意的含义：看护、留意、遵守规则，以及观察征兆。

items.en: The noun covered watching, noting, and also compliance with a custom or a law.
items.cn: 该名词涵盖看护、记录，也涵盖对习俗或法律的遵守。

items.en: French kept both the watching sense and the remark sense, and English borrowed both in the 14th century.
items.cn: 法语同时保留了“观察”与“评论”两义，英语于 14 世纪把两者一并借入。

items.en: English observation grew in science and navigation, where watching had to be recorded with time and place.
items.cn: 英语 observation 在科学与航海领域壮大，那里的观察必须连同时间与地点一起记录。

items.en: The 19th and 20th centuries added medical observation, participant observation, and instrument-based astronomical observation.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪增加了医学留观、参与式观察，以及依靠仪器的天文观测。

note.en: The first group is the observe family; the second compares ways of gaining knowledge by watching, checking, or testing.
note.cn: 第一组是 observe 词族；第二组比较通过观看、核查或检验获取知识的几种方式。

entries.definition: to watch carefully, to notice, or to keep a rule. It names the action behind observation.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细观察、注意到，或遵守规则；命名的是 observation 背后的动作。

entries.definition: a person who watches, especially one sent to report on an event.
entries.definitionCN: 观察的人，尤指被派去报道某一事件的人。

entries.definition: quick to notice things; also careful to keep a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 善于注意细节的；也指谨慎守规的。

entries.definition: the keeping of a law, rite, or custom. It is the 'compliance' sense without the scientific one.
entries.definitionCN: 对法律、仪式或习俗的遵守；只有“遵从”义，没有科学观察义。

entries.definition: looking at something over time, often without a formal purpose. Observation adds method.
entries.definitionCN: 持续地看，常无正式目的；observation 则增加了方法。

entries.definition: continuous checking by instruments or staff, usually against limits. It is observation with a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 用仪器或人员持续核查，通常对照限值；是有阈值的观察。

entries.definition: the assignment of a number to a property. It turns observation into quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 给性质赋予数值；它把观察变成数量。

entries.definition: something said briefly. It need not be based on careful watching.
entries.definitionCN: 简短说出的话；不必基于仔细的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ob- 'over' plus servare 'keep'. Observation is keeping watch, and keeping a rule.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ob-“在上”加 servare“守护”。observation 就是守望着，也是守着规则。

normal.en: Observe means both to watch and to keep: the same act of holding something in view.
normal.cn: observe 既表示“看”，也表示“守”：都是把某物保持在视野里。

normal.en: An observation notebook is a watch that leaves a mark.
normal.cn: 观察笔记本就是一只会留下痕迹的表。

normal.en: In hospital, observation is a room where time does the testing.
normal.cn: 在医院，observation 是一间让时间来检验的病房。

normal.en: An observation post is the act of watching with a fixed address.
normal.cn: 观察哨就是有了固定地址的“看”。

normal.en: Astronomers write down three things: what, when, and with which instrument.
normal.cn: 天文学家记三件事：看到了什么、什么时候、用什么仪器。

abstract.en: Observation never arrives pure; the choice of what to watch is already a theory about what matters.
abstract.cn: 观察从不以纯粹状态到来；选择看什么，本身已是关于“什么重要”的理论。

abstract.en: The same verb means to watch and to obey, as if attention and loyalty came from one root.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既表示观看又表示服从，仿佛注意与忠诚出自同一根。

abstract.en: To observe a group closely is to change it; the observer is always part of the observed world.
abstract.cn: 近距离观察一个群体就会改变它；观察者永远是被观察世界的一部分。

examples.en: The ornithologist's observation of the nest lasted from dawn until the chicks fledged.
examples.cn: 这位鸟类学家对鸟巢的观察从黎明持续到雏鸟长出飞羽。

examples.en: After the head injury, the patient stayed under observation for twenty-four hours.
examples.cn: 头部受伤后，病人留院观察了二十四小时。

examples.en: Her observation that the machine ran quieter after warming up turned out to be important.
examples.cn: 她观察到机器预热后运转更安静，后来证明这一点很重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: observe（观察）+ ation（名词）——看得很仔细，还记下来，就是观察、观测。

root: 源自拉丁语 observatio（看护、留意、遵从），出自 observare：ob-“在上、在前”加 servare“守护、保持”。同一词根兼有“看”与“守”两面，因此既指观察、观测，也指对规则、习俗的遵守。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of observation, all descended from one act of keeping watch. The watch can be scientific, medical, military, or social; its product can be a record, a remark, a data set, or a habit of obeying.
sensesIntro.cn: observation 的八个义项都源自同一个“守望”动作。守望可以是科学的、医学的、军事的或社会的；其产物可以是记录、评论、数据集，或遵守的习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a window with a notebook, writing down the exact second a bird lands.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗边的人拿着本子，记下鸟落下的那一秒。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS RECORD: watching with purpose, and the line written down afterwards.
branches.cn: 行为与记录：有目的地看，以及随后写下的那一行。

branches.en: WORD AND RULE: a remark drawn from noticing, and the keeping of a law or custom.
branches.cn: 言语与规则：由注意得出的评论，以及对法律或习俗的遵守。

branches.en: MEDICAL WAITING: a patient watched until the evidence becomes clear.
branches.cn: 医学等待：病人被观察到证据明朗为止。

branches.en: PLACE AND METHOD: a post built for watching, and a researcher watching from inside a group.
branches.cn: 地点与方法：为观察而建的哨位，以及研究者从群体内部观察。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTAL WATCHING: the sky recorded with time, place, and detector.
branches.cn: 仪器化观察：连同时间、地点与探测器一起记录天空。

intro.en: Observation is observe plus -ation, the action-noun suffix. The family adds -er for the person, -ant for the habit, -ance for the keeping of a rule, and -able for what can be seen.
intro.cn: observation 是 observe 加 -ation（动作名词后缀）。词族用 -er 表示人，-ant 表示习性，-ance 表示对规则的遵守，-able 表示可被看见。

latinIntro.en: The base is servare, to keep or guard, with ob- adding the direction of attention. Related Latin words give preserve, reserve, conserve, and servant.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 servare“保持、守护”，ob- 增加注意的方向。相关拉丁词给出 preserve、reserve、conserve、servant。

items.meaning: to watch closely, notice, or keep a rule
items.example: Scientists observe the same plot every spring.
items.exampleCN: 科学家每年春天观察同一块样地。

items.meaning: the act, result, or remark of watching
items.meaningCN: 观察的行为、结果或评论
items.example: His observation was recorded in the margin.
items.exampleCN: 他的观察被记在页边。

items.example: An observer sat at the back of the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 一名观察员坐在会议后排。

items.meaning: quick to notice; careful to comply
items.meaningCN: 善于察觉的；谨慎遵守的
items.example: An observant reader will spot the repeated date.
items.exampleCN: 细心的读者会注意到重复出现的日期。

items.meaning: the keeping of a law, rite, or custom
items.meaningCN: 对法律、仪式或习俗的遵守
items.example: Observance of the treaty was monitored by neutrals.
items.exampleCN: 条约的遵守情况由中立国监督。

items.meaning: able to be seen or noticed
items.example: The effect is observable only at low temperatures.
items.exampleCN: 这一效应只在低温下可观察到。

items.meaning: a place built for watching the sky or nature
items.meaningCN: 为观测天空或自然而建的场所；天文台
items.example: The observatory opens to the public on Fridays.
items.exampleCN: 这座天文台周五向公众开放。

items.meaning: to keep something safe from harm or change
items.meaningCN: 保护某物免受损害或改变；保存
items.example: The salt preserves the fish for the winter.
items.exampleCN: 盐把鱼保存过冬。

items.meaning: to keep back for later use
items.example: They reserved two seats near the window.
items.exampleCN: 他们预留了两个靠窗座位。

items.meaning: to keep from being lost or wasted
items.example: The town conserves water during dry summers.
items.exampleCN: 这个镇在干旱夏季节约用水。

a watching, a remark, a compliance

definition_zh: 财富；大量钱财与资产；也指丰富、充裕
definition_en: a large amount of money, property and other valuable assets; also an abundance of something valuable
core_image: 一间库房堆着金条、地契与粮袋，角落里还立着一架书，物质与精神都显得充足
scene: 老人把一生的积蓄、房产与藏书都写进同一份清单。 The family's wealth grew from land and trade rather than from wages.
sceneCN: 此处指「大量钱财与资产」（第 1 个义项：可估价的财富总量）；句意为这家人的财富来自土地与贸易，而非工资。图中可辨识物件：金条、地契、粮袋、书架。

pos.zh: 财富；钱财与资产
丰富；大量（用于表示「大量……」的固定结构）

forms.label: 复数（罕见，指多种财富形态）

senses.title: A large amount of money and assets
senses.definition: a great quantity of money, property, investments and other valuable things owned by a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体拥有的大量金钱、房产、投资及其他贵重物品
senses.example: Her wealth came from shares in the family firm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的财富来自家族企业的股份。
senses.why: The word names a large store of what people value, so its first sense is simply the quantity of money and goods held.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是人们所看重之物的大量积蓄，因此第一义就是所持金钱与物品的数量。

senses.title: Total net assets of a person or group
senses.titleCN: 个人或群体的净资产总额
senses.definition: the total value of assets minus debts, viewed as a stock at a point in time
senses.definitionCN: 资产总值减去负债，作为某一时点的存量看待
senses.example: The survey measures household wealth as assets minus mortgage debt.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把家庭财富算作资产减去房贷。
senses.why: Accounting turns a pile of possessions into a single net figure, which is the technical stock sense.
senses.whyCN: 会计把一堆财物变成一个净值数字，这就是技术性的存量义。

senses.title: Valuable natural resources
senses.definition: minerals, fertile land, water, forests and other natural endowments that a place possesses
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方拥有的矿产、沃土、水源、森林等自然禀赋
senses.example: The region's wealth lay in its forests and rivers.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的财富在于森林与河流。
senses.why: A country can be rich without money in banks, because land and resources are also stores of value.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家可以没有银行存款仍然富足，因为土地与资源也是价值储备。

senses.title: Prosperity and wellbeing
senses.definition: the older sense of a good and flourishing condition, close to welfare rather than to money alone
senses.definitionCN: 较古的义项，指良好兴旺的处境，接近福祉而非单指金钱
senses.example: The old prayer asked for health and wealth for the household.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的祷词为全家祈求健康与兴旺。
senses.why: Before it meant money, the word meant a good state of life, and that older flourishing sense still colours religious and ceremonial use.
senses.whyCN: 在指金钱之前，这个词指良好的生活状态，这一较古的兴旺义仍影响宗教与仪式用语。

senses.title: An abundance of a thing
senses.definition: a large supply or great amount of something, as in a wealth of detail or experience
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大量供应，如大量细节或丰富经验
senses.example: The archive offers a wealth of detail about daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 这座档案馆提供了关于日常生活的丰富细节。
senses.why: Abundance of money and abundance of anything share the same shape, so the word extends to non-material plenty.
senses.whyCN: 钱财的充裕与任何东西的充裕形状相同，因此这个词扩展到非物质的丰富。

senses.title: The collective riches of a society
senses.definition: the total stock of valuable assets held by a whole society or economy
senses.definitionCN: 整个社会或经济所持有的有价值资产总量
senses.example: Economists study how wealth is distributed across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家研究财富在全国如何分布。
senses.why: Once the word is applied to a whole society, it names an aggregate stock rather than one person's fortune.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦用于整个社会，命名的就是总存量，而非某个人的财产。

senses.title: Inherited or accumulated stock
senses.definition: riches passed down or built up over time rather than earned in a single transaction
senses.definitionCN: 经继承或长期积累而非一次交易所得的钱财
senses.example: Much of the family's wealth had been inherited from two generations back.
senses.exampleCN: 这家的财富很多是两代之前继承下来的。
senses.why: Wealth accumulates, so it often carries the idea of a stock built or handed down across time.
senses.whyCN: 财富会累积，因此常带有跨时间积累或传下的存量意味。

senses.title: The common good in older usage
senses.definition: the public good or general wellbeing of a community, preserved in the compound commonweal
senses.definitionCN: 共同体的公共利益或整体福祉，保留在「公共福祉」这一复合词中
senses.example: Old writers spoke of the wealth of the realm as its common good.
senses.exampleCN: 古代作者把国家的财富说成公共之善。
senses.why: The oldest sense tied riches to the health of a community, and traces of it survive in formal and historical language.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项把财富与共同体的健全相连，其痕迹仍留在正式与历史语体中。

intro.en: Wealth is native English, built from an Old English noun for wellbeing with an abstract suffix. It has no Latin ancestor and dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 财富是英语本族词，由古英语中表示安好的名词加抽象后缀构成。它没有拉丁语祖先，年代均为约数。

items.en: Wela meant 'wellbeing, prosperity, riches' and was related to the word for 'well'. It described a good condition before it described money.
items.cn: wela 意为「安好、兴旺、财富」，与表示「好」的词同源。它先描述良好处境，后描述钱财。

items.en: The abstract suffix -th turned wela into welth, the state of being well-off, in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 抽象后缀把 wela 变成 welth，即「富足的状态」，时在中古英语时期。

items.en: By the modern period the material sense of money and property dominated, while the older wellbeing sense survived mainly in compounds and religious language.
items.cn: 到近现代，金钱与财产的物质义占据主导，较古的安好义主要保存在复合词与宗教语言里。

items.en: The phrase a wealth of extended the word from money to any large supply, such as detail, experience or evidence.
items.cn: 「大量的」这一说法把词义从金钱扩展到任何大量供应，如细节、经验或证据。

items.en: Economics fixed wealth as a stock of assets held at a point in time, in contrast with income as a flow.
items.cn: 经济学把财富固定为某一时点的资产存量，与作为流量的收入相对。

items.en: Attestation uncertain (first citation of the material sense): the transition from wellbeing to money is gradual and no single first use is recorded.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定（物质义的）：从安好到金钱的转变是渐进的，没有单一的最早用例。

note.en: Group one separates near neighbours that are often mistaken for relatives; group two holds words for large possessions.
note.cn: 第一组区分常被误认作同族的近邻词；第二组是表示大量财物的词。

entries.definition: Health comes from Old English hælþ 'wholeness' and is related to whole, not to wela; the shared ending is deceptive.
entries.definitionCN: 健康来自古英语 hælþ「完整」，与「完整」一词同源，与财富的词根无关；相同的词尾容易误导。

entries.definition: Welfare joins 'well' with 'fare' meaning journey or condition; it is a separate compound, not a derivative of wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 福利由「好」与「行程、处境」合成，是另一个复合词，并非财富的派生词。

entries.definition: Commonwealth is common plus wealth, naming a political community that shares a common good; it is a relative but not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 联邦由「共同」加「财富」构成，指共享公共之善的政治共同体；它是同族词，却不是同义词。

entries.definition: Weal is the older noun for wellbeing from which wealth was built, and it survives mainly in set phrases.
entries.definitionCN: weal 是构成财富的较古名词，意为安好，主要保留在固定说法里。

entries.definition: Riches is a plural noun for abundant valuable possessions, often used figuratively for richness of experience.
entries.definitionCN: riches 是表示大量贵重财物的复数名词，也常比喻经验的丰富。

entries.definition: Fortune is a very large amount of money owned by one person or family, close to the personal sense of wealth.
entries.definitionCN: fortune 指个人或家庭拥有的大笔钱财，接近财富的个人义。

entries.definition: Assets are the items of value on a balance sheet, the accounting parts from which net wealth is calculated.
entries.definitionCN: 资产是资产负债表上有价值的项目，是计算净财富的会计组成部分。

entries.definition: Affluence stresses a high level of consumption and goods rather than the stock of assets itself.
entries.definitionCN: 富裕强调高水平的消费与商品，而不是资产存量本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real native root, real compounds and real accounting phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族词根、真实的复合词与真实的会计说法。

normal.en: The root meant wellbeing before it meant money, so the older sense still echoes in formal language.
normal.cn: 词根先指安好，后指钱财，因此较古的义项仍在正式语体中回响。

normal.en: The abstract ending turns an adjective of goodness into the state of being well-off.
normal.cn: 抽象后缀把表示「好」的形容词变成「富足的状态」。

normal.en: A wealth of detail and a wealth of money share the same shape: a large supply.
normal.cn: 大量细节与大量金钱形状相同：都是一种充裕的供应。

normal.en: Economics keeps wealth as a stock and income as a flow, and the two should not be swapped.
normal.cn: 经济学把财富当存量、收入当流量，两者不能互换。

normal.en: The older public-good sense survives in the compound for a political community.
normal.cn: 较古的公共之善义保留在指政治共同体的复合词里。

abstract.en: Picture a storehouse where gold, grain and books sit on the same shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一间库房，金条、粮食与书摆在同一层架上。

abstract.en: Picture a river that keeps flowing while a reservoir holds its water still.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河不断流动，而水库把水静静存住。

abstract.en: Picture a society whose common good is written on a shared ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个社会，把公共之善记在一本共同的账上。

examples.en: The country's wealth is concentrated in a few coastal cities.
examples.cn: 这个国家的财富集中在少数沿海城市。

examples.en: She brought a wealth of experience to the negotiation.
examples.cn: 她为谈判带来了丰富的经验。

examples.en: Wealth can grow while wages stay flat, which widens the gap between owners and workers.
examples.cn: 财富可以在工资停滞时增长，从而扩大所有者与劳动者之间的差距。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「围」加「思」——把金条、地契与粮食围起来反复思量，就是财富；联想「围起来的家底」

root: 古英语 wela「安好、兴旺、财富」加抽象后缀构成，属日耳曼语本族词，没有拉丁语来源；其较古义为良好处境，后收窄为钱财与资产，并保留「大量、丰富」的引申义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one store of value: money and assets are added into a net stock, extended to land, to prosperity, to any abundance, to a society's total and finally to the common good.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份价值储存展开：钱财与资产先被加成净值，再扩展到土地、兴旺、任何充裕、社会总量，最后到公共之善。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storehouse holding gold, deeds, grain and books on the same shelves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间库房，金条、地契、粮袋与书都摆在同一层架上。

branches.en: THE STORE: possessions are first counted, then reduced to a net stock.
branches.cn: 储存：财物先被清点，再折算成净存量。

branches.en: THE LAND: value also lies in rivers, forests and minerals.
branches.cn: 土地：价值也藏在河流、森林与矿藏里。

branches.en: THE GOOD STATE: the oldest sense is flourishing life, not coin.
branches.cn: 良好状态：最古老的义项是兴旺的生活，而不是钱币。

branches.en: ABUNDANCE AND AGGREGATE: any large supply, and the whole society's total, share the same shape.
branches.cn: 充裕与总量：任何大量供应与整个社会的总量，形状相同。

branches.en: TIME AND THE COMMON: what is handed down, and what is held in common.
branches.cn: 时间与公共：一边是传下的存量，一边是共同持有的福祉。

intro.en: Wealth and its relatives are native English; no Latin source is involved, so the family is read from Old English alone.
intro.cn: 财富及其同族词是英语本族词，不涉及拉丁语来源，因此这个词族只能从古英语读起。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin entries for this word: the root is Germanic and the suffixes are native or French-influenced.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语条目：词根是日耳曼语，后缀为本族或受法语影响的形式。

items.example: Wealth accumulated over three generations.
items.exampleCN: 财富经三代积累而成。

items.example: The wealthy district built its own school.
items.exampleCN: 这个富裕城区自建了一所学校。

items.example: The coast grew wealthier than the interior.
items.exampleCN: 沿海比内陆更富有。

items.example: The wealthiest families owned most of the land.
items.exampleCN: 最富有的家族拥有大部分土地。

items.example: Wealthiness brought political influence.
items.exampleCN: 富有带来了政治影响。

items.example: Old texts wished the town weal.
items.exampleCN: 古籍祝愿市镇兴旺。

items.example: The commonweal was invoked in the debate.
items.exampleCN: 辩论中援引了公共福祉。

items.example: The scheme worked well for small farms.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划对小农场很有效。

definition_zh: 藻类的；由藻类组成的；藻类造成的
definition_en: relating to, consisting of, or caused by algae
core_image: 浅水池壁上那层滑腻的绿膜，肉眼只看到一片绿色，显微镜下才是一团单细胞生物
scene: 池塘边，几个孩子发现浅水处的石头上覆着一层滑腻的绿膜，老师蹲下来指着水样说，那是微型藻类在迅速繁殖。 A thick algal film had formed on the stones where the water was warm and still.
sceneCN: 这里 algal 指「藻类形成的、藻类的」（第 1 个义项：与藻类相关或由藻类构成）；句意为在温暖静止的浅水处，石头上已经结了一层厚厚的藻膜。

pos.zh: 藻类的；由藻类组成的；由藻类引起的

derivatives.zh: 藻类（alga 的复数，也作集合名）

senses.title: Relating to algae as organisms
senses.titleCN: 与藻类这一生物类群有关
senses.definition: relating to algae, the simple photosynthetic organisms that live in water and damp places
senses.definitionCN: 与藻类有关的；藻类指生活在水中或潮湿处、能进行光合作用的简单生物
senses.example: Algal cells were counted under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 藻细胞在显微镜下被逐一计数。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun alga into an adjective of relation, so algal means 'of algae' before it means anything more specific.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 alga 变成表关系的形容词，因此 algal 的基础义就是「藻的」，其余义项都由此细化。

senses.title: Consisting of a mass of algae
senses.definition: made up of a dense layer or mass of algae
senses.definitionCN: 由密集的藻类层或藻类群体构成的
senses.example: A green algal mat covered the rock at the outflow.
senses.exampleCN: 出水口的岩石上覆着一层绿色的藻席。
senses.why: Because algae often grow as a sheet rather than as separate plants, the adjective came to describe the whole mat, not just its members.
senses.whyCN: 藻类常成片生长而非一株株分立，因此这个形容词也用来描述整片藻席，而不只是其中的个体。

senses.title: Caused by algae
senses.definition: brought about by the growth of algae, especially in water
senses.definitionCN: 由藻类生长所引起，尤指水体中的现象
senses.example: The reservoir turned green during an algal bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 藻华期间水库变成了绿色。
senses.why: Once algae are the cause rather than the subject, the adjective marks origin: the bloom is not algae itself but what their growth produces.
senses.whyCN: 当藻类成为原因而不是主体时，这个形容词标记来源：藻华不是藻本身，而是藻类生长造成的现象。

senses.title: Carrying algal toxins
senses.titleCN: 含藻毒素的；有毒藻产生的
senses.definition: produced by toxic algae and able to harm people or animals that drink the water
senses.definitionCN: 由有毒藻类产生、能危害饮水者或动物的
senses.example: Algal toxins forced the town to switch to bottled water.
senses.exampleCN: 藻毒素迫使全镇改用瓶装水。
senses.why: Public-health writing needed a short label for poisons made by algae, and algal toxin became that fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生写作需要一个简短标签来指藻类产生的毒素，algal toxin 于是成为固定说法。

senses.title: Used as a feedstock
senses.definition: grown or harvested as raw material for fuel, feed or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 作为燃料、饲料或化工原料而养殖或采收的
senses.example: Algal oil is pressed from tanks of cultivated microalgae.
senses.exampleCN: 藻油由培养微藻的槽罐中压榨而来。
senses.why: Industry extended 'of algae' to 'derived from algae', because the material, not the organism, is what the refinery handles.
senses.whyCN: 工业把「藻的」扩展为「从藻得到的」，因为工厂处理的是材料而不是生物体。

senses.title: Living inside a host
senses.definition: describing algae that live within the tissue of a host organism such as a coral
senses.definitionCN: 描述生活在珊瑚等宿主体内的藻类
senses.example: Reef-building corals depend on their algal partners for sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 造礁珊瑚依赖体内的共生藻提供糖分。
senses.why: In symbiosis the algae are no longer free-living, so the adjective signals the partner role rather than a place.
senses.whyCN: 在共生关系中藻类不再自由生活，因此这个形容词标示的是「伙伴角色」而非地点。

senses.title: Preserved in rock
senses.titleCN: 保存在岩层中的藻类遗迹
senses.definition: referring to structures in sedimentary rock that were built by algae
senses.definitionCN: 指沉积岩中由藻类建造的结构
senses.example: Algal limestone records shallow seas of the distant past.
senses.exampleCN: 藻灰岩记录了远古的浅海。
senses.why: Geology keeps the same adjective because the rock is still, literally, made of algal remains.
senses.whyCN: 地质学沿用同一形容词，因为这种岩石确实由藻类遗骸构成。

senses.title: Tasting or smelling of algae
senses.definition: having the earthy, fishy taste or smell associated with algae in water
senses.definitionCN: 带有水中藻类那种土腥、鱼腥的味道或气味
senses.example: The tap water had an algal taste after the warm spell.
senses.exampleCN: 回暖之后，自来水带上了藻味。
senses.why: Water-quality reports speak of algal taste and odour, so the adjective also names a sensory impression rather than an organism.
senses.whyCN: 水质报告常说「藻味与藻腥气」，于是这个形容词也指一种感官印象，而非生物体。

intro.en: Algal is an English adjective built from Latin alga 'seaweed' plus the relational suffix -al; the noun is classical, the adjective is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: algal 是英语形容词，由拉丁 alga「海藻」加表关系的后缀 -al 构成；名词是古典的，形容词是近代形成的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Alga meant 'seaweed, sea wrack'. Its deeper origin is not established; a suggested link to algere 'to be cold' is only a guess, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: alga 意为「海藻、海草」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人把它与 algere「发冷」联系起来，那只是猜测，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Classical Latin already had the adjective algosus 'full of seaweed', which shows the noun was productive long before the English form appeared.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语已有形容词 algosus「长满海藻的」，说明这个名词在英语形式出现之前早就有构词能力。

items.en: From the eighteenth century botanists used algae as a group name, and English took the Latin plural in -ae rather than adding an English -s.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，植物学家用 algae 作类群名，英语直接沿用拉丁语以 -ae 结尾的复数，而不加英语的 -s。

items.en: The adjective algal is recorded from the mid-nineteenth century, first in botanical descriptions and later in water-quality writing.
items.cn: 形容词 algal 自 19 世纪中叶有记录，最初用于植物学描述，后来进入水质研究文字。

items.en: Twentieth-century technology fixed phrases such as algal bloom, algal mat, algal toxin and algal fuel, where the adjective simply labels the source.
items.cn: 20 世纪的技术文献固定了 algal bloom、algal mat、algal toxin、algal fuel 等说法，其中形容词只标示来源。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Latin origin of alga is unsettled, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：alga 在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论，凡为它提出的印欧形式都属重构形式，而非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word and its closest derivatives, which are constantly mixed up; group two holds adjectives from neighbouring habitats that are not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词及其最近派生形式，最易混用；第二组是来自相邻生境的形容词，彼此不能替换。

entries.definition: One alga is a single organism; algal is the adjective made from it, never a plural.
entries.definitionCN: 一个 alga 是单个藻体；algal 是由它构成的形容词，从不用作复数。

entries.definition: The plural of alga and also the informal group name; it is a noun, so it cannot replace algal in front of another noun.
entries.definitionCN: alga 的复数，也作非正式的类群名；它是名词，不能像 algal 那样放在另一个名词前作定语。

entries.definition: Built with -oid 'like', it says something looks like algae without necessarily being algal.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -oid「像」构成，表示某物看起来像藻，但不一定真的属于藻类。

entries.definition: The branch of botany that studies algae; the -logy marks a discipline, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 研究藻类的植物学分支；-logy 标示学科，而非性质。

entries.definition: Describes organisms that drift in open water, algae included; it answers where they live, while algal answers what they are.
entries.definitionCN: 描述在开阔水域漂浮生活的生物，包含藻类；它回答「住在哪里」，algal 回答「是什么」。

entries.definition: Describes life on or near the seabed; an algal mat may be benthic, but the adjective benthic says nothing about algae.
entries.definitionCN: 描述生活在海底或其附近的生物；藻席可以是底栖的，但 benthic 本身与藻类无关。

entries.definition: Covers bacteria and other single-celled organisms as well as algae, so it is broader than algal.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖细菌与其他单细胞生物，也包括藻类，因此比 algal 范围更宽。

entries.definition: Describes the process of using light to make food; many algae are photosynthetic, but the term also covers plants.
entries.definitionCN: 描述利用光能制造养分的过程；许多藻类能进行光合作用，但这个词也涵盖植物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: alga is the noun, -al makes the adjective: algal simply means 'of algae'.
normal.cn: alga 是名词，加 -al 构成形容词：algal 的意思就是「藻的」。

normal.en: The plural is algae, with Latin -ae, but algal never takes a plural ending.
normal.cn: 复数是拉丁式的 algae（-ae 结尾），但 algal 本身没有复数形式。

normal.en: Algology is the study of algae, and algologist is the person who does it.
normal.cn: algology 是藻类学，algologist 是从事藻类研究的人。

normal.en: Algicide kills algae, the way herbicide kills plants and insecticide kills insects.
normal.cn: algicide 杀藻，正如 herbicide 除草、insecticide 杀虫。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the technical senses: algal bloom, algal mat, algal toxin, algal fuel.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承担技术义：藻华、藻席、藻毒素、藻类燃料。

abstract.en: Picture a clear pond going opaque green in a single warm week.
abstract.cn: 想象一池清水在一个温暖的星期里变成不透光的绿。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of pond water holding a whole microscopic forest.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴池水里藏着一整座微观森林。

abstract.en: Picture a limestone cliff that is really a cemetery of algae turned to stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一面石灰岩崖壁，其实是被石化了的藻类墓地。

examples.en: Algal growth in the bay doubled after the fertiliser runoff.
examples.cn: 化肥径流之后，海湾里的藻类生长量翻了一倍。

examples.en: The team measured algal biomass to estimate the bloom's size.
examples.cn: 团队测量藻类生物量以估算藻华的规模。

examples.en: Coral bleached when the algal partners inside it died.
examples.cn: 当体内的共生藻死亡时，珊瑚就白化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: alga 读起来像「阿狗」——水里的藻类多得像狗毛一样糊在石头上；algal 就是「藻的」

root: 拉丁 alga「海藻」+ 英语形容词后缀 -al；alga 的更深来源不确定，与 algere「发冷」的联系只是假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all radiate from one attribute: something is of algae, made of algae, or produced by algae; the uses move from the microscope to the lake, the fuel tank, the coral polyp, the rock layer and finally the tap.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从同一个属性展开：某物属于藻、由藻构成或由藻产生；用法从显微镜走向湖泊、燃料罐、珊瑚虫、岩层，最后走到水龙头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slippery green film on a stone, invisible cells seen as one mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头上那层滑腻的绿膜，看不见的细胞汇成一片。

branches.en: PLAIN ATTRIBUTE: from a microscope count to a taste in tap water, the link is simply 'of algae'.
branches.cn: 单纯属性：从显微镜计数到自来水里的味道，联系都只是「与藻有关」。

branches.en: ONE SHEET: algae grow as a mat, so the adjective names a mass rather than a specimen.
branches.cn: 成片：藻类成席生长，因此形容词指的是一片，而非一个标本。

branches.en: ALGAE AS CAUSE: a bloom and its toxins are results attributed to algae.
branches.cn: 藻为起因：藻华与其毒素都是归因于藻类的结果。

branches.en: ALGAE AS MATERIAL: industry turns the organism into oil, feed and chemicals.
branches.cn: 藻作材料：工业把生物体变成油、饲料与化工品。

branches.en: ALGAE INSIDE SOMETHING ELSE: a partner in coral tissue, a ghost in limestone.
branches.cn: 藻在别物之中：珊瑚组织里的伙伴，石灰岩里的幽灵。

intro.en: Algal can be read as a stem plus one suffix, and the stem itself supports a small family of technical words.
intro.cn: algal 可拆为一个词干加一个后缀，而这个词干本身还支撑着一小族技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin alga 'seaweed' yields alga, algae, algal and algology in English; algosus is the classical adjective built on the same noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 alga「海藻」在英语中衍生 alga、algae、algal 与 algology；algosus 是同一名词构成的古典形容词。

items.example: The singular names one organism.
items.exampleCN: 单数形式指一个藻体。

items.meaning: algae, the group as a whole
items.example: Algae drifted in dense patches.
items.exampleCN: 藻类成片漂浮。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表关系的形容词。

items.example: An algal film covered the stones.
items.exampleCN: 一层藻膜覆盖着石头。

items.example: Algology grew out of nineteenth-century botany.
items.exampleCN: 藻类学从 19 世纪的植物学中发展出来。

items.example: The algologist sampled the kelp bed each spring.
items.exampleCN: 这位藻类学家每年春天都给海藻林取样。

items.example: The pool was treated with an algicide.
items.exampleCN: 泳池用杀藻剂处理过。

items.meaning: a gum extracted from brown algae
items.example: Alginate thickens the ice-cream mix.
items.exampleCN: 藻酸盐使冰淇淋浆料变稠。

items.meaning: a rapid overgrowth of algae in water
items.example: The algal bloom stained the shoreline green.
items.exampleCN: 藻华把岸线染成绿色。

latinEntries.structure: algosus, algosa, algosum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 灌木；灌木丛；（园艺）花灌木；灌木层；果味糖浆饮（旧义，另源）
definition_en: a woody plant smaller than a tree, usually with several stems growing from the base
core_image: 一株不到腰高的木本植物，从同一个基部抽出三根细茎，旁边高树的树干已经枯死
scene: 同一基部抽出三根细茎的矮灌木，在高树枯死的地方仍然活着。 A low shrub with three stems from the same base survived where the taller trees had died.
sceneCN: 这里 shrub 指「低于乔木、通常自基部分出多根茎的木本植物」（第 1 个义项：小型多茎木本植物）；句意为同一基部抽出三根茎的矮灌木，在高树枯死之处存活下来。图中可辨识物件：三根细茎、共同基部、枯死的高树干、裸露地面。

pos.zh: 灌木；灌木丛（可数；集合义不可数）
果味糖浆饮（加醋或酒，18 世纪旧义，词源不同）

forms.label: 形容词（灌木状的；多灌木的）
名词（灌木丛；灌木栽植区）

derivatives.zh: 半灌木（基部木质、上部草质）

senses.title: A small multi-stemmed woody plant
senses.definition: a woody plant that stays low and usually sends up several stems from the same base instead of one trunk
senses.definitionCN: 一种低矮的木本植物，通常自同一基部长出多根茎，而非单一下干
senses.example: A low shrub with three stems from the same base survived the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 同一基部抽出三根茎的矮灌木熬过了干旱。
senses.why: the word's core is lowness plus woodiness: it is not a small tree because it branches at the ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「低矮」加「木质」：它不是小树，因为它在贴地处就分叉。

senses.title: Shrubs planted as a garden mass
senses.titleCN: 庭园中成片栽植的灌木
senses.definition: a group or mass of low woody plants grown together for cover, flowers or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 成片栽植的低矮木本植物，用于遮蔽、观花或作边界
senses.example: The gardener cut the shrub back hard after flowering.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁在花后把这丛灌木重剪了一遍。
senses.why: in garden talk the countable plant and the uncountable mass blur, so 'the shrub' can mean the whole bed.
senses.whyCN: 在园艺口语中，单株与成片混在一起，因此这个说法也可指整片花坛。

senses.title: The botanical growth form
senses.titleCN: 植物学上的灌木生长型
senses.definition: a growth form defined by persistent woody stems branching near ground level and a mature height well below the tree layer
senses.definitionCN: 一种生长型：具宿存木质茎、贴近地面分枝，成熟高度远低于乔木层
senses.example: The flora keys out the shrub by its basal branching, not by its height alone.
senses.exampleCN: 这本植物志以基部分枝、而非单以高度来检索灌木。
senses.why: botany needs a form category between herb and tree, and shrub names exactly that middle.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要一个介于草本与乔木之间的形态类别，shrub 正指这个中间层。

senses.title: A flowering ornamental shrub
senses.definition: a woody plant chosen and pruned mainly for showy flowers or coloured foliage in a garden
senses.definitionCN: 主要因花艳或叶色而在庭园中被选用、修剪的木本植物
senses.example: A pink flowering shrub anchors the corner of the border.
senses.exampleCN: 一株开粉花的灌木压住花坛转角。
senses.why: horticulture shifted the emphasis from wild form to cultivated display, so shrub came to mean a planted ornament.
senses.whyCN: 园艺学把重点从野生形态移到栽培展示，于是 shrub 也指栽下的观赏植物。

senses.title: The shrub layer of a forest
senses.definition: the vertical layer of woody plants between the herb layer and the tree canopy
senses.definitionCN: 位于草本层与乔木树冠之间的木本植物层
senses.example: Deer browsing has stripped the shrub layer from the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿的啃食已把这片林子的灌木层剥光。
senses.why: in ecology a single plant gives its name to a whole stratum, because that layer is made of such plants.
senses.whyCN: 生态学中用单株植物之名指整个层，因为该层正是由这类植物构成。

senses.title: A dryland or scrub shrub
senses.definition: a tough, often thorny or waxy-leaved woody plant that dominates dry scrub and semi-desert
senses.definitionCN: 常带刺或具蜡质叶的耐旱木本植物，在干旱灌丛与半荒漠中占优势
senses.example: Salt-tolerant shrubs line the dry lake bed.
senses.exampleCN: 耐盐灌木沿干涸湖床排成一线。
senses.why: where trees cannot hold, shrubs become the dominant cover, so the word doubles as a landscape label.
senses.whyCN: 在乔木立不住的地方，灌木成为主要覆盖，于是这个词也兼作景观标签。

senses.title: Woody encroachment on open land
senses.definition: the spread of woody plants into grassland or pasture, often seen as degradation
senses.definitionCN: 木本植物向草地或牧场扩张，常被视为退化
senses.example: Unchecked grazing let shrub take over the lower pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧失控让灌木占据了低处牧场。
senses.why: a plant name turns into a process name when the plant's spread changes what the land is.
senses.whyCN: 当某种植物的扩张改变了土地性质，植物名就变成了过程名。

senses.title: The old fruit-syrup drink
senses.titleCN: 旧时的果味糖浆饮（另源）
senses.definition: a drink made from fruit juice, sugar and vinegar or rum, popular in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries
senses.definitionCN: 由果汁、糖与醋或朗姆酒调成的饮品，在 18 至 19 世纪流行
senses.example: A jug of raspberry shrub stood cooling on the sill.
senses.exampleCN: 一罐覆盆子糖浆饮放在窗台上晾凉。
senses.why: this is a homonym, not a development of the plant sense: it comes through Arabic sharab 'a drink'.
senses.whyCN: 这是同形异源词，并非植物义的引申：它经阿拉伯语 sharab「饮料」而来。

intro.en: Shrub 'low woody plant' is a Germanic word of uncertain deeper origin; shrub 'fruit drink' is an unrelated homonym from Arabic.
intro.cn: shrub「低矮木本植物」是日耳曼词，更深来源不确定；shrub「果汁饮」则是来自阿拉伯语的不相关同形词。

items.en: Old English scrybb named brushwood and low woody growth. The form is recorded chiefly in glosses, so its early history is thin.
items.cn: 古英语 scrybb 指柴枝与低矮木本植物。该形式主要见于注释文献，早期历史材料很少。

items.en: The word matches North Frisian skrobb 'brushwood' and West Flemish schrobbe 'climbing vetch', which points to a North Sea Germanic stock.
items.cn: 这个词与北弗里斯兰语 skrobb「柴枝」、西佛兰德语 schrobbe「野豌豆」相合，指向北海日耳曼语来源。

items.en: Middle English shrub kept both the plant and the cut-brushwood readings, and the plant sense gradually dominated.
items.cn: 中古英语 shrub 同时保留「植物」与「砍下的柴枝」两义，后来植物义逐渐占主导。

items.en: The drink shrub entered English in the eighteenth century through Arabic sharab 'a drink' (compare sherbet and syrup), a completely separate line.
items.cn: 指饮品的 shrub 于 18 世纪经阿拉伯语 sharab「饮料」进入英语（参较 sherbet 与 syrup），是完全独立的一线。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): no Germanic etymon beyond the North Sea forms is attested, and the pre-Germanic root is a reconstruction; the first English citation of the plant sense is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：除北海诸语形式外没有更早的日耳曼语书证，其日耳曼语之前的词根属重构；植物义的最早英语书证年代也不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates shrub from its closest woody-plant neighbours; group two separates the vegetation words that are not single plants.
note.cn: 第一组把 shrub 与最接近的木本植物词分开；第二组区分那些指植被而非单株的词。

entries.definition: A general word for a low woody plant, often wild and rounded; shrub is the more technical and garden term.
entries.definitionCN: 低矮木本植物的通称，常指野生、团状者；shrub 更技术化，也更常用于园艺。

entries.definition: Low woody vegetation as a cover type, often stunted or thorny; it rarely names a single plant.
entries.definitionCN: 作为覆盖类型的低矮木本植被，常矮小或多刺；很少指单株植物。

entries.definition: A young tree with a single stem; it differs from a shrub in having one trunk that will grow tall.
entries.definitionCN: 单茎的幼树；与灌木的区别在于只有一根将来会长高的主干。

entries.definition: A plant woody only at the base and herbaceous above, so it dies back partly each winter.
entries.definitionCN: 仅基部木质、上部草质的植物，每年冬季部分枯死。

entries.definition: A planted area of shrubs, usually in a garden or park; it names the bed, not the species.
entries.definitionCN: 庭园或公园中成片栽植的灌木区；指花坛，不指物种。

entries.definition: The low plants growing beneath a forest canopy, including herbs and shrubs; broader than shrub.
entries.definitionCN: 林冠下生长的低矮植物，含草本与灌木；范围比 shrub 宽。

entries.definition: A line of shrubs planted and clipped as a barrier; the shrubs are means, the barrier is the point.
entries.definitionCN: 成行栽植并修剪作屏障的灌木；灌木是手段，屏障才是目的。

entries.definition: A dense stand of shrubs or small trees hard to walk through; it stresses impenetrability.
entries.definitionCN: 难以穿行的密集灌木或小树丛；强调难以通过。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: One base, many stems: that is the difference between a shrub and a tree.
normal.cn: 一个基部、多根茎：这就是灌木与乔木的区别。

normal.en: The family runs shrub, shrubby, shrubbery, shrubland, subshrub.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 shrub、shrubby、shrubbery、shrubland、subshrub。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: flowering shrub, evergreen shrub, shrub layer, desert shrub.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：花灌木、常绿灌木、灌木层、荒漠灌木。

normal.en: Ecology names a whole layer after the plant: the shrub layer.
normal.cn: 生态学以这种植物之名为整层命名：灌木层。

normal.en: The homonym warning: the fruit drink comes from Arabic, not from the plant.
normal.cn: 同形异源提醒：果汁饮来自阿拉伯语，与植物无关。

abstract.en: Think of a hand that never grew one wrist but five fingers straight from the palm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手没有手腕，五根手指直接从掌心长出。

abstract.en: Think of a low wall that keeps growing back after every cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵矮墙，每次被砍后都重新长回。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd of short people holding a tall forest up from below.
abstract.cn: 想象一群矮个子在下面把高处的森林托住。

examples.en: Goats will eat almost any shrub before they touch the grass.
examples.cn: 山羊几乎先吃光任何灌木，才去碰草。

examples.en: The shrub layer recovered two years after the fire.
examples.cn: 火灾两年后灌木层恢复了。

examples.en: A single shrub can anchor a whole dune.
examples.cn: 一株灌木就能固定整座沙丘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「shrub」读音像「刷布」——矮矮一丛，像刷子一样贴地散开 → 灌木

root: 古英语 scrybb「柴枝、低矮木本植物」，与北弗里斯兰语 skrobb、西佛兰德语 schrobbe 同源，属北海日耳曼语一线；更深词根不确定。指饮品的 shrub 另出阿拉伯语 sharab。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plant: it grows low and many-stemmed, fills gardens and forest layers, takes over dry ground, and finally shares its spelling with an unrelated drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一株植物展开：它低矮多茎，填满庭园与森林层次，占据干旱地，最后又与一种无关的饮料共用拼写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one root crown sending up several thin stems instead of a single trunk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个根颈抽出几根细茎，而不是一根主干。

branches.en: FORM: lowness and basal branching define the plant both in common speech and in botany.
branches.cn: 形态：低矮与基部分枝，在日常语与植物学中都定义这种植物。

branches.en: GARDEN: the plant becomes an ornamental mass chosen for flower and boundary.
