branches.cn: 庭园：这种植物成为按花与边界选用的观赏群体。

branches.en: STRATUM: in a wood the same plant gives its name to a whole layer.
branches.cn: 层次：在林中，同一种植物为整个层命名。

branches.en: DRY LAND: where trees fail, shrubs dominate, and their spread can count as degradation.
branches.cn: 旱地：乔木立不住时灌木占优，其扩张可算作退化。

branches.en: HOMONYM: the drink is a separate Arabic loan, so the two meanings must not be linked.
branches.cn: 同形异源：饮料是独立的阿拉伯语借词，两义不可串联。

intro.en: Shrub is a free root that takes several suffixes, producing a compact family of plant and landscape words.
intro.cn: shrub 是自由词根，可接若干后缀，形成一组紧凑的植物与景观词族。

latinIntro.en: Shrub has no Latin ancestor; the only Latin-looking item here, sub-, is a prefix borrowed into English word formation, not evidence of a Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: shrub 没有拉丁语祖先；此处唯一像拉丁语的 sub- 是英语构词借用的前缀，不能当作拉丁词根的证据。

items.example: The shrub regrew from the cut stems.
items.exampleCN: 这株灌木从被砍的茎上重新长出。

items.meaning: like a shrub; full of shrubs
items.example: The shrubby slope holds the soil.
items.exampleCN: 长满灌木的坡地能保住土壤。

items.example: A clipped shrubbery hides the wall.
items.exampleCN: 一片修剪过的灌木丛遮住了墙。

items.example: Shrubland replaced the overgrazed pasture.
items.exampleCN: 灌木林地取代了过牧的牧场。

items.meaning: a plant woody only at the base
items.example: Lavender is often grown as a subshrub.
items.exampleCN: 薰衣草常被当作半灌木栽培。

items.example: The sprayed verge was almost shrubless.
items.exampleCN: 喷过药的路边几乎没有灌木。

items.meaning: where shrubs are the main cover
items.example: A shrub-dominated community followed the fire.
items.exampleCN: 火灾后形成以灌木为主的群落。

items.example: Shrub-steppe supports sagebrush and bunchgrass.
items.exampleCN: 灌木草原上长着山艾与丛生禾草。

definition_zh: 精确；精密度；精确性；（仪器、测量的）精度；有效数字位数；（加工）公差
definition_en: the quality of being exact, especially the fineness of a measurement or the closeness of repeated readings to one another
core_image: 一把薄刃把多余的部分削掉，只留下真正要的那一点
scene: 实验室的台面上摆着一支滴定管、一本记录册和一台电子天平，同一份样品被反复称了五回。 The precision of the balance showed in five readings that differed by less than a milligram.
sceneCN: 这里 precision 指「统计意义上的重复一致性」（第 2 个义项：重复测量的一致程度）；句意：这台天平的精密度体现在五次读数相差不到一毫克。图中可辨识物件：滴定管、记录册、电子天平、样品瓶；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 精确；精密度；精度；精确性

senses.title: The fineness of a stated measurement
senses.titleCN: 测量值本身的精细程度
senses.definition: the degree to which a stated measurement is divided into fine enough steps for two nearby values to be told apart
senses.definitionCN: 一个测量值被细分到多细的程度，即能否把两个接近的值区分开
senses.example: The precision of the reading was limited by the smallest mark on the ruler.
senses.exampleCN: 这个读数的精度受限于尺子上最小的那道刻度。
senses.why: Praecisio is a cutting off, and a finely stated measurement is one cut into narrow slices.
senses.whyCN: praecisio 本义是切去，精细报出的测量值就是把量切成一薄片一薄片。

senses.title: Repeatability across repeated measurements
senses.definition: in statistics, the closeness of repeated measurements to one another, whether or not they sit near the true value
senses.definitionCN: 统计上多次测量彼此接近的程度，与它们是否靠近真值无关
senses.example: The five runs showed high precision even when the average was slightly off.
senses.exampleCN: 五次运行即使平均值略有偏差，重复精密度依然很高。
senses.why: Statistics separates the scatter among repeats, called precision, from the distance to the truth, called accuracy.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把重复测量的分散程度称为精密度，把与真值的距离称为准确度，两者分开。

senses.title: The smallest step an instrument can show
senses.definition: the smallest change in a quantity that an instrument can register, display or resolve
senses.definitionCN: 仪器能够记录、显示或分辨的最小变化量
senses.example: The instrument's precision reaches one part in a million.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器的精度达到百万分之一。
senses.why: An instrument whose scale is cut more finely can separate values that a coarse one merges.
senses.whyCN: 刻度切得更细的仪器，能把粗仪器混在一起的值分开。

senses.title: Exactness in wording
senses.definition: careful exactness in the choice of words, so that a statement admits only one reading
senses.definitionCN: 用词上的细致准确，使一句话只容许一种读法
senses.example: She described the procedure with the precision of a manual.
senses.exampleCN: 她像操作手册一样精确地描述了步骤。
senses.why: Latin praecisio also meant brevity of speech, where every surplus word has been cut away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praecisio 也指言辞简省，即把多余的词都切掉。

senses.title: Targeted action on a small site
senses.titleCN: 精准农业与精准医疗的定点干预
senses.definition: an approach that directs water, treatment or medicine only to the exact field, place or patient that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 只把水、处理或药物投到确切需要的田块、地点或病人身上的做法
senses.example: Precision irrigation delivers water to the driest rows alone.
senses.exampleCN: 精准灌溉只把水送到最干的那几垄。
senses.why: The modern compounds keep the old image of a cut made exactly where it is wanted.
senses.whyCN: 现代复合词保留了老意象：只在需要的地方下刀。

senses.title: The number of reliable digits
senses.definition: the count of digits in a reported value that carry real information about how finely it is known
senses.definitionCN: 一个报告值中携带真实精细信息的数字位数
senses.example: Report the mean to four digits of precision.
senses.exampleCN: 把平均值报到四位有效数字。
senses.why: Digits past the reliable cut are noise, so counting the trustworthy digits states the precision.
senses.whyCN: 可靠切点之后的位只是噪声，数出可信位数就是在说明精度。

senses.title: Machining to a very small tolerance
senses.titleCN: 机械加工的公差与精度
senses.definition: the closeness with which a machined part matches its specified size, measured in very small units
senses.definitionCN: 加工件与规定尺寸吻合的紧密程度，以极小的单位计量
senses.example: The shop grinds bearings to a precision of two microns.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把轴承磨到两微米的精度。
senses.why: In a machine shop the abstract fineness becomes metal cut away until the part fits.
senses.whyCN: 在机加工车间，抽象的精细变成被切掉的金属，直到零件合适。

senses.title: Strict exactness in legal or formal form
senses.titleCN: 法律或形式上的严格精确
senses.definition: the strict following of exact wording or procedure, where no looseness or paraphrase is permitted
senses.definitionCN: 严格遵循确切的措辞或程序，不允许任何松动或改写
senses.example: The clause was drafted with precision to close every loophole.
senses.exampleCN: 这一条款起草得十分精确，堵住了每个漏洞。
senses.why: A legal cut must fall on exactly the right word, which is the original image applied to text.
senses.whyCN: 法律之刀必须落在确切的字上，正是原意象用在文本上。

intro.en: Precision comes from Latin praecisio 'a cutting off', a noun of action from praecidere 'to cut short', built on prae- 'in front' plus caedere 'to cut'. French carried the word into English in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: precision 出自拉丁 praecisio「切去」，是 praecidere「切短」的动作名词，由 prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」构成。英语十六世纪经法语引入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caedere meant 'to cut, to strike down'; it also underlies incision, excise and decision, each of which turns on a cut.
items.cn: caedere 意为「切、砍倒」，也构成 incision、excise 与 decision，这几个词都围绕「切」展开。

items.en: Prae- 'in front' plus caedere made praecidere 'to cut off in front, to shorten'; a speech that was praecisus had its surplus trimmed away.
items.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere 构成 praecidere「切去前面、截短」；被称作 praecisus 的言辞就是把多余部分削掉了。

items.en: Praecisio named the act of cutting off and also brevity of style, so the notion of fine trimming sits inside both senses.
items.cn: praecisio 既指切去的动作，也指文风的简省，因此「削到恰好」的观念同时存在于这两层。

items.en: Middle French precision brought the word into English, first for concise speech and only later for exact measurement.
items.cn: 中古法语 precision 把这个词带进英语，先用于简练的言辞，较晚才用于精确测量。

items.en: Nineteenth-century science and manufacturing applied the word to instrument scales and machined parts, which produced the modern technical senses.
items.cn: 十九世纪的科学与制造业把这个词用到仪器刻度和加工零件上，现代技术义项由此形成。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin praecisio, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact year of its first English use is not recorded. The usual route is through French, while a direct Latin borrowing is also argued; no single route is imposed here.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 praecisio，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的具体年份没有记录。通常认为经法语传入，也有直接借自拉丁语的说法；此处不强行选定单一传入路径。

note.en: Group one is the same Latin family seen through its adjective, adverb and negative forms; group two holds the measuring partners that share the field but answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词族在形容词、副词与否定形式上的样子；第二组是同处测量领域的伙伴词，但它们回答的是另一个问题。

entries.definition: Giving exact details with nothing vague; it describes the thing or the person, while precision names the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 给出确切细节、毫不含糊；它形容事物或人，而 precision 是这种性质本身。

entries.definition: In an exact way, or used as an emphatic 'exactly'; it modifies an action rather than naming a measured degree.
entries.definitionCN: 以确切的方式，或用作加强语气的「正是」；它修饰动作，不指一个测得的程度。

entries.definition: Lack of exactness, formed with the negative prefix im-; it is the direct opposite of precision in every sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不精确，由否定前缀 im- 构成；在各义项上都是 precision 的反面。

entries.definition: A less common synonym for precision, stressing the manner of being exact rather than a measured degree of fineness.
entries.definitionCN: precision 的罕用同义词，强调一丝不苟的作风，而非测得的精细程度。

entries.definition: How near a measurement lies to the true value; a rifle can be accurate while its shots are widely spread.
entries.definitionCN: 测量值与真值的接近程度；一支枪可以很准确，但弹着点散布很广。

entries.definition: The state of being wholly correct, often said of a figure or a copy rather than of a spread of repeats.
entries.definitionCN: 完全正确的状态，常用于数字或副本，而不是重复测量的散布。

entries.definition: The smallest interval an instrument or an image can distinguish; it is the hardware side of precision.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器或图像能分辨的最小间隔；它是精密度在硬件上的表现。

entries.definition: The range of variation a specification allows; precision is the aim, tolerance is the slack accepted around it.
entries.definitionCN: 规格允许的变动范围；precision 是瞄准的目标，tolerance 是允许的松量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin cut, the fine scale and the fixed phrases that keep the word technical.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的「切」、细密的刻度，以及把这个词固定在技术语境里的搭配。

normal.en: Prae- 'before' plus caedere 'to cut': trim off the surplus.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」：把多余的部分削掉。

normal.en: A fine scale cuts a quantity into narrow slices.
normal.cn: 细密的刻度把一个量切成一薄片一薄片。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: precision measurement, precision instrument, precision farming.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：精密测量、精密仪器、精准农业。

normal.en: Statistics keeps precision for repeats and accuracy for the true value.
normal.cn: 统计学用「精密度」说重复，用「准确度」说真值。

normal.en: In a machine shop precision is measured in microns.
normal.cn: 在机加工车间，精度以微米计。

abstract.en: Picture a blade shaving a hair's width off a metal block.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃从金属块上削下一根头发那么薄的一层。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose marks sit closer together than a fingernail.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，刻度线比指甲还窄。

abstract.en: Picture five arrows in one tight cluster, though none of them near the bullseye.
abstract.cn: 想象五支箭扎在同一小簇里，却都不靠近靶心。

examples.en: The survey reported its margin with more precision than the sample size deserved.
examples.cn: 这项调查报出的误差范围，比它的样本量所能支撑的更为精细。

examples.en: Precision alone does not make a scale trustworthy if it was zeroed wrongly.
examples.cn: 如果零点调错了，光有精密度并不能让一台秤可信。

examples.en: Precision medicine matches a drug to the genetic profile of one patient.
examples.cn: 精准医疗把药物匹配到某一位病人的基因特征上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pre（在前）+ cise（切）」——把多余的部分切掉，留下的就是精确

root: 拉丁 praecisio「切去」= praecidere（prae-「在前」+ caedere「切」）的动作名词。同族词有 precise、precisely、preciseness、imprecision。英语经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one cut: a finely stated value, statistical repeatability, an instrument's smallest step, exact wording, targeted action, reliable digits, machining tolerance and strict legal form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一刀：精细报出的测量值、统计上的重复一致性、仪器的最小刻度、确切的措辞、定点干预、可靠位数、加工公差，以及法律形式上的严格精确。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin blade cutting away everything that is not the exact point.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把薄刃削掉一切不属于那一点的部分。

branches.en: FINE DIVISIONS: stating a value in narrow steps and counting the reliable digits are the same cut seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 细分：把值报成窄小的台阶与数出可靠位数，是同一刀的两面。

branches.en: REPEATS AGREE: statistical precision is the spread among repeats, not the distance from the truth.
branches.cn: 重复一致：统计上的精密度是重复测量之间的散布，而不是与真值的距离。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT'S EDGE: a finer scale lets a device separate what a coarse one merges.
branches.cn: 仪器的刃口：刻度更细的装置能把粗装置混在一起的值分开。

branches.en: CLEAN WORDING: exact speech and strict legal form both cut off every second reading.
branches.cn: 干净的措辞：确切的表达与严格的法律形式，都切掉了第二种读法。

branches.en: ACTION AT ONE SPOT: precision farming and precision machining both demand the cut land where the work requires.
branches.cn: 定点下手：精准农业与精密加工都要求这一刀落在工作真正需要的地方。

intro.en: Precision is a Latin noun of action built from a prefix, a verb root and a suffix, and the same pieces also build the everyday adjectives precise and imprecise.
intro.cn: precision 是由前缀、动词词根与后缀构成的拉丁动作名词，同样的构件也造出日常形容词 precise 与 imprecise。

latinIntro.en: Prae- 'in front' plus caedere 'to cut' yields praecidere, and -io turns it into the action noun praecisio; English then adds -ly and -ness and negates the whole word with im-.
latinIntro.cn: prae-「在前」加 caedere「切」得到 praecidere，-io 把它变成动作名词 praecisio；英语再加上 -ly 与 -ness，并用 im- 否定整个词。

items.example: The prefix puts the cutting ahead of the thing cut.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把切割放在被切之物的前面。

items.example: Incision and excise share this verb.
items.exampleCN: incision 与 excise 共用这个动词。

items.example: A long speech could be cut down to a short one.
items.exampleCN: 一段长话可以被截短成几句。

items.example: The Latin noun already carried the idea of trimming to the right size.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已经含有「削到恰好」的意思。

items.example: The word moved from speech to instruments.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从言辞转到了仪器上。

items.example: A precise answer leaves no room for a second reading.
items.exampleCN: 确切的回答不给第二种读法留空间。

items.example: The parts fit precisely together.
items.exampleCN: 这些零件严丝合缝地拼在一起。

items.example: Any imprecision in the clock ruins the timing.
items.exampleCN: 时钟的任何不精确都会毁掉计时。

items.example: An imprecise word can start a quarrel.
items.exampleCN: 一个不准确的词就能引起争吵。

items.example: Her preciseness made the instructions easy to follow.
items.exampleCN: 她的一丝不苟让说明容易照着做。

definition_zh: 参与式的；让人参与的；参与性民主的；参与式管理的；参与式研究的；参与式艺术的；参与式预算的；参与式体育的；参与式文化的
definition_en: organized so that members of a group take part in decisions, activities, or creation, rather than receiving them from above or watching them from outside
core_image: 圈子的门敞开着，里面的人都能伸手去改正在用的规则
scene: 社区花园不请设计师画定稿，而是让每户居民投票决定哪块地种什么。 Every household votes on what to plant, so the planning is participatory.
sceneCN: 这里 participatory 是「参与式的」（第 1 个义项：决策由成员共同做出，而非由上方定好）；句意：每户居民投票决定种什么，所以这种规划是参与式的。

pos.zh: 参与式的；让人参与的；共同参与的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 参与性的（更强调共同决策特征）

senses.title: Decisions made with the members
senses.titleCN: 由成员共同作出决定的
senses.definition: describing a process in which the people affected take part in making the decision rather than receiving it from above
senses.definitionCN: 指受影响的人参与作出决定、而不是从上方接受决定的流程
senses.example: The housing council adopted a participatory model for allocating flats.
senses.exampleCN: 住房委员会采用参与式模式分配住房。
senses.why: The suffix -ory means 'serving to' or 'having the function of'. Participatory marks a system whose function is to let feet enter the circle and move the pattern.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ory 意为“起……作用的”。participatory 标记的是一种制度，它的功能就是让脚踏进圈子并改变图案。

senses.title: Open to anyone affected
senses.definition: open in structure, so that outsiders and ordinary members can join, speak, and influence the outcome
senses.definitionCN: 结构上是开放的，外人与普通成员都能加入、发言并影响结果
senses.example: The planning meeting was unusually participatory for a city office.
senses.exampleCN: 对市政部门而言，这次规划会议开放得不同寻常。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes the door, not the decision. A participatory forum is one whose walls are low enough that a passer-by can lean in.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词描述的是门，而不是决定。参与式论坛的墙足够低，路过的人也能探身进来。

senses.title: Of participatory democracy
senses.definition: relating to a model of democracy in which citizens take part directly in decisions, not only in periodic elections
senses.definitionCN: 指公民直接参与决策、而不只在定期选举中投票的民主模式
senses.example: Participatory democracy requires time that representative systems do not.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式民主需要代议制所不需要的时间。
senses.why: The circle is the polity. Where representative democracy asks citizens to choose who decides, this model asks them to sit in the circle themselves, so the word becomes a political label.
senses.whyCN: 这时的圈子是政治共同体。代议制民主请公民选择由谁决定，这种模式则请公民自己坐进圈里，于是这个词成了一个政治标签。

senses.title: Of shared management
senses.definition: relating to management in which employees help set goals, solve problems, and shape working rules
senses.definitionCN: 指员工参与设定目标、解决问题并制定工作规则的管理方式
senses.example: Participatory management failed here because no one owned the final call.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式管理在这里失败了，因为没有人对最终决定负责。
senses.why: A factory floor is also a circle. The adjective turns the org chart sideways: the boxes at the bottom are given lines back up into the decision.
senses.whyCN: 车间也是一个圈子。这个形容词把架构图横过来：底部的方框获得了指回决策的连线。

senses.title: Of research done with participants
senses.titleCN: 与参与者共同做的研究
senses.definition: relating to research in which the people studied help design the questions, collect data, and interpret results
senses.definitionCN: 指被研究者参与设计问题、收集数据与解释结果的研究方式
senses.example: Participatory research gave the village a say in what counted as success.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式研究让村民对“什么算成功”有了发言权。
senses.why: Researchers once stood outside the circle and measured it. This sense puts them inside, so the people being studied become co-authors of the finding.
senses.whyCN: 研究者从前站在圈外测量圈子。这个义项把他们放进圈内，于是被研究的人成了研究结论的共同作者。

senses.title: Of art that needs the audience
senses.definition: relating to art whose meaning or existence depends on the audience doing something, not only looking
senses.definitionCN: 指意义或存在依赖观众动手做事、而不只是观看的艺术
senses.example: The participatory installation asked visitors to write on the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 这件参与式装置请参观者在墙上写字。
senses.why: A painting can be finished by the artist. A participatory work is unfinished until a foot enters the circle, which makes the viewer a material of the piece.
senses.whyCN: 一幅画可以由艺术家完成。参与式作品在有人踏进圈子之前都未完成，这使观众成了作品的材料。

senses.title: Of budgeting by residents
senses.definition: relating to a budget process in which residents decide how part of a public budget is spent
senses.definitionCN: 指由居民决定部分公共预算如何使用的预算流程
senses.example: Participatory budgeting moved the playground repair to the top of the list.
senses.exampleCN: 参与式预算把操场维修提到了清单最前面。
senses.why: Money is the clearest test of the open door. If residents can move a real sum, the participation is not a consultation but a hand on the lever.
senses.whyCN: 钱是检验门是否敞开的最清楚方式。如果居民能挪动一笔真实的款项，参与就不是征询意见，而是手真的握上了操纵杆。

senses.title: Of sport played, not watched
senses.titleCN: 亲自参与而非观看的体育
senses.definition: relating to sport that people play themselves, as opposed to professional sport watched by spectators
senses.definitionCN: 指人们亲自从事的体育运动，相对于观众观看的职业赛事
senses.example: Funding shifted from stadiums to participatory sport in schools.
senses.exampleCN: 资金从体育场转向了学校的参与性体育。
senses.why: Here the contrast is between feet in the circle and eyes outside it. The word classifies an activity by who is doing it, not by how organized it is.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对比是圈里的脚与圈外的眼。这个词按“谁在做”来分类活动，而不是按组织程度。

senses.title: Of a culture that remakes its content
senses.titleCN: 会改写自身内容的文化
senses.definition: relating to a culture in which fans and users produce, remix, and circulate content rather than only consuming it
senses.definitionCN: 指粉丝与用户生产、混编并传播内容、而不只是消费内容的文化
senses.example: Fan translation is a participatory culture in its purest form.
senses.exampleCN: 粉丝翻译是参与式文化最纯粹的形式。
senses.why: The suffix now attaches to culture itself. When readers become writers, the circle stops having a clear outside, and the adjective marks that blurred boundary.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀现在挂到了文化本身上。当读者变成作者，圈子不再有清楚的外面，这个形容词标记的正是那条模糊的边界。

intro.en: Participatory is the adjective of participate, formed with -ory from Latin -orius, a suffix meaning 'serving for, having the function of'. The base is Latin participare, from particeps 'part-taking', itself pars 'part' plus capere 'take'. English built the adjective in the 19th century; it first described political arrangements and later spread to management, research, art, and digital culture.
intro.cn: participatory 是 participate 的形容词，由 -ory（拉丁 -orius，意为“用于……的、具有……功能的”）构成。基础是拉丁语 participare，出自 particeps“拿取一份的”，而 particeps 又是 pars“部分”加 capere“拿取”。英语在 19 世纪造出这个形容词，最初描述政治安排，后来扩展到管理、研究、艺术与数字文化。

items.en: The suffix -orius in Latin forms adjectives of function, as in amatorius 'serving for love' and obligatorius 'binding'. English -ory keeps that sense of 'designed to do this'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 -orius 构成表功能的形容词，如 amatorius“用于爱的”、obligatorius“有约束力的”。英语 -ory 保留了“被设计来做这件事”的含义。

items.en: The adjective appears in English in the 19th century, mainly in political writing about schemes in which citizens share in government.
items.cn: 这个形容词在 19 世纪进入英语，主要用于讨论公民共同参与治理的政治写作。

items.en: Management theory, development practice, and adult education all adopt it: participatory management, participatory research, participatory rural appraisal.
items.cn: 管理学、发展实践与成人教育都采用了它：参与式管理、参与式研究、参与式农村评估。

items.en: Participatory democracy becomes a slogan of student and civic movements, fixing the word as a positive political label.
items.cn: 20 世纪 60 至 70 年代，参与式民主成为学生运动与公民运动的口号，使这个词固定为一个正面的政治标签。

items.en: Media studies apply it to fan production and online platforms: participatory culture, participatory media. The suffix now marks a blurring line between producer and audience.
items.cn: 20 世纪 90 年代至 2000 年代，媒介研究把它用于粉丝生产与网络平台：参与式文化、参与式媒介。这个后缀此时标记的是生产者与受众之间正在模糊的界线。

items.en: The -ory here is not the -ory of 'laboratory' (a place) or the -ory of 'sensory' (belonging to). It is the function suffix: a participatory system is one whose function is participation.
items.cn: 这里的 -ory 不是 laboratory（地点）的 -ory，也不是 sensory（属于）的 -ory，而是表功能的后缀：参与式制度的功用就是“参与”。

note.en: The first group follows the particip- family and marks the near neighbour that only shares the suffix. The second group compares adjectives for things opened to members, to the public, to collaborators, or to users.
note.cn: 第一组沿着 particip- 词族，并标出一个只是共享后缀的近邻。第二组比较表示“对成员开放”“对公众开放”“协作的”“动手的”几个形容词。

entries.definition: to take part in something. The adjective participatory adds -ory to describe a system built to make this happen.
entries.definitionCN: 参加某事。形容词 participatory 加 -ory，用来描述一个被设计成让这种事发生的体系。

entries.definition: the act or share of taking part. It names what happens, while participatory names the design that invites it.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的行为或份额。它命名发生的事，而 participatory 命名邀请这件事发生的设计。

entries.definition: a person who takes part. It is a countable role, whereas participatory is a property of a process.
entries.definitionCN: 参与的人。它是可数的角色，而 participatory 是流程的属性。

entries.definition: relating to a participle. It looks close to participatory but belongs to grammar, not to decision-making.
entries.definitionCN: 与分词有关的。它看起来接近 participatory，却属于语法领域，与决策无关。

entries.definition: deliberately taking in all groups, especially those usually excluded. It stresses who is admitted, while participatory stresses what they do once admitted.
entries.definitionCN: 有意把一切群体纳入，尤其是不常被纳入的群体。它强调谁被接纳，而 participatory 强调被接纳后他们做了什么。

entries.definition: based on the principle that power belongs to the people, usually through voting. It is the wider constitutional idea; participatory names one method of realizing it.
entries.definitionCN: 基于权力属于人民的原则，通常通过投票实现。它是更宽的宪制理念，participatory 是实现它的一种方法。

entries.definition: involving two or more parties working jointly on a task. It stresses joint labour, while participatory stresses shared authority over decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 由两方或多方共同完成一项任务。它强调共同劳动，而 participatory 强调决策权的共享。

entries.definition: involving direct practical activity. It describes the mode of work, not the distribution of decision-making power.
entries.definitionCN: 涉及直接的实践活动。它描述工作方式，而不描述决策权的分配。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: -ory as a function suffix, participare, particeps, the 19th-century political origin, and the four -ory words that are not this -ory.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：-ory 作功能后缀、participare、particeps、19 世纪的政治来源，以及四个不属于这个 -ory 的词。

normal.en: -ory means 'serving to': a participatory system is a system whose job is to let people take part.
normal.cn: -ory 意为“用于……”：参与式体系就是一个以让人参与为职责的体系。

normal.en: The base is particeps, 'part-taker': participatory design gives every member a part to take.
normal.cn: 基础是 particeps“拿取一份的人”：参与式设计给每个成员一份可以拿的东西。

normal.en: The word rose in 19th-century political writing about citizens sharing in government, then moved into offices, clinics, and studios.
normal.cn: 这个词兴起于 19 世纪关于公民共同治理的政治写作，之后进入办公室、诊所与工作室。

normal.en: Do not confuse -ory here with the -ory of laboratory (a place) or sensory (belonging to): this one says 'designed for'.
normal.cn: 不要把这里的 -ory 与 laboratory（地点）或 sensory（属于）的 -ory 混同：这里是“为……而设计”。

normal.en: Participatory democracy, management, research, art, and culture are five arenas where the same open door is installed.
normal.cn: 参与式民主、管理、研究、艺术与文化，是同一扇敞开的门被装进去的五个场所。

abstract.en: A door that is open is not the same as a room that is shared; the adjective names the hinge, not the furniture.
abstract.cn: 门开着不等于房间被共享；这个形容词命名的是合页，而不是家具。

abstract.en: A rule written by everyone is slower to finish and harder to overturn.
abstract.cn: 由所有人写成的规则完成得更慢，也更难被推翻。

abstract.en: When the audience holds the brush, the painting no longer has an outside.
abstract.cn: 当观众握住画笔，这幅画就不再有一个“外面”。

examples.en: The school adopted a participatory approach to curriculum design.
examples.cn: 学校在课程设计上采用了参与式方法。

examples.en: Participatory budgeting gave residents control over a fifth of the budget.
examples.cn: 参与式预算让居民掌控了五分之一的预算。

examples.en: The exhibition is participatory: visitors build part of the work.
examples.cn: 这场展览是参与式的：参观者会搭建作品的一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「帕提西破特瑞」——帕提把门推开，让圈里每个人都“破”例伸手改规则 → participatory 参与式的；让人参与的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 participare「分享、参与」，出自 particeps「拿取一份的人」（pars「部分」+ capere「拿取」）；后缀 -ory（拉丁 -orius）表功能，意为“用于……的”。核心是「把圈子的门敞开，让成员的手伸进规则里」。同族含 participate、participation、participant；perception 共享 capere 但前缀不同。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of participatory all describe an open door in a circle. What changes is the circle — a council, a workplace, a research team, a gallery, a budget, a playing field, or a fandom — and whether the adjective describes the decision, the openness, or the culture.
sensesIntro.cn: participatory 的九个义项都描述圈子上的一扇敞开的门。变化的是圈子本身——议事会、工作场所、研究团队、美术馆、预算、球场或粉丝社群——以及形容词描述的是决定、开放程度，还是文化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle whose door is open, so that members can reach in and change the rules while they are being used.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个门敞开的圈子，成员可以在规则还在使用时伸手进去修改。

chain: THE DESIGN IS NAMED FOR THIS

branches.en: THE OPEN PROCESS: decisions made with members, and a structure open to anyone affected.
branches.cn: 开放的流程：与成员共同作出决定，以及向所有受影响者开放的结构。

branches.en: GOVERNANCE AND WORK: participatory democracy in the polity, participatory management at the workplace.
branches.cn: 治理与工作：政治共同体中的参与式民主，工作场所中的参与式管理。

branches.en: KNOWLEDGE: research in which the studied help design the questions and read the results.
branches.cn: 知识：由被研究者参与设计问题与解读结果的研究。

branches.en: CULTURE AND MONEY: art that needs the audience to act, and budgets that residents can move.
branches.cn: 文化与金钱：需要观众行动的艺术，以及居民可以挪动的预算。

branches.en: PLAY AND PRODUCTION: sport played rather than watched, and a culture that remakes its own content.
branches.cn: 游戏与生产：亲自从事而非观看的体育，以及会改写自身内容的文化。

intro.en: Participatory is participate plus -ory, from Latin -orius. The stem is participat-, from participare, which rests on particeps (pars 'part' + capere 'take'). The adjective is a 19th-century English formation; the Latin language had no participatory.
intro.cn: participatory 是 participate 加 -ory（拉丁 -orius）。词干是 participat-，出自 participare，其基础为 particeps（pars“部分”+ capere“拿取”）。这个形容词是 19 世纪英语的构词，拉丁语本身并没有 participatory。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is pars 'part', capere 'take', particeps 'part-taker', participare 'to share'. Latin -orius formed adjectives of function, the source of English -ory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 pars“部分”、capere“拿取”、particeps“拿取一份的人”、participare“分享”。拉丁 -orius 构成表功能的形容词，是英语 -ory 的来源。

items.meaning: designed so that people take part
items.meaningCN: 被设计成让人参与的（-ory 功能形容词）
items.example: The workshop used a participatory method.
items.exampleCN: 工作坊采用了参与式方法。

items.example: All residents may participate.
items.exampleCN: 所有居民都可以参与。

items.meaning: the act or share of taking part
items.meaningCN: 参与的行为或份额（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Participation was higher than expected.
items.exampleCN: 参与程度高于预期。

items.example: Every participant signed the form.
items.exampleCN: 每位参与者都签了表。

items.meaningCN: 以共同决策为特征的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: The team prefers a participative style.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队偏好参与性的风格。

items.example: He was a silent participator in the debate.
items.exampleCN: 他是这场辩论中沉默的参加者。

items.meaning: a piece of a whole, or a share
items.example: Each part has its own label.
items.exampleCN: 每一部分都有自己的标签。

items.structure: Old French parçonier, from Latin partitionem
items.meaning: one who shares an activity or business
items.meaningCN: 共同从事活动或经营的人；伙伴
items.example: The two firms became partners in 2010.
items.exampleCN: 这两家公司在 2010 年成为合作伙伴。

items.meaning: a taking in through the senses
items.example: Depth perception develops early in infancy.
items.exampleCN: 深度知觉在婴儿期很早就发展起来。

latinEntries.meaning: serving for, having the function of

definition_zh: 发展过程；开发流程（事物从早期形态逐步推进到成形或成熟的一连串阶段）
definition_en: the sequence of stages through which something grows, is built, or is brought to a finished form
core_image: 一面长墙上钉着排成一列的图纸，从潦草草图、分解图到能开动的样机，每一格都按着一枚进度图钉
scene: 实验室的长墙上钉着一排图纸，从最初的潦草草图一直排到成型的样机。 The development process moved from a rough sketch to a working prototype in eighteen months.
sceneCN: 这里指「事物从早期形态逐步推进到成形的连续阶段」（第 1 个义项：从初步构想到成形的整体推进过程）；句意为这一推进过程在十八个月里从粗草图走到了能运转的原型。可辨识物件：长墙、图纸、进度图钉、样机。

pos.zh: 发展过程；开发流程（可数）

collocations.phrase: the development process of a vaccine

senses.title: Growth from an early to a mature state
senses.titleCN: 从初期到成熟的整体生长过程
senses.definition: the whole sequence by which something grows from an early condition to a mature one
senses.definitionCN: 事物从早期状态走向成熟状态的全过程
senses.example: The development process of a coral reef spans centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁的生长过程跨越数百年。
senses.why: development began as the act of unfolding something rolled up, so the word naturally names a thing opening out over time.
senses.whyCN: 发展一词本指把卷起之物摊开，因此天然用来指事物随时间展开。

senses.title: The staged work of making a product
senses.titleCN: 制造产品时按阶段推进的工作
senses.definition: the ordered stages of designing, building and testing a new product before it reaches users
senses.definitionCN: 新产品在交付使用之前，依次经历设计、制造与测试的有序阶段
senses.example: The engineers shortened the development process by testing parts earlier.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师提前测试部件，从而缩短了产品开发流程。
senses.why: once industry needed a word for work that unfolds in steps, the older idea of unfolding was applied to factories.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要指称按步骤展开的工作，于是「展开」的旧义被移用到厂房里。

senses.title: The lifecycle of a piece of software
senses.titleCN: 软件从需求到维护的完整生命周期
senses.definition: the cycle of specifying, coding, testing, releasing and maintaining a program
senses.definitionCN: 程序从确定需求、编写代码、测试、发布到维护的循环
senses.example: Their development process includes a review before every release.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的开发流程在每次发布前都包含一次评审。
senses.why: software projects made the stages explicit and repeatable, so the phrase became a technical label.
senses.whyCN: 软件项目把各阶段明确化、可重复化，这个短语于是成了技术标签。

senses.title: Structural change in an economy or region
senses.titleCN: 经济或地区长期的结构性变化
senses.definition: the long sequence of changes by which an economy, city or region alters its structure
senses.definitionCN: 经济、城市或地区改变自身结构的长期变化序列
senses.example: Road building was one step in the region's development process.
senses.exampleCN: 修路是这个地区发展过程中的一步。
senses.why: economists borrowed the word because a region is said to grow much as a living thing does.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家借用了这个词，因为一个地区也被说成像生物那样生长。

senses.title: A child's course of maturing
senses.definition: the course through which a child's body, speech and understanding mature
senses.definitionCN: 儿童的身体、语言与理解力逐步成熟的历程
senses.example: Teachers record each child's development process in a portfolio.
senses.exampleCN: 教师用成长档案记录每个孩子的发展过程。
senses.why: psychology kept the biological reading of unfolding and applied it to the mind.
senses.whyCN: 心理学保留了「展开」的生物学含义，并把它用于心智。

senses.title: The steps by which a plan is worked out
senses.titleCN: 计划或协议逐步成形所经过的步骤
senses.definition: the series of talks and revisions through which a plan or agreement takes shape
senses.definitionCN: 计划或协议通过一连串商谈与修改而逐步成形
senses.example: The peace talks were a slow development process with many drafts.
senses.exampleCN: 和平谈判是一个经过许多草案的缓慢推进过程。
senses.why: the phrase extends the factory image to any piece of work that is built rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把工厂图景扩展到一切需要「做出来」而非「现成得到」的工作。

senses.title: A repeating cycle of drafting and revision
senses.titleCN: 起草、试用、修改的反复循环
senses.definition: a loop in which a draft is tried, criticized and improved until it is accepted
senses.definitionCN: 草稿经过试用、批评与改进直到被接受的循环
senses.example: The handbook went through three rounds of the development process.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册经历了三轮反复修改的流程。
senses.why: modern design treats the process as a loop rather than a line, which the phrase easily accommodates.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计把过程看成循环而非直线，这个短语正好容纳这种理解。

senses.title: Building the capacity of an organization
senses.titleCN: 组织逐步建立规则与能力的过程
senses.definition: the staged work of giving an organization the rules, staff and habits it needs to last
senses.definitionCN: 让一个组织获得长期存续所需的规则、人员与习惯的分阶段工作
senses.example: Donors funded the development process of the local health office.
senses.exampleCN: 捐助方资助了当地卫生机构的建设过程。
senses.why: development aid made the word common for institutions, not only for things.
senses.whyCN: 发展援助使这个词不只用于物件，也用于机构建设。

intro.en: Development process joins development, from Old French desveloper 'to unwrap, unfurl', and process, from Latin processus 'a going forward'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词由表「发展」与表「过程」的两个名词组合而成：前者出自古法语 desveloper「解开、展开」，后者出自拉丁 processus「向前行进」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Desveloper meant 'to unwrap, unfurl, disclose'. It was built with a negative prefix plus a verb probably meaning 'to wrap', and that second element is the uncertain part.
items.cn: desveloper 意为「解开、展开、显露」，由否定前缀加一个大概意为「包裹」的动词构成，不确定的正是后一部分。

items.en: Processus 'a going forward, advance' came from procedere, pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'to go, to yield'.
items.cn: processus「向前行进、推进」出自 procedere，即 pro-「向前」加 cedere「走、让」。

items.en: English took process in the fourteenth century and development in the sixteenth, at first meaning the act of unfolding or disclosing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入「过程」一词，十六世纪借入「发展」一词，后者最初指展开或显露的动作。

items.en: From the nineteenth century development was applied to land, resources and industry, where growth is planned rather than natural.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，「发展」一词被用于土地、资源与工业，那里的成长是被规划的而非自然的。

items.en: The two nouns were joined in the twentieth century, when project management needed a name for work that advances in ordered stages.
items.cn: 两个名词在二十世纪合为一体，当时项目管理需要一个名称来指按有序阶段推进的工作。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-French origin of the 'wrap' element is not established, and any Frankish or Germanic form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「包裹」的成分在法语之前的来源未获证明，凡为其提出的法兰克或日耳曼语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same stems that are easily mistaken; group two holds near neighbours that name a sequence without naming growth.
note.cn: 第一组是由同一词干构成、容易看错的词；第二组是语义相近、但只说顺序不说生长的词。

entries.definition: Names growth or the built result; it lacks the explicit step-by-step frame that the full phrase supplies.
entries.definitionCN: 单指生长或建设成果，缺少完整短语所提供的分步框架。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to grow or to build up; the process is what the verb produces over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指生长或逐步建成的动词；过程正是这个动词随时间产生的产物。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'relating to development', common in biology and psychology, not a synonym of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与发育有关的」形容词，常用于生物学与心理学，并非该短语的同义词。

entries.definition: Names the person or company that carries out building work, so it is an agent rather than a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施建设的人或公司，是施动者而不是一个序列。

entries.definition: A prescribed order for doing something; it stresses rules, while the phrase stresses growth.
entries.definitionCN: 指办事的规定顺序，强调规则，而该短语强调生长。

entries.definition: The full span from birth or launch to end; it is close but usually names a closed loop.
entries.definitionCN: 指从诞生或推出到终结的全程，意思接近，但通常指闭合循环。

entries.definition: A forward movement through stages, without implying that the thing itself is being built.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐阶段向前推进，不含「事物本身被建造」的意思。

entries.definition: Slow change over a long time, often without a planner; the phrase usually implies deliberate work.
entries.definitionCN: 指长时间内的缓慢变化，常无规划者；该短语通常含有刻意推动之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two real nouns sit inside the phrase: one for growth, one for a forward march.
normal.cn: 短语里含两个真实名词：一个表生长，一个表向前推进。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: product development, software development.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：产品开发、软件开发。

normal.en: The family runs develop, developer, developmental, developmentally.
normal.cn: 同族包括「发展」「开发者」「发育的」「在发育方面」。

normal.en: The second noun shares its root with proceed and procedure.
normal.cn: 第二个名词与「继续进行」「程序」共享同一词根。

normal.en: A wall chart with dated pins is the clearest picture of the phrase.
normal.cn: 钉着日期图钉的墙面进度图，是这个短语最清楚的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a rolled carpet slowly opened across a floor, room by room.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷地毯在地板上慢慢展开，一个房间接一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that must pass through soil, shoot and leaf before it is a plant.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子必须经过土、芽、叶，才成为一株植物。

abstract.en: Picture a relay race where each runner may not start before the last hand-off.
abstract.cn: 想象一场接力赛，每一棒都必须等上一棒交完才能起跑。

examples.en: The development process for the new battery took four years and three prototypes.
examples.cn: 新电池的开发过程历时四年，做了三台原型。

examples.en: Reviewers are invited into the development process before the design is frozen.
examples.cn: 评审者会在设计定稿之前被引入开发流程。

examples.en: A region's development process rarely follows a single straight line.
examples.cn: 一个地区的发展过程很少沿着一条直线走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「底外乐普门特」加「破塞斯」——底下外面都乐着进门，一步一步把东西做出来。

root: development 出自古法语 desveloper「展开」，其表「包裹」的成分来源不确定；process 出自拉丁 processus「向前行进」，由 pro-「向前」与 cedere「走」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: something is opened out step by step, and the same shape is then given to products, software, economies, children, plans, repeated drafts and organizations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：某物被一步一步摊开，这个形状随后被赋予产品、软件、经济、儿童、计划、反复草稿与组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall chart whose dated pins march from a rough sketch to a finished machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张墙面进度图，日期图钉从潦草草图一路排到成型的机器。

branches.en: GROWTH ITSELF: the phrase first names a thing opening out over time, with no factory in sight.
branches.cn: 生长本身：这个短语先指事物随时间展开，画面里还没有工厂。

branches.en: MAKING THINGS: product work and software work turn the sequence into a managed pipeline.
branches.cn: 制造物件：产品工作与软件工作把序列变成可管理的流水线。

branches.en: WHOLE REGIONS: an economy or city is said to grow the way a living body grows.
branches.cn: 整片地区：经济或城市被说成像生物体那样生长。

branches.en: MINDS AND PLANS: a child and a draft both move forward by steps that can be observed.
branches.cn: 心智与计划：孩子与草稿都按可观察的步骤向前。

branches.en: LOOPS AND BODIES: revision repeats the steps, and an organization acquires them as habits.
branches.cn: 循环与机构：修改让步骤重复，而一个组织把步骤沉淀为习惯。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two ordinary English nouns, so its parts can be read through the prefixes and roots that also build a large family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个普通英语名词构成，其各部分可通过同样构成一大族词的前缀与词根来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin cedere 'to go, yield' supplies proceed, procedure and process; the first noun goes back to a French verb whose second element is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cedere「走、让」衍生出「继续进行」「程序」与「过程」；第一个名词则上溯到一个法语动词，其后一成分来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix turns a wrapping action into an unwrapping one.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「包裹」的动作变成「解开」。

items.example: Its origin is not established, so no older form can be quoted as fact.
items.exampleCN: 其来源未获证明，因此不能把任何更早的形式当作事实引用。

items.example: The team developed the sensor over three winters.
items.exampleCN: 团队用了三个冬天研发出这个传感器。

items.example: Housing development changed the edge of the town.
items.exampleCN: 住宅建设改变了小镇的边缘。

items.example: The clinic tracks developmental milestones.
items.exampleCN: 诊所追踪发育里程碑。

items.meaning: a person or firm that builds
items.example: The developer kept the old trees on the site.
items.exampleCN: 开发商保留了地块上的老树。

items.example: The process takes six working days.
items.exampleCN: 这个流程需要六个工作日。

items.example: Work proceeded in stages after the permit.
items.exampleCN: 拿到许可后，工程分阶段推进。

definition_zh: 知觉的；感知的；感官层面的；知觉心理学的；与概念相对的；视觉感知的；言语感知的；知觉障碍的；知觉阶段的
definition_en: relating to perception, to the way the senses take in and organize information, as opposed to abstract reasoning or conceptual thought
core_image: 地图的绘制方式本身，而不是地图上写着的那些地名
scene: 同一张格子图，有人先看见整体轮廓，有人先数清小方块。 One sees the whole shape first, the other counts the squares: this is a perceptual difference.
sceneCN: 这里 perceptual 是「知觉层面的」（第 1 个义项：与感官如何接收并组织信息有关）；句意：有人先看见整体轮廓、有人先数清小方块，这是知觉层面的差异。

pos.zh: 知觉的；感知的；感官层面的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Of the perceiving process
senses.definition: relating to perception as a process, especially how sensory information is received, selected, and organized
senses.definitionCN: 与知觉这一过程有关，尤指感官信息如何被接收、筛选与组织
senses.example: Perceptual processing begins before conscious attention arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉加工在有意识的注意到来之前就开始了。
senses.why: Percept- is the thing taken in, and -ual (Latin -alis) means 'belonging to'. Perceptual therefore names the belonging: not the object seen, but the way it is taken in.
senses.whyCN: percept- 是被拿进来之物，-ual（拉丁 -alis）意为“属于……的”。所以 perceptual 命名的是这种归属：不是被看见的对象，而是看见它的方式。

senses.title: Of the senses rather than the mind
senses.definition: relating to sensory experience as distinct from reasoning, memory, or abstract thought
senses.definitionCN: 与感官经验有关，以区别于推理、记忆或抽象思维
senses.example: The task measured perceptual speed, not verbal reasoning.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务测量的是知觉速度，而不是言语推理。
senses.why: The word draws a line down the mind: on one side sit the senses with their maps, on the other the concepts built from them. Perceptual marks the first side.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在心灵中划下一道线：一边是感官和它们的地图，另一边是由此建起的概念。perceptual 标记的是前一边。

senses.title: Contrasted with conceptual
senses.definition: describing information that comes through the senses, as opposed to information organized by categories and definitions
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过感官而来的信息，相对于按类别与定义组织的信息
senses.example: Infants begin with perceptual categories before they form concepts.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿先有知觉类别，之后才形成概念。
senses.why: A concept is taken together and held still; a percept is taken in and kept moving. The adjective marks the difference between the map as drawn and the map as reasoned about.
senses.whyCN: 概念是被聚在一起并固定住的东西，而知觉对象是被拿进来且仍在变动的东西。这个形容词标记的就是“画出来的地图”与“对地图进行推理”之间的差别。

senses.title: Of the psychology of perception
senses.definition: relating to the branch of psychology that studies how organisms detect patterns, depth, colour, and motion
senses.definitionCN: 属于心理学中研究生物如何辨别图案、深度、颜色与运动的分支
senses.example: Perceptual psychology explains why the lines seem to bend.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉心理学解释了这些线条为什么看起来是弯的。
senses.why: When a discipline takes the taking-in as its object, its adjective becomes part of its name. Perceptual psychology studies the drawing of the map, not the land it represents.
senses.whyCN: 当一门学科把“拿进来”当作研究对象，它的形容词就进入了学科名称。知觉心理学研究的是地图怎么画，而不是它代表的那片土地。

senses.title: Of visual illusions and constancy
senses.definition: relating to visual effects in which the eye's interpretation differs from the measured reality, or stays constant despite changes
senses.definitionCN: 指眼睛的解释与实测现实不符，或在变化中仍保持恒常的视觉效应
senses.example: The Müller-Lyer figure is a classic perceptual illusion.
senses.exampleCN: 缪勒—莱尔图形是经典的视觉错觉。
senses.why: The eye draws its map quickly and confidently, and sometimes draws it wrong. The adjective marks the gap between the quick drawing and the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛画地图又快又自信，有时会画错。这个形容词标记的就是“快速画出的图”与“尺子”之间的差距。

senses.title: Of hearing speech sounds
senses.titleCN: 与言语声音的听辨有关的
senses.definition: relating to the way listeners segment and identify speech sounds, often before any meaning is assigned
senses.definitionCN: 指听者切分并识别言语声音的方式，通常发生在赋予意义之前
senses.example: Perceptual training helps learners separate two similar vowels.
senses.exampleCN: 知觉训练帮助学习者区分两个相近的元音。
senses.why: The map here is drawn by the ear. Perceptual work is the parsing of a continuous stream into units, long before the mind asks what the units mean.
senses.whyCN: 这里的地图由耳朵来画。知觉工作是先把连续的声音流切分成单位，远在头脑追问这些单位是什么意思之前。

senses.title: Of a disorder in perceiving
senses.definition: relating to a disturbance in the way the senses register or interpret information, as in clinical diagnosis
senses.definitionCN: 与感官登记或解释信息的方式出现紊乱有关，见于临床诊断
senses.example: The patient showed a perceptual deficit after the stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 中风之后，患者表现出知觉缺陷。
senses.why: The instrument can break. When the hand no longer takes in properly, the adjective names the fault in the apparatus rather than in the world.
senses.whyCN: 工具是会坏的。当那只手无法正常拿取时，这个形容词命名的是器械的故障，而不是世界的问题。

senses.title: The first stage of cognition
senses.definition: relating to the early stage of information processing that precedes memory, reasoning, and decision
senses.definitionCN: 指先于记忆、推理与决策的信息加工早期阶段
senses.example: The model separates a perceptual stage from a decision stage.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把知觉阶段与决策阶段分开。
senses.why: Information passes through rooms. The first room is where the senses draft the map; later rooms annotate it. Perceptual names the drafting room.
senses.whyCN: 信息要经过一个个房间。第一个房间是感官起草地图的地方，后面的房间才在上面加注。perceptual 命名的就是起草的那个房间。

senses.title: Of an effect on the senses
senses.definition: relating to the immediate sensory impression made by a design, artwork, or environment, before interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 指设计、艺术品或环境在解释之前造成的直接感官印象
senses.example: The building's perceptual impact comes from its low contrast, not its size.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的知觉冲击来自低对比度，而不是体量。
senses.why: Designers work on the drawing before meaning arrives. A perceptual effect is what the map does to the eye before anyone asks what the map is of.
senses.whyCN: 设计者在意义到来之前先处理这张图。知觉效果就是地图在任何人追问“这是什么”之前，先对眼睛做了什么。

intro.en: Perceptual is percept plus -ual, from Latin -alis 'belonging to'. Percept is Latin perceptum, the neuter past participle of percipere 'to take in', itself per- 'thoroughly' plus capere 'take'. The adjective is a modern psychological term: it appears in English in the 19th century, when experimental psychology separated sensation from perception and needed a word for the process itself.
intro.cn: perceptual 是 percept 加 -ual（拉丁 -alis“属于……的”）。percept 是拉丁 perceptum，即 percipere“拿进来”的中性过去分词，而 percipere 是 per-“彻底”加 capere“拿取”。这个形容词是现代心理学术语：19 世纪实验心理学把感觉与知觉分开、需要一个词指知觉过程本身时，它才在英语中出现。

items.en: Perceptum is the neuter past participle of percipere: literally 'that which has been taken in'. Latin already used perceptio for both the receiving and the understanding.
items.cn: perceptum 是 percipere 的中性过去分词，字面即“已经被拿进来之物”。拉丁语早已用 perceptio 同时表示接收与理解。

items.en: Experimental psychology distinguishes sensation (raw stimulation) from perception (organized interpretation) and adopts perceptual for everything belonging to the second term.
items.cn: 实验心理学把感觉（原始刺激）与知觉（有组织的解释）区分开，并采用 perceptual 指属于后者的全部内容。

items.en: The -ual ending is the English form of Latin -alis, the same suffix that gives manual, visual, and conceptual. It marks belonging, so perceptual means 'of perception', never 'able to perceive'.
items.cn: -ual 词尾是拉丁 -alis 的英语形式，也是 manual、visual、conceptual 使用的同一个后缀。它表示归属，所以 perceptual 意为“知觉的”，绝不是“能感知的”。

items.en: The adjective spreads from psychology to design, music, and human factors research: perceptual load, perceptual salience, perceptual speed.
items.cn: 这个形容词从心理学扩散到设计、音乐与人因研究：知觉负荷、知觉显著性、知觉速度。

items.en: Perceptive means the person is quick to notice; perceptible means the thing can be noticed; perceptual means the process of noticing. The three share the -cept- stem but split by the suffix.
items.cn: perceptive 指人察觉得快；perceptible 指事物可被察觉；perceptual 指察觉这一过程。三者共享 -cept- 词干，靠后缀分工。

items.en: Conceptual looks like perceptual but its stem is concept, from concipere 'take together' (con- + capere). It is the companion term, not the same branch: concept holds, percept takes in.
items.cn: conceptual 看起来像 perceptual，但词干是 concept，出自 concipere“聚在一起拿取”（con- + capere）。它是配套术语，却不是同一分支：概念握着，知觉拿进来。

note.en: The first group separates three adjectives from the same -cept- stem, then adds the conceptual companion and one different-root trap. The second group compares the adjectives for sensory input, thinking, observing, and what appears.
note.cn: 第一组分开同出 -cept- 词干的三个形容词，再补上 conceptual 这个配套词与一个不同词根的陷阱。第二组比较表示“感官输入”“思维”“观察”“显现”的几个形容词。

entries.definition: quick to notice and understand. It describes a person, while perceptual describes the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 察觉与理解敏捷的。它描述人，而 perceptual 描述过程本身。

entries.definition: able to be seen, heard, or noticed at all. It is a possibility, not a property of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被看见、听见或察觉的。它表示的是一种可能性，而非过程的属性。

entries.definition: relating to concepts, the categories made by taking things together. It is the usual partner and opposite of perceptual in psychology.
entries.definitionCN: 与概念有关的，即把事物聚在一起所形成的类别。在心理学里，它常与 perceptual 配对并相对。

entries.definition: a point of view or the art of showing depth. Its root is specere 'to look', not capere 'to take', so it belongs to the eye's position, not to the intake of information.
entries.definitionCN: 观点或表现深度的技法。它的词根是 specere“看”，不是 capere“拿取”，所以属于眼睛的位置，而非信息的接收。

entries.definition: relating to the sense organs and their input. It names the hardware, while perceptual names the organizing work done with that input.
entries.definitionCN: 与感觉器官及其输入有关的。它命名硬件，而 perceptual 命名对这些输入所做的组织工作。

entries.definition: relating to mental processes such as memory, reasoning, and problem-solving. It covers the whole mind, of which the perceptual stage is the entry.
entries.definitionCN: 与记忆、推理、解决问题等心理过程有关的。它覆盖整个心智，而知觉阶段是其中的入口。

entries.definition: based on watching and recording events, often deliberately. It is an activity of a researcher, not a process of the nervous system.
entries.definitionCN: 基于观看并记录事件的，常带有刻意性。它是研究者的活动，而不是神经系统的过程。

entries.definition: relating to experience as it appears to a subject, or simply extraordinary. The philosophical sense is close to perceptual experience, but the everyday sense is 'remarkable'.
entries.definitionCN: 与主体所经验到的显现有关的，或仅指非凡的。其哲学义接近知觉经验，但日常义是“了不起的”。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: -alis 'belonging to', perceptum, the 19th-century psychology split, the three -cept- adjectives, and the con- 'together' contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：-alis“属于”、perceptum、19 世纪心理学的划分、三个 -cept- 形容词，以及 con-“一起”的对比。

normal.en: -ual means 'belonging to': perceptual belongs to perception, just as conceptual belongs to concept and visual to sight.
normal.cn: -ual 意为“属于”：perceptual 属于 perception，就像 conceptual 属于 concept、visual 属于 sight。

normal.en: Perceptum is 'what has been taken in'; perceptual describes the machinery that does the taking.
normal.cn: perceptum 是“已经被拿进来之物”；perceptual 描述执行拿取的那套机制。

normal.en: Perceptive is the person, perceptible is the thing, perceptual is the process: one stem, three suffixes, three jobs.
normal.cn: perceptive 是人，perceptible 是物，perceptual 是过程：一个词干，三个后缀，三种职责。

normal.en: Conceptual has con- 'together' inside: a concept holds things together, while a percept merely brings them in.
normal.cn: conceptual 里面有 con-“一起”：概念把事物握在一起，而知觉只是把它们拿进来。

normal.en: Psychology split sensation from perception in the 19th century, and perceptual became the adjective of the second half.
normal.cn: 19 世纪心理学把感觉与知觉分开，perceptual 成为后半部分的形容词。

abstract.en: A map is not the land, and the drawing style is not the landscape; perceptual is the style of the drawing.
abstract.cn: 地图不是土地，画法也不是风景；perceptual 指的是那种画法。

abstract.en: Two people read the same page: one sees letters, one sees words. The page never moved; the organizing did.
abstract.cn: 两个人读同一页：一个看见字母，一个看见单词。纸页没动，组织方式动了。

abstract.en: An illusion is a map drawn with confidence before the ruler is consulted.
abstract.cn: 错觉就是在还没问尺子之前，就被自信地画出来的地图。

examples.en: Perceptual learning lets the eye recognize the pattern faster.
examples.cn: 知觉学习让眼睛更快认出这个图案。

examples.en: The study compares perceptual and conceptual categories in children.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较儿童的知觉类别与概念类别。

examples.en: Perceptual judgments vary more than the physical measurements do.
examples.cn: 知觉判断的差异比物理测量值的差异更大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破塞普图尔」——眼睛“破”开外面的世界，把东西“塞”进去，画成一张图，这张图的画法就是 perceptual → 知觉的；感知的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 拉丁 perceptum「被拿进来之物」，出自 percipere「拿进来、把握」（per-「彻底」+ capere「拿取」）；后缀 -ual（拉丁 -alis）表归属。核心是「地图的画法本身，而不是地图上的地名」。同族含 perceive、perception、percept、perceptive、perceptible；conceptual 共享 capere 但用 con-「一起」，perspective 的词根则是 specere「看」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of perceptual all describe the drawing of an inner map rather than the land it shows. What changes is which part of the drawing is in view: the process, the sensory side, the contrast with concepts, the psychology, the illusion, the disorder, or the effect on a viewer.
sensesIntro.cn: perceptual 的九个义项都描述内部地图的画法，而不是它所显示的土地。变化的是画法中哪一部分进入视野：过程本身、感官一侧、与概念的对照、心理学、错觉、障碍，还是对观看者的效果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the drawing style of the inner map, not the place names written on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：内部地图的画法本身，而不是写在地图上的地名。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: the receiving and organizing itself, and its place as the first stage of cognition.
branches.cn: 过程：接收与组织本身，以及它作为认知第一阶段的地位。

branches.en: THE SENSORY SIDE: experience through the senses, defined against conceptual thinking.
branches.cn: 感官一侧：通过感官获得的经验，以概念思维为对照来界定。

branches.en: THE STUDY AND ITS SURPRISES: perceptual psychology and the illusions it explains.
branches.cn: 研究及其意外：知觉心理学，以及它所解释的错觉。

branches.en: EARS AND CLINICS: the parsing of speech sounds, and deficits in the perceiving apparatus.
branches.cn: 耳朵与临床：言语声音的切分，以及知觉器械的缺陷。

branches.en: THE DESIGNED EFFECT: what a visual or spatial arrangement does to the eye before interpretation.
branches.cn: 被设计的效果：视觉或空间安排在任何解释之前对眼睛做了什么。

intro.en: Perceptual is percept plus -ual, the English form of Latin -alis. Percept is Latin perceptum, from percipere (per- 'thoroughly' + capere 'take'). The whole family is built by suffix change on one stem: -ion, -ive, -ible, -ual, and the bare -t.
intro.cn: perceptual 是 percept 加 -ual，即拉丁 -alis 的英语形式。percept 是拉丁 perceptum，出自 percipere（per-“彻底”+ capere“拿取”）。整个词族都在同一个词干上换后缀：-ion、-ive、-ible、-ual，以及零后缀的 -t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is capere 'take', percipere 'take in', perceptum 'the thing taken in'. Latin had no perceptual; the adjective is a modern extension of the participle stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 capere“拿取”、percipere“拿进来”、perceptum“被拿进来之物”。拉丁语并没有 perceptual，这个形容词是分词词干在现代的延伸。

items.meaning: belonging to the process of perceiving
items.meaningCN: 属于知觉过程的（-ual 表归属）
items.example: Perceptual errors are common in low light.
items.exampleCN: 光线不足时知觉错误很常见。

items.meaning: the act or result of perceiving
items.meaningCN: 知觉的行为或结果（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: Her perception of the tone was accurate.
items.exampleCN: 她对语气的感知是准确的。

items.meaning: to take in through the senses or mind
items.meaningCN: 通过感官或心智拿进来；察觉
items.example: We perceived a slight shift in the light.
items.exampleCN: 我们察觉到光线有轻微变化。

items.meaning: the content taken in by the senses
items.meaningCN: 感官所拿进来的内容；知觉对象
items.example: The percept is not the object but the object as sensed.
items.exampleCN: 知觉对象不是物本身，而是被感觉到的物。

items.meaningCN: 察觉敏捷的（-ive 倾向形容词）
items.example: She is perceptive about other people's moods.
items.exampleCN: 她对别人的情绪很敏锐。

items.example: The difference was barely perceptible.
items.exampleCN: 这一差别几乎察觉不到。

items.meaningCN: 从知觉角度来说（-ly 副词）
items.example: The two colours are perceptually identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两种颜色在知觉上是相同的。

items.meaning: belonging to concepts formed by taking things together
items.meaningCN: 属于把事物聚在一起所形成的概念的（con- 一起 + capere 拿取）
items.example: Conceptual models guide the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 概念模型指导这项实验。

items.meaningCN: 与感觉器官有关的（sentire 感觉 + -ory）
items.example: Sensory overload makes concentration hard.
items.exampleCN: 感官过载会让注意力难以集中。

latinEntries.meaning: that which has been taken in
